count
The Bulldogs went 1-1 in basketball action last week. Haxtun took the court on the road in Kimball, Neb. Friday night and in a quick turnaround, hosted Prairie at home on Saturday. The Bulldogs suffered a 21-point loss on the road but came back home for the win against the Mustangs for the team's second home victory this season. Haxtun has had just two home games thus far into the 2024-25 season, but will add a third this weekend as the Bulldogs prepare to face Holyoke later this week.
Friday night's action put the Bulldogs on the court in a fast pace match up with a Nebraska team that seemed to sink just about every shot that went up. Despite a solid effort from the visiting team, Kimball took the win 70-49.
Senior Ryland Wolff led his team on offense with 13 points on the road in Nebraska Friday. Junior Chase Goddard added 10 points to the board followed by Colin Cone, who registered nine. Carter Lock contributed five points, Kanin Koberstein put up four, Max Grauberger and Tate Michael scored three apiece and Jaxsen Schram put up two points.
Saturday's match up was just the opposite as the Bulldogs took the court in front of their home crowd. Haxtun took the advantage and never looked back, picking up 50-30 win over the 1A Mustangs.
"It was great to back at home. We hadn't had a home game since early December. The boys were excited to back in front of the home crowd. Right now, it seems like we can get points from anywhere on our roster. If a few of our main scoring options are having a rough night, guys coming off the bench have been stepping up to keep our offense going," Jayden Stieb, Bulldog Head Coach said.
Madden Larsen racked up 15 points against the Mustangs, the team high. He also brought down nine rebounds under the basket. Ryland Wolff had back-to-back, double-digit showings for the weekend, putting 11 points on the board against Prairie. He also tallied nine rebounds. Goddard and Koberstein both added eight points. Goddard registered two rebounds in addition to his eight points. Schram put up four points and brought down one rebound. Corbin Andersen scored two points and Michael had two points and two rebounds.
In a busy week of basketball action, the Bulldogs traveled on Tuesday where they met up with the Otis Bulldogs. Haxtun fell in that match up, 68-39. Following that contest, the Bulldogs hold a 5-5 record.
This weekend Haxtun will travel to Peetz on Friday and Saturday host Holyoke. Peetz is currently 7-2 overall, according to MaxPreps. Holyoke stands at 6-3 on the season.
"I expect both Peetz and Holyoke to be tough games," said Stieb. "Both teams have had good starts to their seasons. We'll need to take care of the ball and step up our defensive effort. Offensively we just need to execute and do the little things right."

title: Fleming TC left with two vacancies following Muller's resignation
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Fleming Town Council held their regular monthly meeting on Wednesday, Jan. 8. The meeting was called to order by Mayor Stefan Betley at 6:30 p.m. The following council members were present: Andrew…
content:
count
The Fleming Town Council held their regular monthly meeting on Wednesday, Jan. 8. The meeting was called to order by Mayor Stefan Betley at 6:30 p.m. The following council members were present: Andrew Muller (left at 7:37 p.m.), Cathy Castillo (left at 6:45 p.m.), Bill Langridge, Suzanne Wales (left at 6:45 p.m.), Alex Gapter (left at 6:48 p.m.) and Bonnie Jackson. Also present were Gary Schmidt (left at 6:40 p.m.), Dale Lousberg (left at 6:49 p.m.), Kamie Lambrecht, Melinda Hickey, Felicity Wales (left at 6:45 p.m.), Joelle and Daniel Gapter (left at 6:48 p.m.), Justin Hickey, Lewis Frank and Michelle Asfeld.
Additions/Corrections to the Agenda: Betley requested adding Council Resignation as Action Item number five and asked for any other additions or corrections to the agenda. Hearing no other additions or corrections, it was moved and seconded to approve the agenda as amended, the motion passed unanimously.
Public Comment: Schmidt addressed the council regarding the Zoning Ordinance for placement of intermodular containers/storage containers.
Lousberg requested an additional month to get compliant with his ordinance infraction. Betley stated that the Council will discuss the ordinance infraction later on in the meeting under Discussion Items and he is welcome to stay and be part of the discussion.
Consent Agenda: A motion was made and seconded to approve the consent agenda consisting of the December minutes and bills. The motion passed unanimously.
Oath of Office: Prior to swearing in the new council members, Betley took a couple moments to acknowledge the commitment and insight of the three outgoing council members; Wales, Castillo and A.Gapter. They were provided with a token of thanks.
The Clerk introduced the two new council members; Kamie Lambrecht and Milinda Hicky and administered the Oath of Office. Following the Oath of Office, Langridge was nominated as Mayor Pro-Tem.
With three outgoing council members and only two new council members seated, Betley formally declared a council vacancy.
Maintenance Report: J. Hickey reported that the maintenance team is working on projects around the shop.
Treasurer's Report: Frank reviewed the financial reports. It was moved and seconded to approve the Treasurer's Report. The motion passed unanimously.
Action Items:
1. The Council discussed the day, time and location for the 2025 council meetings. It was moved and seconded to designate the second Wednesday of the month at 6:30 p.m., at the Fleming Town Hall as the regular council meeting. The motion passed unanimously.
2. The Council discussed posting places for the agenda. It was moved and seconded to designate the Fleming Town Hall, Fleming Post Office and the Town Website (flemingcolorado.us) as the official posting places for the council agenda and publication location for legal notices. Motion passed unanimously.
3. The Council discussed the designation of an official newspaper. It was moved and seconded to designate The Haxtun-Fleming Herald as the official newspaper. Motion passed.
4. Langridge shared with the Council a synopsis of the interviews that were held for the community center custodian position. Three well-qualified candidates were interviewed. After a brief discussion, it was moved and seconded to offer the position to Felicity Wales. The motion passed with Jackson abstaining.
5. Betley read a letter of resignation from Councilman Andrew Muller. With regret, it was moved and seconded to accept the resignation. The motion passed unanimously, leaving the council with two vacancies.
Discussion Items:
1. Betley gave an overview of the Council Committees. It was decided that the Council will wait to make changes to the committees at a future meeting.
2. J. Hickey updated the Council on the Resource Sharing Meeting he attended in December that was hosted by Municipal Energy Agency of Nebraska.
3. The Council is still in the process of attaining cost estimates for a new equipment/shop building.
4. The Council discussed the Lousberg ordinance violation. It was determined to continue moving forward with prosecuting the infraction.
Upcoming Meetings: Town Council meeting on Feb. 12 at 6:30 p.m. at Town Hall.
Adjournment: A motion was made and seconded to adjourn at 8:04 p.m. The motion passed unanimously.

title: SC/F wrestlers earn team title at Elm Creek's Invitational last week
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Sedgwick County/Fleming wrestling team showed resilience and determination at the 2025 Elm Creek Invite, with several standout athletes earning top finishes. While a few competitors faced tough…
content:
The Sedgwick County/Fleming wrestling team showed resilience and determination at the 2025 Elm Creek Invite, with several standout athletes earning top finishes. While a few competitors faced tough losses, many of their teammates made strong runs, contributing valuable points to the team's overall score. With multiple podium finishes across various weight classes, the team is looking to continue building momentum as the season progresses.
In the 106-pound bracket, Carter Imhof, 3-9, had a tough day but showed resilience in his matches. Imhof started the tournament with a loss by fall to Connor Edwards of Hi-Line in 1:44. He then received a bye in the consolation round before bouncing back with a win by fall over Beau Strom, Neligh-Oakdale, in 2:40. Unfortunately, his tournament ended with a second loss by fall to Josh Russell, Alma, in 1:55, and Imhof was unable to place.
Grant Firme, 15-11, had a solid showing in the 126-pound bracket, earning 9.5 team points and securing fourth place. Firme began his tournament with a bye in the first round but was quickly sidelined by a fall in the quarterfinals against Chase Hamilton, Southern Valley, in 1:26. However, Firme battled back through the consolation rounds, earning a tech fall victory over Ryan Hodges, Elm Creek, with a 15-0 score in 1:48. He followed that up with a dominant 12-3 major decision win over Breckon Johnson of Alma. Unfortunately, Firme's tournament ended in the third-place match when he was pinned by Keigan Couch ofn St. Mary's in 3:26, but his comeback after the initial loss showed the heart and persistence that define a strong competitor.
Maddox Herskind, 6-14, had a difficult tournament in the 132-pound division, failing to place and contributing no team points. Herskind lost a close 11-10 decision in the first round to Sully Bantam of Southern Valley before receiving a bye in the consolation round. In the second consolation round, he was defeated by Tristan Woolf, Sutherland, with an 8-4 decision. Although Herskind didn't place, his effort throughout the tournament showed his determination to improve and learn from each experience.
Austin Knox, 18-9, bounced back from a semifinal loss to earn a third place finish in the 138-pound bracket, scoring 22 team points. After quick falls over Trey Allison, North Platte St. Patrick's, and Hayden Lans, Southern Valley, Knox faced Hoefer in the semifinals, where he lost 16-4 by major decision. However, Knox responded with a fall over Sebastian Gandara, Lexington JV, and a quick 35-second pin over Lans in the third place match to earn his spot on the podium.
Scotty Engle, 23-3, had a stellar performance in the 144-pound bracket, capturing the first place title and contributing 26 team points. Engle received a bye in the first round, then won his quarterfinal match by fall over Hayden Walker, Cozad JV. He continued his strong run with a fall over Parker Schutz of Hi-Line in the semifinals. In the first place match, Engle showed his power with a quick 1:47 fall over Cooper Arehart from Neligh-Oakdale to clinch the gold medal.
Grant Statz, 3-1, had an excellent tournament, finishing in second place and scoring 22 team points in the 165-pound division. Statz made a strong run, with wins over Nick Grantski from Centennial, Myles Smith from Fullerton and Bryton Baca from Cozad JV, all by fall. In the first place match, Statz faced off against Francis Pieper from North Platte St. Patrick's, but was pinned in 3:42, securing second place.
Bryden Woodside, 1-5, had a challenging time in the 175-pound division at the Elm Creek Invite, ultimately failing to place. Woodside's tournament began with a difficult loss in the first round to Matt Hittner, Fullerton, who pinned him in 4:24. In the consolation round, Woodside fought hard but was again pinned by Markus Bester from Arcadia/Loup City in 3:36, ending his day early.
Overall, Sedgwick County-Fleming finished with a solid performance earning the team title with 180.5 team points at the Elm Creek Invite, earning numerous podium finishes.
The 2025 Chase County Boys Invitational saw impressive performances from SC/F's athletes, who competed with determination across a range of weight classes. With several podium finishes, the team made their mark, earning numerous medals and points for the tournament. Individual results for varsity wrestlers competing out of Fleming and Haxtun are as follows:
Grant Firme, 18-13, showed resilience in the 126-pound class, securing a sixth-place finish and 13 team points. Firme started strong with a 2:45 fall over Diego Alvarez of Dundy County-Stratton in round one. After a tough quarterfinal loss to Tripton Stec from Minatare, Firme bounced back in the consolation rounds, securing wins by fall over Byron Gonzalez of Wray JV and Jarrett Vanarsdall from Hershey. However, a major decision loss in the consolation semifinals and a medical forfeit in the fifth-place match resulted in Firme finishing in sixth place.
Maddox Herskind, 6-16, competed in the 132-pound class, unfortunately finishing without placing. Herskind lost both of his matches by fall, with the first loss coming in 3:15 against Cooper Barnes from Burlington and the second in 4:40 against Hayden Sittner of Sidney.
Austin Knox, 23-10, impressed at 138 pounds, claiming third place with 21 team points. Knox won his first match by decision, 11-8, over Cameron McGinnis of Kimball, but was pinned by Jason Saucedo from Burlington in the quarterfinals. In the consolation rounds, Knox showed tremendous resilience, winning four straight matches, all by fall, including victories over Amaythian Clark from Ogallala, Cole Block from Hitchcock County, and Connor Einspahr from Chase County. Knox closed out his tournament with a 2:24 pin of McGinnis in the third-place match.
Scotty Engle, 26-4, was dominant on his way to a second-place finish at 144 pounds. Engle pinned his first three opponents, including Noah Griffee of Minatare, Dallas Brunk of Yuma, and James Jeffords of Bridgeport, all in under 1:10. Unfortunately, Engle was edged out by Tristan Campbell from McCook in the final, losing by a 6-4 decision, but still securing a strong second-place finish.
Bryden Woodside, 1-7, had a difficult tournament at 175 pounds, unfortunately not placing. Woodside was pinned in both of his matches, with the first coming in 1:21 against Adam Staman, Bridgeport, and the second in 4:59 against Brayden Kendall from South Platte.
The team will look to build on this momentum as they prepare for the remainder of the season. With strong showings in nearly every weight class, SC/F is positioning itself as a team to watch as the season progresses.
The boys are scheduled to dual Wray on Thursday, Jan. 23 at 5:30 p.m. in Ovid. This will also be Parents' Night. They are then set to travel to Kearney, Neb., where they will participate in the UNK Younes Hospitality Duals on Friday, Jan. 24 with matches beginning at 9 a.m.

title: County officials begin new terms after being sworn into office
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Having won their offices in the Nov. 5, 2024 general election, three elected county officials took their oaths of office on Jan. 14 in the main courtroom of the Phillips County Courthouse. Also,…
content:
(Photo from by JR Krueger) count
PHILLIPS County Court Judge, Kimbra Killin, issues the oath of office to (l-r), District 2 County Commissioner Gerald Roberts, District 3 County Commissioner Tom Timm and County Sheriff Michael Beard.
Having won their offices in the Nov. 5, 2024 general election, three elected county officials took their oaths of office on Jan. 14 in the main courtroom of the Phillips County Courthouse. Also, having been approved for retention in the same election, the Phillips County judge also took the oath of office.
Commissioners Garold Roberts and Tom Timm and Sheriff Michael Beard were sworn in by Phillips County Court Judge, Kimbra Killin. Sedgwick County Court Judge, Myka Landry, joined the courtroom via a video link to witness Killin swearing to the oath.
Commissioner Roberts was first elected to the board of county commissioners in 2020. He is a Phillips County native. He has been employed by the county as a sheriff's deputy and the undersheriff and has also worked for road and maintenance crews. He has been a lineman for Highline Electric Association and a maintenance coordinator for Longmont Power and Communication.
Roberts is the board of county commissioners' representative on the following local or regional boards: Comboard that assists the county's Communications Center, Northeast Colorado Housing, Emergency Medical Services, Eastern Transportation Planning Region, Workers' Compensation Insurance Pool, Colorado Counties Casualty and Property Pool and the Region I Translator Association that supports local access to more TV channels. He is also an alternate representative to the Phillips County Fair Board when Timm is not available.
Commissioner Timm was first elected to the board of county commissioners in 2020. He is the current chairman of the board. He has lived in Phillips County since the early 1970s. He has worked in the farming and ranching industry for close to 30 years. He operates his own trucking company.
Timm is the commissioner representative on the following local or regional boards: Eastern Colorado Services for the Developmentally Disabled, Northeast Colorado Association of Local Government, and Phillips County Fair Board. He is the alternate representative to the Eastern Transportation Planning Region and the Recreation District. He is also the designated proxy for the Legislative Committee of Colorado Counties Inc. for when Commissioner Terry Hofmeister is not available. Additionally, Timm serves on the Seizure Committee with the sheriff and district attorney.
Sheriff Michael Beard has been working in law enforcement in Phillips County for nearly 15 years. He joined the Haxtun Police Department in August of 2010. He became the undersheriff for Phillips County in May of 2020. He graduated from the Military Police Academy in 1979 and later from an Airborne Ranger School at Fort Benning, Georgia. While raising his family, he worked in the mountain states region of a nationwide refrigeration and mechanical company. He also worked in Haxtun for a local drilling and pump company.
Judge Kimbra Killin was appointed to the Phillips County Court in 2014. It is a part-time position. She hears misdemeanor, traffic and county civil cases. Killin received her bachelor's degree magna cum laude from Regis University in 1990 and her Juris Doctor from the University of Denver in 1994. She practiced law in the private sector before being appointed to the county court. She also helps operate a family business.
The board of county commissioners meets three times per month in its meeting room at the courthouse. The 2025 schedule is available at the Phillips County website, http://www.phillipscounty.colorado.gov. Meeting agendas are posted on a bulletin board in the courthouse the day prior to the meeting, as well as at the website.
County court is held once a month at the courthouse, which is typically the first Thursday of the month. Court dockets can be searched for at http://www.coloradojudicial.gov. Start a search by first selecting the 13th judicial district.

title: Miniature memories: Mesa couple builds 1950s hometown in their front yard
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: There's never a dull moment in Craig and Pamela Morris' front yard. Hogs are being slaughtered. Passenger trains whiz by school children on a playground. Police have the local bar surrounded as they…
content:
(Courtesy photo) count
CRAIG AND PAMELA (Hovel) Morris's 1:24 scale replica of Haxtun's main street as she remembers it in the 1950. The replica is in the front yard at the Morris home in Mesa, Ariz.
There's never a dull moment in Craig and Pamela Morris' front yard.
Hogs are being slaughtered. Passenger trains whiz by school children on a playground. Police have the local bar surrounded as they search for a suspect, described by witnesses as being three inches tall.
Craig chuckles and admits he isn't sure what the miniature man is wanted for.
"Was he in a fight or something?" Craig asks. "I don't know, I haven't gotten that far."
Prior to their retirement several years ago, Craig, a firefighter and his wife Pamela, a nurse practitioner, knew nothing about model trains or the engineering that goes into "layouts" or dioramas. What began as a simple hobby to fill their golden years has blossomed into something far more meaningful.
"The neighbors love it and people outside the community who have found it; we have lots of visitors," Pamela said.
Most train enthusiasts confine their passion to plywood boards in a basement. The Morrises took a different approach, turning their front yard into an ever-evolving tiny town.
But it's not just any town.
It's a replica of Haxtun, a farming community of roughly 900 in northeast Colorado. There's a reason it took Pamela 10 years to build it by hand.
It had to be perfect.
"Every building has a story about when I was growing up," Pamela said.
The 1:24 scale main street in her front yard is how Pamela (Hovel) Morris remembers her hometown in the 1950s. Three inches in the world she built translates to six feet in the real life. Cars, people, animals, buildings and, of course, trains are all to scaled appropriately.
"We went back to my hometown, took pictures, came back and built most of the buildings of the main street," Pamela said.
The detailed recreation captures not just the physical structures but the heart of her childhood.
The jewelry store next to the hotel is where Pamela got her ears pierced when she turned 16. Next door is the Haxtun Harvest newspaper where her father worked as editor for 26 years. Pamela remembers everyone in her family proofreading at the kitchen table every Monday and Tuesday night.
"If there were any mistakes, we were in trouble!" Pamela said.
A stone's throw away (quite literally) is the Long Branch bar where her grandpa would have his daily beer at three o'clock on the dot. Pamela was sent to fetch him if her grandma needed something.
"I couldn't go in there but they'd say 'Willie, your granddaughter is here and needs you!'" Pamela recalls.
The "G" scale, or garden scale model train also passes by the movie theater where Pamela got her first job selling tickets, candy and popcorn. The grade school she attended sits next to the community park outlined by a concrete wall. Pamela poured it herself but it's beginning to crack under the Arizona sun - she installed a miniature work crew to repair it.
"If I'm out here Craig will say 'What did you get accomplished today?' and I say not much. I visited with a lot of neighbors because they stop," Pamela said.
Pamela considers herself a maintenance worker, caring for more than 600 feet of track which she cleans with a green scouring pad attached to a wood pole. It's a labor of love.
Craig serves as the railroad's chief engineer, managing the electrical systems that bring their tiny town to life, especially at night. He controls the locomotive's horn, speed and direction from a comfy chair near their front door.
"He does all the engines and stuff and I try to do as much out here as I can without his help. He has taught me how to be an electrician," Pamela said. Craig butts in. "Nothing with AC, all DC."
Craig has his own indoor set of tracks on a sheet of plywood. It's a much smaller scale compared to his wife's railroad but, nonetheless, served as her initial inspiration.
"He invited me to run trains on his track and I said, "No, I'll run my own trains outside.,'" Pamela said.
The Morris' try to run their trains at least once a week but will bring out the engine any time a neighbor's grandchildren, or their own, are in town to visit.
They fear this hobby with die with them.
"We're trying to get younger kids involved because it's engineering," Pamela said. "You have to lay out your track and have a certain radius and run a certain size train on it but they are not just picking it up."
There will come a day when Pamela can no longer get down on her hands and knees to level the track. Model train enthusiasts call it "getting out of the business."
Until then, they still welcome people to stop by their house at 7214 E. Avesta Circle in Mesa, Ariz.
Like many Arizona snowbirds, the miniature town takes a summer break. Its residents would otherwise melt.
It takes a full week to pick up all the buildings, people and cars every May and six weeks to put it back together in the fall.
"I just have to have something to do, so coming out here is kind of my happy place and there is always something to do," Pamela said.

title: Wray outlasts SC/F in intense dual; SC/F takes 9th at UNK MidWest
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The SC/F wrestling team came out just a little short in a hard-fought wrestling dual against Wray, losing 34-39, on Thursday night. The matchup saw numerous thrilling bouts, with both teams showcasing…
content:
(Courtesy photo) count
165-POUND GRANT Statz pinned Brody Richards of Wray at 2:57 during the dual against Wray in Ovid on Thursday, Jan. 23.
The SC/F wrestling team came out just a little short in a hard-fought wrestling dual against Wray, losing 34-39, on Thursday night. The matchup saw numerous thrilling bouts, with both teams showcasing impressive skill and determination on the mat. SC/F was off to a strong start, picking up wins in the lower weight classes, but Wray's middle to upper weights eventually carried them to victory. Individual results for wrestlers competing out of Fleming and Haxtun are as follows:
Grant Firme dominated Kace Chamberlain with a 14-0 major decision, to extend the team's lead to 17-0.
Austin Collins earned a pinfall victory over SC/F's Maddox Herskind at 1:44, closing the scoring gap to 17-6.
At 144 pounds, Scotty Engle fought back for his team, securing a 16-0 tech fall over Andrew Buoy Wray, to bring SCF ahead 22-12.
Ben Riggleman scored a critical pin over SC/F's Zach Statz at 5:10, putting Wray in the lead for the first time at 22-24.
Grant Statz quickly put his team back on track with a pinfall win over Brody Richards Wray at 2:57, bringing SCF within striking distance at 28-24.
Wray's heavyweights proved to be the difference in the final stretch.
Eric Tracy outlasted Ryan Davis with a 12-7 decision, cutting the lead to 34-27, SC/F.
Another pair of closing victories ultimately earned the dual win for Wray.
SC/F faced tough competition at the UNK MidWest Duals, but battled their way to a ninth-place finish thanks to some standout individual performances and a strong team effort. The team went 3-2 in the tournament, highlighted by impressive victories over Millard South JV, Amherst and Norton Community. Individual highlights of the tournament from wrestlers competing out of Fleming and Haxtun are as follows:
Engle, 144 pounds, showed his wrestling strength, scoring multiple falls, including two in under two minutes. His consistency was key in keeping the team competitive in each dual.
Competing at 190 pounds, Davis was another strong performer, earning several falls, including in the wins over Millard South JV and Norton Community. His quick finishes were pivotal for the Cougars in key rounds.
Grant Statz, 165 pounds, made significant contributions, including a fall in 0:52 over Amherst's Gavin Knajdl, continuing to show his ability to capitalize on opponents' mistakes.
Firme, 126 pounds, had a tough tournament, facing challenging competition. Despite the outcome of his matches, Firme's presence and willingness to fight through tough matches were valuable for the team's spirit. Though he didn't secure any victories, his determination to push through each bout was an important aspect of the team's overall effort.
While the team had to face some heavy defeats, losing to Minden, 50-28, and Kearney, 71-12, they showed resilience in the consolation rounds. Their 56-24 win over Amherst and strong finish against Norton Community solidified their position in the tournament rankings.
Match results are as follows: Round 1, Minden 50, SC/F 28; Round 2, Kearney 71, SC/F 12; Round 3, SC/F 50, Millard South JV 28; Consolation Round, SC/F 56, Amherst 24; Ninth-place match, SC/F 48, Norton Community 29.
The team is set to travel to Curtis, Neb., on Friday, Jan. 31 to participate in the Medicine Valley Invitational and then they are set to travel to Stratton for their final regular season tournament on Saturday, Feb. 1 for the Stratton Invitational.

title: SC/F shines capturing two team championships last weekend
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Sedgwick County/Fleming wrestling team delivered an outstanding performance at the Mitchell Invitational, finishing in first place with a total of 236 points. The team's deep roster, featuring 18…
content:
Regional Wrestling - Friday and Saturday
The Sedgwick County/Fleming wrestling team delivered an outstanding performance at the Mitchell Invitational, finishing in first place with a total of 236 points. The team's deep roster, featuring 18 athletes across various weight classes, showcased talent and resilience, placing numerous wrestlers on the podium.
Grant Firme earned fourth place at 126 pounds for five team points. He worked his way into the fourth place match but fell short, despite securing a key win by decision over Micah Woodbeck of Hemingford in the consolation semifinals.
Maddox Herskind competed at 132 points. He had a tough run but picked up a win over Jonah Conley of Bridgeport. He dropped his next match by tech fall to Taylor Eichthaler of Bridgeport and ultimately finished out of the top six.
Austin Knox earned fourth place for 10 team points in the 138-pound bracket. He earned a spot in the fourth place match after a win by fall in the quarterfinals. However, he was pinned by teammate Mario Ortiz in the semifinals and then fell short to Cameron McGinnis of Kimball in the third place match.
144-pound Scotty Engle took first place and earned 29 team points. He proved his dominance, pinning Josiah Frueh of Scottsbluff JV in the opening round and Anthony Ging of Bridgeport in the quarterfinals. He finished his title run with a tech fall, 15-0 in the finals against Alyck Rodriguez of Scottsbluff JV.
Grant Statz earned first place in the 165-pound class for 24 team points. He secured the title with three falls, including one over Matthew Corne of Sidney in the quarterfinals and another in the final in 1:01 over Quinten Tretter of Bridgeport.
Bryden Woodside competed at 175 pounds. He had a rough outing, with a fall loss to Zech Roggasch of Sidney in the quarterfinals and a subsequent decision loss to James Brandner of Yuma in the consolation rounds.
190-pound Ryan Davis placed second for 18 team points. He made it to the first place match after an injury default win and a fall, but lost in the finals to Patrick McCartney of Sidney by tech fall, 22-5.
The team proved their dominance once again, securing their second tournament victory of the weekend at the Stratton Invitational. With an impressive total of 220 points, the team outpaced several formidable opponents to claim the top spot. The tournament saw standout performances across the board, with multiple wrestlers earning high placements.
106-pound Carter Imhof received a bye in the first round but struggled in his matchups, ultimately dropping a narrow decision, 9-8, to Landen Spicknall from Wray in the quarterfinals and a loss by decision to Gunner Fye of Stratton in the consolation rounds.
Firme took fourth place at 126 pounds for 11 team points. He reached the semifinals but was pinned by Ronin VanWynen of The Classical Academy. After bouncing back with a major decision victory in the consolation semis, Firme eventually fell in the third place match by fall to Jaden DePue of Wray, securing his fourth place finish.
Maddox Herskind struggled in the 132-pound bracket, losing by fall to Skyler Cooper of The Classical Academy in the quarterfinals. He later lost by major decision to Hayden Pfost from Simla, ending his tournament run early.
Knox took second place in the 132-pound division for 17.5 team points. He fought hard to make it to the finals, earning a tech fall victory in the semifinals over Skyler Cooper of The Classical Academy, but was pinned by Alexander Hamel of Hill City HS in the finals.
Engle added 23 team points with a first-place finish in the 144-pound class. His powerful tournament run included four straight pins. His championship victory came with a pin over Luke Sorensen of The Classical Academy in 1:49, adding another title to his impressive season.
Statz took first place in the 165-pound division for 24 team points. He continued his dominant form with a series of pins, including a win over Archer Amrein of Hill City HS in the championship.
Woodside struggled in the 175-pound class, losing by fall to Coleson Waitman of Wray and Ethen Garay of County Line in his later match, ultimately ending up without a placing finish.
Davis finished in second place at 190 pounds for 17 team points. He earned second place in a competitive weight class, advancing to the finals with a fall and a major decision. He fell short to Chason Turner of County Line, who defeated him 15-2 in the championship.
SC/F's impressive 220-point total at the Stratton Invitational further cements their status as one of the region's top wrestling teams. With multiple champions and consistent top finishes, the team showed their strength across multiple weight classes.
SC/F boys are set to travel to Akron on Feb. 7 and 8 for their regional tournament where they will compete for a trip to the Colorado State Wrestling Tournament in Denver on Feb. 13-15.

title: SC/Fleming girls earn 2nd Mitchell Invitational

content:
Regional Wrestling - Friday & Saturday, Feb. 7 & 8
The Sedgwick County/Fleming girls' wrestling team brought their A-game to the Mitchell Invitational, finishing in second place overall with 112 team points. The SC/F ladies showed their depth and skill with multiple strong finishes across many weight classes.
Annie Wilson claimed first place in the in the 130-pound weight class contributing 20 team points. Her path to victory was dominant, as she won all of her matches by fall. Her consistent performance in the tournament made her a key factor in the team's success.
Kinsleigh Jerman fought hard to earn a fourth place finish in the 120-pound division. Jerman collected 11 team points, including a win by fall in the consolation semifinals. Despite her efforts, she came up short in the third place match, but her performance was key to the team's overall success.
Kaiya Hall placed third in the 135-pound weight class, contributing nine team points. After two early losses in the tournament, she bounced back with a win by fall over Kynnady Hajeh of Leyton in the consolation round, securing the third place finish for the team.
Olivia Stone placed fourth in the 155-pound class earning 11 team points. After receiving a bye in the first round, she won her quarterfinal match by decision, 10-4. Unfortunately, she was pinned in the semifinals and again in the third place match, but her overall effort was crucial for the team's strong finish.
Bella Allen competed in the 105-pound weight class. After a loss in the quarterfinals to Cecilia Barron-Berrelleza of Morrill, Allen was eliminated in the first round of the consolation bracket.
Autumn Volkman competed in the 115-pound weight class. She lost her first two matches, one by fall and the other by major decision, before being defeated in her final match as well.
The SC/F girls will be looking to build on this success as they head into the final stretch of the season, with hopes of punching multiple tickets to the Colorado State Wrestling Tournament Feb. 13-15. The girls' regional tournament is set to be held in Yuma on Friday, Feb. 7 and Saturday, Feb. 8.

title: Lady Wildcats set to battle Briggsdale
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: We apologize for the inconvenience, but we must restart your session so you can continue browsing our website.
content:
Fleming's Lady Wildcats are scheduled to meet the Briggsdale Lady Falcons this week in a battle for best in the league. With the regular season drawing to a close, the two teams hold identical 3-0 league records with Briggsdale sitting in the number one spot, according to MaxPreps. Rankings released by Colorado High School Activities Association put the league's top two contenders in the fifth and sixth spots in the State, respectively.
Last week's action added two games in the win column for the local ladies. They took commanding wins over Weldon Valley on Friday, 70-42, and Denver Waldorf on Saturday, 54-22.
Juniors Ciana Lousberg and Brooke Schaefer and sophomore Hayley Chamberlain led for the weekend in scoring. On Friday night, all three players hit double digits with Lousberg earning the team's high at 21 points. She went one-for-one from behind the three point arc, two-for-four from the charity stripe and added the remaining 16 on two-point shots.
Schaefer tallied 19 on that outing making three-of-four at the free-throw line and 16 points on two-point field goals.
Chamberlain added another 10 after sinking six at the free-throw line and a pair of two-point shots.
On Saturday night, the same trio led in scoring. This time, Schaefer tacked on the team high with 12 off two free throws and five two-point shots. Lousberg added 10 all by means of two-point field goals. And Chamberlain scored nine; shooting 100 percent from the free-throw line for two points, sinking a three-pointer and two two-point buckets.
On Friday against Weldon Valley, junior Ashley Bornhoft led the group in rebounds with 10. She brought down four offensive and six defensive boards. Chamberlain and junior Siena Donnelson led under the basket on Saturday with nine and eight rebounds, respectively.
Other notable stats from last week's games included eight steals by Schaefer against Denver Waldorf. Lousberg added another six steals in that contest.
Just three games remain on the regular season schedule for the Lady Wildcats. This week's contest against Briggsdale marks the final league contest of the season. That game is set to take place at Briggsdale on Friday night. Girls' varsity is set to tip off at 5 p.m. that day.
On Saturday, Feb. 15, the Lady Wildcats are scheduled to travel to Lone Star to face off with the 8-7 Lady Longhorns. A junior varsity boys' contest will begin the day's play at 2 p.m. with girls' and boys' varsity to follow.

title: Van Natta family opens appliance store in Haxtun
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Haxtun's newest business, Natta's Scratch 'n Dent Appliances, brings convenience and affordability while meeting the needs of the northeast Colorado community. Located at the corners of highways 6 and…
content:
(Herald photo by Candie Fix) count
TARAH, Casey and Elise Van Natta (l-r), are pictured in the show room of their new business, Natta's Scratch 'n Dent Appliances in Haxtun. Tarah and her husband Joe, and his brother Casey and wife Elise (Atkins), are all partners in the new business endeavor, which brings affordable appliance sales to northeast Colorado.
Haxtun's newest business, Natta's Scratch 'n Dent Appliances, brings convenience and affordability while meeting the needs of the northeast Colorado community. Located at the corners of highways 6 and 59 in Haxtun, Natta's Scratch 'n Dent Appliances features all styles of household appliances that were refused by the original owner or slightly cosmetically damaged in shipping.
Casey and his wife Elise Van Natta and brother Joe and his wife Tarah all teamed up to embark on this new business venture after they themselves saw a need for such a store.
Elise (Atkins) Van Natta grew up in Haxtun and recently returned to the area with her husband and his family. Elise, Casey and Tarah all work in healthcare at Melissa Memorial Hospital in Holyoke but in their off time now manage a small appliance store in Haxtun. Tarah's husband, Joe Van Natta, works in the oilfield in Alaska, two weeks on and two weeks off. On his off time, Joe too resides in Haxtun and assists in the business.
When Casey and Elise were first married and purchased their first home, the two were forced to look for a new appliance just weeks after their closing on their property. Just putting all their funds into the purchase of their new home, the two were limited on funds when looking for something new. In Iowa, where the couple lived at the time, they found a similar scratch and dent appliance business that allowed them to affordably purchase new appliances for the new-to-them home.
After relocating to Haxtun, the idea of establishing such a business here became a dream turned to reality.
Right now, Natta's Scratch 'n Dent Appliances is open by appointment at 142 North First Street in Haxtun. As Casey, Elise and Tarah have time off, and when Joe is home, the four run the appliance business along the south side of Highway 6.
Casey said convenience is the best asset his new business brings to northeast Colorado with a number of appliances in stock and ready to take home same day. Natta's Scratch 'n Dent Appliances currently features a display floor of refrigerators, dishwashers, electric ovens, microwaves, stackable washer and dryer sets and several stand-alone washers and dryers.
The trio explained that appliances in their store may be slightly damaged cosmetically, however, a number of pieces are in perfect shape because they were simply returned to the manufacturer as "refused" upon delivery. Any blemishes or damages are strictly cosmetic and do not affect the function in any way.
Having the appliances on site means shoppers can walk in, pick what they are looking for and take it home; a convenience brand name stores don't or can't seem to offer right now. Many big, corporate-named appliance stores can have a wait time of up to six months.
"You can take it home today," Casey Van Natta said.
Another market that may be looking for exactly what Natta's Scratch 'n Dent Appliances has to offer are rental property owners and house flippers. Many of the pieces have small dents or scratches that, if installed with those in mind, can be hidden from sight.
"This isn't our main source of income, but we wanted to do something to benefit the community. To provide something for the community," Tarah Van Natta said.
Store stock is not brand specific and varies in colors and design, but at the time of opening, features a good amount of stainless steel and Samsung appliances.
Natta's Scratch 'n Dent Appliances is just two weeks into business and so far, business has been great.
"We are overwhelmed, but in a very good way," said Tarah Van Natta. We are just overwhelmed with how well the response has been, just in the first week. We're testing the waters and it's been great. It's also giving us direction on where we need to go."
The Van Natta group said that with the arrival of the first shipment and customers visiting the store, they are open to feedback and are already taking requests for items like stand-up freezers and gas ovens.
"We are trying to keep note of what people want for future orders. We are testing it all out right now," said Casey Van Natta.
To reach any of the Van Nattas for an appointment, customers can call or text (970) 236-8558 or reach out on Facebook at Natta's Scratch 'n Dent Appliances. The business Facebook page features announcements of new shipments and any upcoming open hours. Last week, it worked for the store to be open for a few hours on a Friday afternoon. A website is also in the works and will be up soon: nattasappliances.com.
"Please just give us grace, we will respond to messages as soon as we can," Tarah Van Natta said. "We all work in healthcare so often times we can meet in evenings and on weekdays, depending on schedules."

title: SC/F girls' and boys' teams take 2nd at respective regional tournaments
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Sedgwick County/Fleming girls wrestling team secured an impressive second place finish at the Colorado High School Activities Association 4A Girls' Region 4 Wrestling Tournament, and six of their talented athletes are now headed to the State Tournament next week. Wrestlers competing in the Regional Tournament out of Fleming and Haxtun are as follows: Annie Wilson earned an impressive...
content:
The Sedgwick County/Fleming girls wrestling team secured an impressive second place finish at the Colorado High School Activities Association 4A Girls' Region 4 Wrestling Tournament, and six of their talented athletes are now headed to the State Tournament next week. Wrestlers competing in the Regional Tournament out of Fleming and Haxtun are as follows:
Annie Wilson earned an impressive third place finish, scoring 18 team points in the 130-pound bracket. She dominated her first-round match with a fall over Maykayla Ward of Berthoud, but was pinned in the semifinals by Alyssa Solis-Ornelas from Fort Lupton. Wilson bounced back with a win by fall over Dahneen Muhammad of Sierra in the consolation semifinals and sealed her third place spot with a win by fall over Amarae Venegas of Fort Morgan. She enters State at 31-9 on the year.
Olivia Stone made a strong showing at Regionals, finishing in third place and scoring 17 team points in the 155-pound division. After receiving a bye in the first round, Stone rebounded from a quarterfinal loss to Kiersten Brush from Sterling with three consecutive fall victories in the consolation rounds. She secured her third place finish with a dominant 13-2 major decision over Addison Mayer of Wiggins School District. Stone heads to the State Tournament at 16-17 on the season.
Autumn Volkman delivered a gritty performance at Regionals, finishing fourth in the 110-pound weight class and earning nine team points. Although she placed in the top four, Volkman ultimately lost her challenge match, preventing her from advancing to the State Tournament. She showed remarkable resilience throughout the competition, especially after a tough opening round loss and finished the year at 6-20.
Kinsleigh Jerman showed resilience in the 120-pound class, finishing sixth and scoring seven team points. Despite a tough loss in the semifinals, Jerman pushed through the consolation bracket before being pinned in the fifth place match. She finished the year at 15-12 overall.
Bella Allen had a tough tournament, but her efforts helped the team's overall score. She unfortunately did not place, with losses in both the first and second rounds of the 105-pound division. She finished her year at 2-17.
Kaiya Hall was also unable to place but earned two team points after a hard-fought competition in the 135-pound bracket. Her season closed at 10-17 overall.
The SC/F boys' wrestling team showcased an impressive performance at the CHSAA 2A Region 1 Tournament, securing second place in the team standings. The team qualified 10 athletes total for the upcoming State Tournament, four of those competing out of Haxtun. Regional results for wrestlers competing out of Haxtun are as follows:
Scotty Engle continued his dominance, securing a first-place finish with a perfect 3-0 record in the 144-pound class. Engle, who has a 40-5 season record, recorded two tech falls and a fall, including a 2:14 victory over Caden Geanetta of Forge Christian in the Championship match. His victory earned him 27 team points.
Grant Statz had a flawless tournament as well, finishing in first place with 29 team points in the 165-pound bracket. Statz advanced to the finals by pinning all three of his opponents in the early rounds, and claimed the 165 lb. championship with 16-8 major decision win over Joseph Noce of Dayspring Christian Academy in the finals. He enters State at 17-3 this season.
Austin Knox battled his way to a fourth-place finish in the 132-pound division, recording a 3-2 tournament record and scoring 13.5 team points. He fought back after a semifinal loss, earning his fourth-place finish and enters State at 29-16 so far this year.
Ryan Davis placed fourth in the 190-pound weight class and scored 16 team points. After a tough loss in the quarterfinals, he fought his way through the consolation bracket, earning three straight falls. Davis came up short in the third place match but will represent the team at 190 pounds at the state tournament.
Grant Firme had a tough run in the Regional Tournament, going 0-2 and not scoring any team points. He faced off against Aidan Sherman of Merino in his opening match, where he lost by tech fall, 16-1, in 5:06. Firme then received a bye in the consolation bracket before facing Canyon Andrist from Lyons, who won by fall in 3:36, ending Firme's tournament run. His season closed with an overall record of 23-23.
The State Wrestling Tournament is slated for Thursday-Saturday, Feb. 13-15 at Ball Arena in Denver.

author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Last week's battle for the best in the league between the Fleming Lady Wildcats and the Briggsdale Lady Falcons ended in a Valentine's Day victory for the local squad. At the conclusion of league…
content:
(Herald photo by Spring Atchison) count
LADY WILDCAT sophomore Emma Feather looks for an outlet in the final home contest against Denver Waldorf earlier this month.
Last week's battle for the best in the league between the Fleming Lady Wildcats and the Briggsdale Lady Falcons ended in a Valentine's Day victory for the local squad. At the conclusion of league play, the Lady Wildcats boast a perfect 4-0 record.
Fleming and Briggsdale looked evenly matched in the first half with the Lady Wildcats up by just four after the opening two quarters. Briggsdale's offense couldn't keep pace in the second half and Fleming's defense shut them down to just seven points in the third and fourth quarters combined. Fleming added 22 in the second half and the game closed at 41-22.
Junior Brooke Schaefer, the team's leading scorer, topped her 13 point per game average with 15 against Briggsdale. She also led the team in assists with five.
Junior Ciana Lousberg followed on the scoreboard with eight points. Lousberg, along with sophomores Hayley Chamberlain and Hadley Stull, led the team in steals with three apiece.
Junior Ashley Bornhoft led under the net in rebounds with seven. She also led in blocked shots with three. Junior Quincy Stull brought down five rebounds.
The Lady Wildcats traveled to Lone Star on Saturday night where they took a 20-point victory over the Lady Longhorns, 57-37.
Four Lady Wildcats hit double digits on the scoreboard. That group was led by Schaefer with 15 points for the second consecutive night. Hadley Stull added 12 points in the contest. Lousberg and Chamberlain added 11 points apiece.
Bornhoft brought down the team-high eight rebounds. Hadley Stull and Chamberlain added five boards each.
In addition to her 11 points, Lousberg led the team in assists and steals with five in each category.
The Lady Wildcats are scheduled to play Idalia on Friday, Feb. 21. The Lady Wolves hold the top spot in the YWKC League with a 5-0 record. Junior varsity boys are set to open the evening's play at 4 p.m. with girls' and boys' varsity games to follow.
Beginning next Monday, Feb. 24, the North Central League is set to enter tournament play with the YWKC League which includes Idalia, Hi Plains, Otis, Arickaree, Lone Star and Bethune. Brackets for the tournament had not been released as of press time.

title: PFC announces record $7.25 million dividend for member-owners
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Premier Farm Credit, a trusted cooperative lender committed to supporting the agricultural community, recently announced that it will pay a record $7.25 million in patronage dividends to its member…
content:
Premier Farm Credit, a trusted cooperative lender committed to supporting the agricultural community, recently announced that it will pay a record $7.25 million in patronage dividends to its member-owners in 2025. This dividend will be distributed to eligible members across six counties in northeast Colorado. This marks over 25 years of continuous patronage dividend payments, demonstrating the cooperative's unwavering dedication to its members.
"At Premier Farm Credit, we pride ourselves on our strong commitment to our member-owners and their operations," said Chris Hornung, Chief Executive Officer of Premier Farm Credit. "The patronage dividend is a testament to the financial strength and stability of our cooperative. We look forward to once again sharing our success with those who make it all possible."
With input costs on the rise for producers, Premier Farm Credit recognizes the need for extra capital to support its members. The patronage dividend distribution will help alleviate some of the financial pressures faced by its member-owners, allowing them to invest in their operations and continue thriving in a challenging economic environment.
"The consistent payment of patronage dividends for 28 consecutive years and over $94 million returned underscores the association's dedication to its member-owners. Our success is their success and we are proud to continue providing financial benefits that support their agricultural businesses and communities throughout northeast Colorado where our members live and work,' Rebecca Lenz, Premier Farm Credit Board Chair said.
About Premier Farm Credit: As part of the Farm Credit System (established in 1916), Premier Farm Credit is a mission-driven lending cooperative owned entirely by its borrowers/member-owners. Sometimes referred to as an Association, Premier Farm Credit serves Northeast Colorado and the surrounding areas with loans, leases, insurance and appraisals for agriculture and ag-related businesses. Premier Farm Credit has an aggregate loan volume of over $1 billion and welcomes farmers and ranchers to stop by their offices in Sterling, Fort Morgan, Yuma and Holyoke. Learn more about them at premieraca.com, or on Facebook, X, LinkedIn or Instagram.

title: Haxtun honors Cathy Starkebaum; Lady Bulldogs set to face Limon in Akron
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Lady Bulldogs closed out play at home with a final match against Sedgwick County on their home court. To mark the occasion, players and coaches honored parents, supporters and long-time champion…
content:
(Courtesy photo by Zoe Kurtzer) count
CATHY STARKEBAUM, far left, was showered with flowers and gifts from the Bulldog community as she plans to retire from the scorers' table after 20+ years. Haxtun Athletic Director Collyn Heinz, middle, and Principal Becky Heinz honored Starkebaum before the Lady Bulldogs' final home game this season. In addition to keeping book and managing the clock, Starkebaum has always been ready to tape ankles, provide care to injured athletes and ensure all Bulldogs and visiting athletes are ready to compete at their best.
The Lady Bulldogs closed out play at home with a final match against Sedgwick County on their home court. To mark the occasion, players and coaches honored parents, supporters and long-time champion Cathy Starkebaum before tipoff.
For the past two decades, Starkebaum has played a pivotal role at the scorers' table for the Bulldogs, both in volleyball and boys' and girls' basketball. She's manned the clock and kept book but her contributions to the Bulldogs go far beyond the score table as she is always readily available to tape ankles, provide care to injured athletes and ensure all Bulldogs and visiting athletes are ready to compete.
"Her selfless service, reliability and passion for the game have made an incredible impact on our teams, coaches and community," said Haxtun Athletic Director Collyn Heinz as Starkebaum was honored Friday night. "We are beyond grateful for her dedication and we truly appreciate everything she has done for the Bulldogs!"
After honoring parents, Starkebaum and seniors, the Lady Bulldogs took the court against the Lady Cougars. Sedgwick County currently holds the second-place slot in all of Colorado 2A rankings, including Colorado High School Activities Association RPI standings.
Haxtun put seven points on the board in the first quarter and another eight in the second but the Lady Cougars dominated for the half-time lead. They continued with that pressure throughout the second half to nab a 60-28 point win over the Lady Bulldogs.
Senior Jayleigh Bullard put eight points on the board for the Lady Bulldogs. Senior Emily Anderson contributed six, senior Kelsie Hadeen added five and junior Katiegh Cody put up four.
Bobbi Starkebaum, Lady Bulldog senior, pulled down eight rebounds, the team high. Bullard brought down seven, junior Lilly Lemesany and freshman Leah Edwards grabbed three and Emma Lemesany and Hadeen each tallied two.
Hadeen registered four assists. Bullard, Hadeen and Emma Lemesany all tallied a single steal.
On Tuesday, the Lady Bulldogs opened play in an end-of-the-season tournament slated for this week. Haxtun fell on the road to Burlington. The loss pits them in a contest with Limon scheduled for Friday morning in Akron. When tournament play wraps up this weekend, CHSAA is expected to release Regional standings. Regionals are set for the second weekend in March.

title: PC voters favor Biden, Trump in primary election
author: JR Krueger
description: Information made available from the Colorado Secretary of State's office, as of March 15, indicates a Phillips County voter turnout of 52.92 percent of active voters for the March 5 presidential…
content: Information made available from the Colorado Secretary of State's office, as of March 15, indicates a Phillips County voter turnout of 52.92 percent of active voters for the March 5 presidential primary election. This exceeds the statewide voter turnout of 38.67 percent. An 'active voter' is defined as a registered voter who has a record of voting in the past three years per the county clerk's rolls. County-level election-related statistics are considered 'unofficial' until the process is closed out by a county canvas board. Phillips County vote counts of the Democrat's ballot tallied 161. President Joseph R. Biden received the most votes at 115, or 71.43 percent. The next highest was the 'Noncommitted delegate' category with 18, or 11.18 percent, followed by Dean Phillips with 15, or 9.32 percent. Another 13 votes were spread across five of the other six candidates. County vote counts of the Republican's ballot tallied 1,284. Former president Donald J. Trump received the most votes at 1,037, or 80.78 percent. The next highest was Nikki Haley with 204, or 15.89 percent, followed by Ron DeSantis with 26, or 2.02 percent. Another 17 votes were spread across the four other candidates. A law that Colorado enacted in 2016 allows unaffiliated voters to vote in primary elections. They receive both the Democrat and the Republican ballots but must choose which one they will use to cast their vote. They can return only the one ballot voted. If they return both ballots the votes are not counted. This was the first year that Colorado's presidential primary was held in March along with 15 other states and America Samoa. It's dubbed 'Super Tuesday' because it's the day that the most states hold the presidential primary on the same day. Super Tuesday primary elections resulted in Biden and Trump becoming their parties' presumptive nominee for president because of the number of electoral votes secured across the participating states. Final Phillips County vote counts for every presidential candidate will be available when the results become official. Per state election laws, the canvas board shall complete their duties no later than the 22nd day after any election coordinated by the county clerk and recorder.

title: Relentless Gardener
author: Linda Langelo
description: Birds have different niches in which each family of birds needs shelter and food. The key to developing great habitats for birds is to have a diversity of specific plants for the types of birds that…
content:
Attracting birds to your landscape
Birds have different niches in which each family of birds needs shelter and food. The key to developing great habitats for birds is to have a diversity of specific plants for the types of birds that visit your yard. It doesn't require scrapping what you already have in your landscape. It just means adding a tree or shrub(s) or herbaceous perennials. Besides adding plants to your landscape, the more bugs, the more birds as author Sally Roth states in her book Bird-By-Bird Gardening. This means pesticides that kill bugs, kill birds. The American Robin eats caterpillars and feeds off insects that nest in the furrow of the tree bark. Who eats aphids? Tiny chickadees do while cicadas are a meal for big-beaked cardinals. Swallows eat gnats and airborne insects but won't eat grasshoppers or cicadas. Here are some other birds that feed on insects: Woodpecker, Flycatcher, Swallow, Waxwing, Vireo, Nuthatch, Wren, Warbler, Tanager and Thrush. If you add annuals to your landscape such as zinnias, bachelor buttons and impatiens they will provide seed for sparrows, meadowlarks, grosbeaks and more. Trees such as Abies spp, Pinus spp and other conifers provide seed for birds. Trees such as hawthorn, oak, Rocky Mountain juniper, Austrian and pinyon pines, spruces, firs, hackberries, plums and flowering crabapples provide both food and shelter for the birds. Shrubs that provide food and cover include honeysuckles, snowberries, red and yellow twig dogwoods, sumacs, serviceberries, chokecherries and a wide variety of shrubby plums according to Planttalk.colostate.edu. To appeal to a larger number of birds from different families, plants such as blackberries, raspberries, elderberries, cherries, prickly pear cholla cactus, bayberry and mulberry appeal across many bird families. Of course, there are plants such as the prickly pear and cholla cactus that are not appealing to certain landscapes. Prickly pears can overrun a field and become challenging to control. For those who are interested in using more native plants in your landscape, here is a link for the Denver Audubon Society: https://www.denveraudubon.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Native-Plants-for-Birds-Final.pdf. This link gives the plant care information and the birds that are attracted to the plant. For example, Black-eyed Susan provides seeds for the birds and brings in pollinators. It lists Waxwings, orioles, nuthatches, warblers, wrens, thrushes, jays and chickadees that feed on the seed. This is a broad topic with a great deal to cover and learn. Starting with a few plants and adding more over time can create appeal for birds, butterflies, and many other pollinators.

content:
(Courtesy photo)
HAXTUN FBLA members are pictured at the Colorado State Conference at the Gaylord Rockies Resort.
The Haxtun FBLA Chapter had a great showing at the Colorado FBLA State Conference. This year, 60 students competed at the conference. This included students in presentations, objective tests, production events and the Business Achievement Awards. Throughout the conference, students were able to explore the Gaylord Rockies Resort and attend various activities related to the conference.

Here, the chapter was recognized for their donation to the March of Dimes and the students that completed their Business Achievement Awards. Tuesday was a busy day for Haxtun. Ten teams competed in the final round of presentations, while many other chapter members took their objective tests. A highlight for many of the students were the workshops offered throughout the day. Some of the most talked about workshops were related to internships, the Make-A-Wish foundation, and entrepreneurship. The kids were able to finish the day with chapter bonding at Top Golf.
The anticipation was high on Wednesday as students waited for the results of finals and their tests. We had several teams and individuals make the stage. In the end, we had 16 students qualify to attend the National Leadership Conference that will be held in Orlando this summer.
The following groups will move on: American Enterprise Project, Cassidy Goddard, Brock Miller and Grant Statz; Community Service Project, Brandon Nall, Alyssa Molde and Corbin Andersen; Local Chapter Annual Business Report, Mason Bornhoft, Seth Seger and Carter Lock; Partnership with Business, Megan Walker, Kaiden Schelling and Lilly Lemesany; Website Design, Kelsie Schelling and Emily Anderson; Graphic Design, Torrie Wernsman; Electronic Career Portfolio, Samantha Seger.

title: Haxtun Health hires Dr. Dana Morgan to start seeing patients this summer
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The medical team at Haxtun Health is fully staffed. That news came from Chief Executive Officer Dewane Pace in a late-April meeting of the Haxtun Health Board of Directors. Pace said that Dr. Dana Morgan has accepted a full-time position with Haxtun Health. Dr. Morgan grew up in Montana and graduated from the University of Washington School of Medicine. She finished her residency in Family...
content:
The medical team at Haxtun Health is fully staffed. That news came from Chief Executive Officer Dewane Pace in a late-April meeting of the Haxtun Health Board of Directors.
Pace said that Dr. Dana Morgan has accepted a full-time position with Haxtun Health. Dr. Morgan grew up in Montana and graduated from the University of Washington School of Medicine. She finished her residency in Family Medicine at Poudre Valley Hospital in 1996. Dr. Morgan's areas of interest include family medicine for all ages, age management medicine, bio-identical hormone replacement and cosmetic medicine. She is a certified BioTE provider and is enthusiastic about helping middle aged men and women live healthier lives through hormone optimization.
Dr. Morgan has five grown children and four grandchildren. In her free time, she enjoys spending time with her kids, quilting, crocheting and traveling. Dr. Morgan worked in Yuma for several years before moving to Eaton and missed living and working in a small town.
The new Doctor at Haxtun Health should start seeing patients in early summer. With her addition, the Medical Staff team at Haxtun health is now fully staffed.
In his report to the Board, Pace also announced the addition of a new vehicle to Haxtun Health. Pace said Haxtun Health delivers almost 2,000 prescriptions a year and puts nearly 15,000 miles on the delivery vehicle. The current delivery vehicle had become unreliable which put Haxtun Health at risk of losing the delivery service to the community.
However, with funds from the Haxtun Hospital Foundation, Haxtun Lions Club and several other private donors, enough money was raised to purchase a new vehicle, which will give Haxtun Health the ability to transport patients to and from medical appointments such as the dentist and eye doctor and offer pharmacy delivery to the Haxtun community.
The new vehicle is a 2024 Chevy Equinox and came at no cost to Haxtun Health.
At the end of the meeting, during action items, board members with Haxtun Health voted to extend a line of credit with Pioneer Bank for another 12 months. According to Pace, last year the Board asked Pioneer Bank for a line of credit to bridge any gaps that might occur while waiting for funds from grants to keep construction progress on the Main Street Project moving forward.
'We have not had to use any of those funds but the line of credit expires this month and this was just to extend it for another 12 months. We have been very fortunate that the grants have come in timely but just want to make sure there are no gaps in the timeline and can keep going forward,' Pace added. 'The line of credit is for $1.8 million against our CDS (Congressionally Directed Spending) Grant of $2 million.'
In other business:
• Haxtun Health has one nursing staff position open, one for a certified nurse's aide;
•Dr. Stephenson competed Advanced Cardiac Life Support and Pediatric Advanced Life Support recertification and both Dr. Seinfeld and Dr. Stephenson competed certification to be able to assist with Medical Barium Swallow Studies with Speech Therapy;
• Ellen McConnell assumed the role of Pharmacist in Charge effective April 1;
• Charles Choe will be joining the pharmacy team upon graduation from the Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences. Choe was one of several students who rotated at Haxtun Health from Colorado State University during the School year;
• Tsveta Petkova started as Lab Director. The Director begins with a fully staffed lab.

title: Haxtun Town Council establishes truck route
author: Candie Fix Managing Editor
description: After many conversations and months worth of work, the Haxtun Town Council adopted an ordinance establishing a truck route through city limits. The adoption came at a Monday evening, May 6 meeting of…
content:
After many conversations and months worth of work, the Haxtun Town Council adopted an ordinance establishing a truck route through city limits. The adoption came at a Monday evening, May 6 meeting of the Haxtun Town Council.
In 2021 Haxtun voters passed ballot question 2A to approve a major street project by a margin of 325 yes votes to 70 no votes. Since then, the Town of Haxtun has worked to complete those major street repairs and in doing so, the Council wishes to protect that investment.
Over the past year or so, many discussions around the Council table have involved a truck route for vehicles overweight and oversized. The ordinance states its intent is to restrict overweight and oversized vehicles as necessary to protect the health, safety and welfare of the Town's citizens and its streets.
Per the ordinance, found on page 3 of last week's of the Herald, all trucks weighing 15,000 pounds or more should use only the follow roadways: all of Washington Avenue (Highway 59) and First Street (Highway 6); south Cooper Avenue to east Fletcher Street; east Fletcher Street to Washington Avenue; all of Railroad Street; south Fairview Avenue from First Street to Railroad Street; south Colorado Avenue from First Street to Railroad Street; and south Burlington Avenue from First Street to Railroad Street.
The routes listed above are now known as the Haxtun Truck Route and should be utilized by all trucks exceeding 15,000 pounds. There are some exemptions, which can be found in the full ordinance. Copies of the full ordinance can be located at the Haxtun Town Hall or online at https://townofhaxtun.colorado.gov/. The Haxtun Police Department will be working with the public to education the new route.
At the start of the May meeting, council members held a public hearing for a zoning request for the CB & Pods Annexation. There was no public comment and no changes made to the annexation agreement. A public hearing was held on May 20 at 7 p.m. at the Town Hall to adopt the annexation resolution, annexation ordinance and zoning ordinance.
The land for the annexation sits just west of Dollar General and Better Forage lots on the south side of Highway 6. The plan is to use the space for storage units by CB & Pods.
Council members also spent time reviewing and discussing the Town's building permit application and policy. According to Town Clerk Kelsey Harms there were no changes made to the fee but some wording was added to the policy to address possible damages.
The policy change states that any person, homeowner or contractor, involved in the damage of Haxtun roadways during the construction or demolition process of the property is liable for the repairs of the roadway. The Town of Haxtun Superintendent will evaluate the damage and take necessary steps for the repairs and bill for the damages accordingly.
The addition to the policy, Harms said, is a way for the Town to protect the streets and upgrades the Town is working towards.
In other business:
• Discussed the Colorado State University Rural Action Project. The winning mural, called "One Heart, One Family, One Community" by Olivia Stone will be painted on the old concession stand at the ball park. That building is used for equipment storage;
• Tabled an Incentive application from Rod Salvador to gather more information;
• The Town of Haxtun received a grant for Town Hall to help with ADA accessibility for the website.

title: Haxtun Board of Education selects Jones from initial 10 applicants
author: Candie Fix Managing Editor
description: Following a long application and interview process, the Haxtun Board of Education selected the next Superintendent of Haxtun Schools. The Board voted to appoint Aron Jones as Superintendent starting…
content:
Following a long application and interview process, the Haxtun Board of Education selected the next Superintendent of Haxtun Schools. The Board voted to appoint Aron Jones as Superintendent starting July 1. That decision came on Tuesday afternoon, May 14 following candidate in-person interviews earlier that day and a community meet and greet the night prior.
The search for a new superintendent began in March. At that time, the local school board partnered with McPherson & Jacobson, LLC an executive recruitment and development firm used by the Haxtun School District in the past. Over the course of several weeks, McPherson and Jacobson created a job posting and collected applications; 10 in total.
Of those, school board members reviewed video introductions from each candidate as well as their applications. From those 10, the search was narrowed down to three candidates, Jones, Barry Schaeffer and Todd Bissell.
Those three candidates visited Haxtun last Monday and Tuesday. Tuesday morning brought on-site, in-person interviews and school tours. Later that day, the Board of Education met in executive session to discuss their choices. That closed-door meeting included board members, principals Becky Heinz and Amanda Ridlen and Business Manager Debbie Myers.
In just under an hour's time, the Board returned to regular, open meeting to vote on their final selection. Jones' appointment came unanimously.
Jones is currently principal and superintendent of Woodlin High School. He and his wife Vanessa have one son who just recently graduated from high school. His contract start date with Haxtun Schools is July 1.
After appointing a new superintendent, the Board moved on to regular business for the monthly, May meeting. In doing so, they first approved the personnel report as presented by current Superintendent Marsha Cody. Paige Thompson was named Certified Preschool Director; Dustin Seger was approved as Junior High Assistant Football Coach and Jessica Firme resigned from her position as elementary PE teacher and cheerleading sponsor.
The Board also:
• Approved disposing of bus four and seven by June 28; and
• Approved changes to the classified schedule to reflect pay for CDL and non CDL bus drivers.

content:
The Haxtun Town Council met in a special meeting on Monday night, May 20 for a public hearing regarding the CB & Pods Annexation. Hearing no concerns, the proper motions followed to approve the annexation.
The one acre of land on the west edge of Haxtun has been annexed into Haxtun city limits following a series of motions as required by Colorado State Statue. The CB & Pods annexation includes an acre of land on the south side of Highway 6, west of the current Better Forage site, also just west of Dollar General.

According to Carpenter, finish work continues on the pool with the goal of opening in June. As for the incentive application, the Council reviewed cost breakdown numbers and plan to add the subject to the June meeting agenda.

title: John Rhodes
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: We apologize for the inconvenience, but we must restart your session so you can continue browsing our website.
content:
John D. Rhodes passed away Thursday, May 30, 2024 at the Sedgwick County Hospital in Julesburg at the age of 79.
John was born in Julesburg on Sept. 30, 1944 to John and Elizabeth (Lundburg) Rhodes.
John's love for his family was evident in his upbringing on the family farm in the Fairfield Community, south of Haxtun, with his four sisters. He cherished his time there, creating lasting memories. He graduated from Haxtun High School in 1963.
John's unwavering dedication to his country was a testament to his character. He enlisted in the United States Air Force in April 1965 and served with pride for three years. Sargent Rhodes was an aircraft mechanic stationed at Yakota Air Force Base in Japan.
John married Lynette Alberts in Holyoke and had two children, Brenda and Scott. They later divorced.
John worked as a machinist for Timpe Tools in Denver for many years. After working for Timpte Trailers, he was a machinist at Morse Chain Company for several years. In 2019, he moved back to Julesburg to be closer to family and enjoyed the slower-paced life.
John found joy in his hobbies, particularly his love for classic cars. He was especially fond of his Classic Ford, which brought him many happy memories.
He is survived by his daughter Brenda Morrison, Westminster; grandsons Scott Morrison and Trevor Morrison; sisters Betty Smith and husband Ray, Fowler, Mary Young, Julesburg, Marlene Gastellum and husband David, Fort Bragg, Calif. and Virginia Garcia and husband Ruben, Phoneix, Ariz. as well as other relatives and friends.
John is preceded in death by his grandparents; parents; and son Scott Rhodes.
Condolences may be shared online at prairiehillsjulesburg.com, where the service will be streamed live.
Funeral services will be held on Thursday, June 6 at 10 a.m. at the Prairie Hills Funeral Home Chapel in Julesburg with Pastor Alan Harris officiating. Burial will be in the Haxtun Cemetery.
Prairie Hills Funeral Home of Julesburg is in charge of arrangements.
