title: Lady Wildcats move up 2 to number 2
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Fleming Lady Wildcats have worked their way into the top two in the Colorado High School Activities Association's weekly rankings. The local squad swept Otis and High Plains last week to move up…
content:
The Fleming Lady Wildcats have worked their way into the top two in the Colorado High School Activities Association's weekly rankings. The local squad swept Otis and High Plains last week to move up two spots from number four to number two behind the Merino Lady Rams in 1A action. Fleming is scheduled to meet Merino at the end of October.
The Lady Wildcats now stand at 11-2 on the season. All of those 11 victories have been 3-0 sweeps.
Last Thursday, the Lady Wildcats traveled to Otis to face off with the Lady Bulldogs. Otis played a close first set, but fell to the Lady Wildcats 27-25. Fleming won sets two and three by larger margins, 25-15 and 25-19 for the three-set win.
Junior Ciana Lousberg led her team at the net in assists and kills. She set the ball for the Lady Wildcat hitters 18 times and added 14 kills for the offense. She also led from behind the service line with five aces. She served 100 percent on 20 attempts scoring 15 points.
Junior Ashley Bornhoft added 14 kills at the net. She also tallied one assisted block.
Senior Kylie Bretz-Hoskins led the Wildcats' defensive efforts with three blocks; all of those assisted. Junior Quincy Stull followed with two assisted blocks.
Junior libero Brooke Schaefer led in the back row. She put up 14 digs with zero errors and received 25 serves with a single error. Sophomore Hadley Stull followed in receives with 12.
On Friday night, the Lady Wildcats traveled to Seibert where they took on the Hi-Plains Lady Patriots. The Lady Wildcats held the home team in the teens for all three sets winning 25-19, 25-18 and 25-15.
Bornhoft and Quincy Stull lee the Lady Wildcats in attacks, both hitting double digits in the contest. Bornhoft led with 13; Stull followed with 10.
Bornhoft along with Schaefer and sophomore Hayley Chamberlain each served two aces for the night. Bornhoft served 100 percent for 10 points; Schaefer served 21 times scoring 15 points.
Bornhoft led at the net on defense with four total blocks. She blocked two solo and two assisted.
Three Lady Wildcats hit double digits in the dig category led by Schaefer and Lousberg with 13 apiece. Chamberlain added another 11.
Schaefer also led on serve receive with 25. Freshman Hadley Stull also hit double digits with 10 receives.
The Lady Wildcats are scheduled for a busy week this week. They open with a Thursday, Oct. 10 contest at Weldon Valley. The two teams met in mid-September with Fleming taking a 3-0 match win. Play is set to begin at 5:30 on that day.
On Friday, Fleming hits the road to Peetz where they'll take on the Lady Bulldogs for the second time this season. Their earlier outing ended in a Lady Wildcat sweep. A 4 p.m. start time is listed for Friday, Oct. 11 at Peetz.
On Tuesday, Oct. 15, Fleming is set to travel to Haxtun to play the 10-4 Lady Bulldogs. Action at Haxtun is scheduled to start at 4 p.m.
The Lady Wildcats close out the week next Thursday, Oct. 17 on their own home court against Prairie. Fleming defeated the Lady Mustangs by sweep in late-September.

title: Wildcats take 30-point league victory on the road at Peetz; Kuntz adds 324 rushing yards making way into top 2 Colorado
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Wildcats of Fleming stand in second place in 6-man's North Central League behind top-ranked Caliche following a big Friday night victory over league foe Peetz. The Wildcats are now ranked number…

count
The Wildcats of Fleming stand in second place in 6-man's North Central League behind top-ranked Caliche following a big Friday night victory over league foe Peetz. The Wildcats are now ranked number 11 in the state in 6-man and Caliche sits at number eight, according to Colorado High School Activities Association rankings. Those two teams are set to meet on Nov.1 in the regular season closer.
The story of Friday night's win over Peetz came down to Fleming's running game. The local team rushed for 605 yards in the contest in comparison to Peetz's 252.
Lonestar senior Grant Kuntz, who plays running back for the Wildcats this year, gained 324 ground yards against Peetz on Friday night. He is the top rusher in the State throughout the 6-8-man divisions. Kuntz sits in the number two spot in rushing yards among all classifications with 1,281 rushing yards on the season, less than 100 yards behind the top-ranked man.
At Peetz, Kuntz carried the ball 18 times averaging 18 yards per carry. He rushed along of 47 yards and scored four rushing touchdowns.
Sophomore Conner Marchant racked up 245 rushing yards on 22 carries. He ran for a long of 57 yards and scored six rushing touchdowns.
Sophomore quarterback Treyson Kirkwood completed four of six passes for the night. He threw for 88 total yards and one touchdown, earning a QB rating of 149.3.
Junior Pierson Japp caught four passes in the game, earning 88 Wildcat yards. He scored one touchdown.
Four Wildcats hit double digits and tackles. Kuehn led the charge with 14. He made eight solo and six assisted tackles. Senior Peter Brekel followed with 13 total tackles; split at seven and six, respectively. Freshman Dylon Monroe brought down 12 tackles. He tallied five solo and seven assisted. Junior Mason Mollohan brought down 11; split at four and seven, respectively.
Other highlights of the contest include two deflected passes by Brekel. Marchant and Monroe each deflected one pass. Sophomore Michael Weis blocked one field goal. Freshman Alex Champ recovered one fumble. Kuntz caught one interception and returned it 36 yards.
Marchant led on the scoreboard with 36 points off his six rushing TDs. Kuntz followed with 24. Junior Dane Cunningham added 10 points off points-after kicks. He made good on five of 11 attempts. Japp rounded out Fleming's tally with six points in the Wildcats 76-46 victory over Peetz.
Next up the Wildcats are scheduled to host Briggsdale on Friday, Oct. 18. The Falcons sit at 3-3 overall and are the fifth ranked team in the league behind Peetz. Kick off on Friday is set for 7:30 p.m.

title: Haxtun Health gives back locally
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Haxtun Health has completed their annual campaign, "Healthy Student, Happy Teacher." During the months of June, July and August, for every student who completes a Well Child Check or annual wellness…
content:
(Courtesy photo) count
FLEMING School Principal Kortney Firme, left, and Haxtun Junior/Senior High Principal Amanda Ridlen, right, receive funds for classrooms from Haxtun Health's "Healthy Student, Happy Teacher" campaign.
Haxtun Health has completed their annual campaign, "Healthy Student, Happy Teacher." During the months of June, July and August, for every student who completes a Well Child Check or annual wellness exam, Haxtun Health donates $10 to that student's classroom teacher to help offset classroom expenses. The ultimate goal is to help students start the year on a healthy note and set them up for success as the cooler months, which often bring illnesses, approach.
These annual exams provide an opportunity for the Haxtun Health team to perform checkups and administer any due vaccines. Routine checks allow providers to identify and address potential issues early. The "Healthy Student, Happy Teacher" campaign continues to grow each year.
Haxtun Health also aims to support teachers, who often use personal funds to purchase classroom supplies.
"We are so grateful to partner with our local school districts as we continue to pursue optimal health for everyone in northeast Colorado," said Sara Huss, Marketing and Communication Coordinator at Haxtun Health. "We hope that our joint efforts lead to a healthier school year and healthier households."
This summer, Haxtun Health performed 61 qualifying Well Child Checks, resulting in $610 donated back to schools, including Haxtun, Fleming, Holyoke and Revere.

Larry David Rutledge entered into eternal life on Thursday, Oct. 24, 2024 at the age of 80.
Larry was born Nov. 14, 1943 in Auburn, Neb. to Carroll Carson and Cora Merle (Hutchinson) Rutledge. Larry enlisted in the United States Army at Ft. Leonard Wood, Mo. and was honorably discharged on April 24, 1965. He married Carolyn Sue Henderson on Dec. 28, 1971 in Loveland. Larry worked as an engineer at Lockheed Martin for many years.
Larry is survived by his wife Carolyn; daughters Barbara Holsapfel, Carrie and husband Greg Zimmerman and Catherine Castillo; grandchildren Cora (Karma), Triston, Dawna, Katie, Lincoln, Dane, Trinity and Lexanna.
He is preceded in death by his parents; sister Norma Jean Hoff; and brother John Carroll Rutledge.
Memorial contributions may be made in Larry's name to Berean Bible Church, 137 W. Bryan, Haxtun, CO 80731.
A funeral service will be held at 10:30 a.m., Friday, Nov. 1 at the Berean Bible Church in Haxtun with Pastor Don LaRue and Pastor Matt Waitley officiating. Larry will be laid to rest with military honors at the Fleming Cemetery.

title: Dec. 1st benefit planned for Mike & Kim Bowers
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: In October 2022 Mike Bowers began experiencing severe headaches and what seemed like vertigo. He also was beginning to have panic attacks for no apparent reason. These attacks lasted for over a year. In July of 2023, Mike had a panic attack while driving his family home from a work event. After that incident, Mike quit driving for his safety and others for around six months. Mike, and his wife...
content:
In October 2022 Mike Bowers began experiencing severe headaches and what seemed like vertigo. He also was beginning to have panic attacks for no apparent reason. These attacks lasted for over a year. In July of 2023, Mike had a panic attack while driving his family home from a work event. After that incident, Mike quit driving for his safety and others for around six months.
Mike, and his wife Kim, live in the Wages community with their children, Sawyer, Lincoln and Phoenix. He is the Superintendent/Principal at Lone Star Schools. Their children attend Haxtun Schools and are currently in seventh, fourth and second grades.
When the symptoms didn't seem to fade, Mike went to see his local doctor. Medical staff performed routine blood work, checked for vertigo, did a brain scan and ultimately treated him for anxiety.
None of the anxiety medication helped and he was beginning to experience severe shoulder and neck pain. He was then referred to a neurologist at UC Health Neurology clinic in Greeley. In the fall he underwent a battery of blood work, scans, genetic testing and imaging.
After consultation, Mike was referred to another Doctor at UC Health Anschutz in Denver who was a movement disorder neurology specialist. There he, again, went through a battery of exams, blood work and genetic testing. It was during that visit that Mike was diagnosed with Cervical Dystonia.
According to definition from the Mayo Clinic's website, Cervical Dystonia, also sometimes called spasmodic torticollis, is a painful condition in which neck muscles contract involuntarily, causing the head to twist or turn to one side. Cervical Dystonia can also cause the head to uncontrollably tilt forward or backward. It is a rare disorder that can occur at any age, but most often occurs in middle-aged people. There is no cure for Cervical Dystonia, however, injecting botulinum toxin into the affected muscles often reduces the signs and symptoms.
On Oct. 6, 2023 Mike received his first dose of Botox from his neurologist. The treatment gave him little relief. Four days later he received a spinal tap to rule out other disorders. Over the course of the next two weeks he saw an ENT specialist, an audiologist, optometrist and genetic counselor. In November he was given another round of Botox by his doctor. This also did not give much relief.
Doctors decided to refer Mike to the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minn. to see a movement specialist at their neurology center. In January this year, Mike met with a specialist at Mayo for a consultation. He was able to have a consultation with a neurosurgeon as well.
The neurosurgeon agreed that Mike was a candidate for a surgery called selective denervation for torticollis. Another appointment was scheduled at the Mayo Clinic to perform a procedure called muscle mapping to pinpoint which nerves in his neck were causing the torticollis.
This information was sent to his doctors at Anschutz as his insurance, Anthem, would not cover the cost of the Botox or surgery at Mayo as it was deemed out of network. This is a very rare surgery, which is why most neurologists aren't aware of the procedure.
Moving forward without surgery and minimal relief from Botox, Mike's neck is stuck to the right and down to his right shoulder. He worked from home for most of the 2023-24 school year as he wasn't able to drive nor sit in a normal chair.
His children are all very active in school, sports, music and other activities and not being able to drive has also drastically changed their lives as he's no longer able to help out nor attend any of their activities. Not being able to be a part of his family's daily life has made a huge impact on Mike as he is a very active person. Mike has worked very hard on maintaining a good, positive attitude, but his mental health is definitely a concern of his moving forward without proper treatment.
Mike began to see a new doctor in Colorado that his insurance company deemed to be in network. After multiple appointments Mike was able to see some positive results with the different techniques and higher doses of Botox. Mike was looking forward to his next appointment where the neurologist decided it was probably time to consider surgery.
Once again, Anthem insurance jumped in and decided that his new doctor was now out of network. The cost of either the selective denervation neck surgery or DBS, which is a deep brain stimulation surgery, were now off the table. The cost of both surgeries are between $90,000-$100,000 and must be paid upfront. Mike knows this is just not an option.
Mike has begun driving again and is back to work in person, part-time. Ultimately, he knows he needs surgery to give him a normal quality of life and he is doing his best to live with his current diagnosis.
Unfortunately, Cervical Dystonia is not curable, but through research, patients have been able to thrive when given the option to have either of the surgeries mentioned prior.
To help get Mike the medical treatment necessary for the best quality of life possible, friends and family have rallied around the Bowers family. An account has been set up at the Haxtun Community Federal Credit Union and a benefit is planned for Sunday, Dec. 1 at Lone Star School.
The Bowers Family benefit includes dinner from 4-6 p.m. followed by live and silent auctions and a magic show on Sunday, Dec. 1. Illusionist Dave Laflin plans to perform following the dinner and the live auction. Tickets for the dinner and show are $20 for adults and $10 for children 12 and under. Tickets for the benefit may be purchased day of at the door.
To make a donation to the Bowers Family, checks may be mailed to the Haxtun Community Federal Credit Union at P.O. Box 41, Haxtun, CO 80731 payable to Mike and/or Kim Bowers. Donations may also be made by debit or credit card by visiting http://www.haxtuncu.com, clicking on Make A Deposit and adding Mike and Kim Bowers to the Comment Area.
For more information contact Kristin Hadeen at (970) 774-7396.

title: Bulldogs earn third League title in four years; sit #1 in 8-man action
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Haxtun Bulldogs are the 2024 Plains League Champions. The team clinched the title following a 32-6 win over Sedgwick County on Friday night. The championship marks the Bulldog's third in the last…
content:
(Courtesy photo from Ryan Kanode) count
THE 2024 Haxtun Bulldogs clinched the Plains League Championship following a 32-6 win over Sedgwick County in Julesburg on Friday night. Haxtun sits #1 in 8-man action in State standings and is set to face Hoehne at home in first round play off action on Saturday.
(Herald photo by Candie Fix) count
Zach Statz
The Haxtun Bulldogs are the 2024 Plains League Champions. The team clinched the title following a 32-6 win over Sedgwick County on Friday night. The championship marks the Bulldog's third in the last four years.
"Our League is special, proof of that is 90 percent of the State Championships have come out of it over the last 35 years," Bulldog Head Coach JD Stone said. "Winning our third league title in the last four years is very special to us, it was a major goal of ours, but it isn't our ultimate goal."
With an overall 8-1 record and going undefeated in the Lower Platte League gives the Haxtun Bulldogs the number one spot in Colorado High School Activities Association final RIP rankings in 8-man football. Seeded first, Haxtun is now set to face 16th seeded Hoehne in the first round of post-season play.
Haxtun went up 20-0 in first half action in Julesburg against the Cougars on Friday night. With the outcome of the league title on the line, the Bulldogs came out in the second half, holding the Cougars to only six points while adding another 12 for a final 32-6 victory and the Plains League Championship in the final week of regular season play.
"We played very physically, both on the front and back end of our defense," Stone said of the Bulldog's performance on Friday night.
In the absence of senior quarterback Ryland Wolff due to an ankle injury, junior Colin Cone started for Haxtun's offense. He completed six of 11 passes for 102 yards and completed one touchdown pass. Senior Grant Statz threw one pass, resulting in a 32-yard score for the Bulldogs.
Chase Goddard racked up 103 yards off four receptions including two touchdowns on Friday. He averaged 25.8 yard per catch.
Grant Statz led the Bulldog's ground game with 142 yards and two rushing touchdowns. He averaged 5.9 yards per carry. Cone carried the ball 11 times for 106 yards. Junior Zach Statz carried the ball 10 times for 32 yards, including one trip into the end zone.
Total the Bulldogs earned 410 yards on offense against the Cougars.
Grant Statz and Cole Firme led in tackles, combing for a total of 26. Grant Statz totaled 16 including nine solo and seven assisted. Firme racked up 11 with seven solo and four assisted. Zach Statz, Kanin Koberstein and Corbin Andersen each registered six total tackles.
Seth Seger sacked the Cougars quarterback once.
The release of CHSAA'S final RPI rankings and 8-man playoff bracket puts Haxtun in a first round contest against Hoehne on Saturday, Nov. 9 at 1 p.m. at Adam Wernsman Field. According to MaxPreps, the Hoehne Farmers are 6-3 overall and went 5-0 in their league.
"We must be mentally prepared, both for the weather and for Hoehne's 35 different offensive formations," Stone said of preparations for this week's game.
CHSAA information states that all higher seeded teams in the bracket will host until the finals.
A win this week in the first round would send Haxtun to the quarterfinals in a match up against the winner of a contest between eighth ranked Sanford and Springfield, who came in ninth.
"This team has goals and is willing to do almost anything it takes to reach them," Stone said of his Bulldogs.
A complete playoff bracket can be found at chsaanow.com.

content:
The Lady Bulldogs punched their ticket to the 2A State Volleyball Tournament at the Denver Coliseum this weekend with a Region 12 Championship on Monday. Haxtun enters the State Tournament as the ninth seeded team and is set to face Del Norte in round one on Thursday.
Haxtun's road to State was delayed due to Colorado's winter weather. What was supposed to be Saturday afternoon Regional pool play was forced to be played on Monday, Nov. 11 due to snow that covered much of the mountains over the weekend, making it difficult for teams to travel on Friday and Saturday.
Monday's action put Haxtun on the court first with Custer County and then with Denver Christian. Region 12 volleyball action took place at Denver Christian, the home of the Lady Thunder, who earned the 12th seed in Colorado High School Activities Association Regional bracket paired by RPI ratings following the regular season. Haxtun came in 13th and Custer County entered as the 25th seed.
As the higher seated hosting team, Denver Christian took the court first, taking down Custer County in three. The second match of the day pitted the Lady Bulldogs against the Lady Bobcats from Custer County. Haxtun picked up a sweep in the first contest, winning 25-10, 25-20 and 25-14.
The second contest for the Lady Bulldogs put them against the Lady Thunder of Denver Christian. Haxtun went up two sets, taking the first 25-18 and the second, 25-23, but fell the following two, sending the contest to five. The Lady Bulldogs came out hot in the final set, making sure to leave their mark in history with a Regional Championship and extending their season to include the State Tournament, with a 15-7 victory.
Senior Jayleigh Bullard put down a commanding 34 kills in Regional pool play. She led her team with a .369 hitting percentage. Senior Bobbi Starkebaum registered 24 combined kills in the two contests followed by Emma Henry with 16, Maggie Kilgour with 15 and Josie Freeman with 12. Starkebaum led at the net with 10 total blocks. Bullard trailed with six, Freeman racked up five and Emma Lemesany registered four.
Kilgour and Lilly Lemesany led the Lady Bulldogs in aces, each sending over six. Emily Anderson tallied two aces and Bullard had one. Starkebaum served 100 percent in the two-contest outing, sending over a total of 30 serves.
In the back row, Kilgour led the Lady Bulldog defense with 29 digs. Anderson and Lilly Lemesany each tallied 19 digs in the back row followed by Starkebaum with 17 and Kelsie Hadeen with 16.
As setters, Starkebaum and Hadeen combined for 79 assists throughout the eight sets of action in Denver on Monday. Starkebaum registered 42 assists while Hadeen contributed 37.
The 2-0 Regional showing puts the Lady Bulldogs at 16-8 overall entering the final week of volleyball action. Haxtun is seated ninth at State in a 12 team tournament bracket released Tuesday by CHSAA.
Haxtun's first contest at State is set for 8 a.m. on Thursday against Del Norte, who enters the bracket as the eighth seeded team.
According to MaxPreps, the Lady Tigers of Del Norte are 21-2 and went 6-0 in their Southern Peaks League.
A win for Haxtun would advance the Lady Bulldogs to a contest later the same day against the top ranked Simla Cubs. For a complete 2A State Volleyball bracket, visit chsaanow.com.
Each of the five classifications will play their tournaments this Thursday, Friday and Saturday at the Denver Coliseum. Play begins at 8 a.m. each day with championship matches set for 6 p.m. on Saturday.

title: Kelley takes over at PC Veterans' Service Officer
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Chris Kelley is Phillips County's new Veteran's Service Officer. Kelley took over his new role with the County on Nov. 1 as an appointment made by the Phillips County Commissioners. Kelley grew up in…
content:
(Courtesy photo) count
THE KELLEY FAMILY, front row (l-r), Camden and Carson; back row (l-r), Holly, Chris and Kallin.
Chris Kelley is Phillips County's new Veteran's Service Officer. Kelley took over his new role with the County on Nov. 1 as an appointment made by the Phillips County Commissioners.
Kelley grew up in Central, Nebraska and moved to Haxtun with his family when his wife, Holly, took a position with Haxtun Schools as the Family Consumer Science Teacher.
After high school, Kelley served active duty with the United States Marine Corps from 1996-1998. He served as a Lance Corporal before he was involuntarily discharged under honorable conditions due to a service-connected injury. Kelley received the National Defense Service Medal.
Kelley takes the reigns as the local Veterans' Service Officer following a vacancy left by Jeremy Kilpatrick in late August. Kilpatrick served as VSO in Phillips County for three years. Prior to his service, Haxtun's Steve Firme assisted local Veterans for a numbers of years.
"As I am just starting out as a Veteran Service Officer, I am just learning about services and duties," Kelley said. "I have already reached out to several resources and hope to get all of those resources working for our Veterans here in Phillips County."
Each county in Colorado has a Veterans' Service Office that offers free assistance to Veterans. Veterans' Service Officers specialize in assisting Veterans, and their family members, with claims, applications and appeals to the Veterans Affairs.
"As a Veteran myself, my priorities are to make sure that our Veterans, their dependents and survivors here in Phillips County have a point of contact if they find themselves needing help with a variety of topics, questions or concerns," said Kelley.
To reach Kelley for resources, benefits or other information, local Veterans can call (970) 520-6310 or email [email protected].
"Some Veterans are going to need some basic information or help with documents. I believe many Veterans are going to be in unique situations and I will do everything I can in these situations," Kelley said.

title: Lady Bulldogs end season with top six finish at State Tournament
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Only six teams remain in each classification's bracket as of Saturday morning of the Colorado State Volleyball tournament and in their first year returning to 2A, the Lady Bulldogs were one of the top…
content:
(Herald photo by Candie Fix) count
LADY BULLDOG blockers Josie Freeman, #2, and Maggie Kilgour, #18, get up and over the net for a touch against Del Norte hitter, #10, Addie Roepke in the opening round of the 2A State Volleyball Tournament.
(Herald photo by Candie Fix) count
HAXTUN LIBERO #3 Lilly Lemesany saves a pass in the back row in the Lady Bulldogs' contest at State with Simla. Setter Kelsie Hadeen watches from the back.
Only six teams remain in each classification's bracket as of Saturday morning of the Colorado State Volleyball tournament and in their first year returning to 2A, the Lady Bulldogs were one of the top six teams in the State. Haxtun entered the 2024 playoff bracket as the ninth ranked team following a Region 12 Championship just three days prior to the start of the Colorado State Volleyball Tournament.
Haxtun's road at the State Tournament started early on Thursday morning as the ninth ranked Lady Bulldogs took on eighth seeded Del Norte to kick action off on the 2A court. The Bulldogs earned a sweep, 25-21, 25-18 and 25-21, in their first outing at the Denver Coliseum last week. That win pitted the hometown ladies in red in a match up with Simla later that afternoon.
Simla, who entered the bracket as the top team, had a first round bye, putting them on the court against the Lady Bulldogs in their State Tournament debut on Thursday afternoon. The Lady Cubs took sets one and two, 25-22 and 25-15 but Haxtun played the number one team tight, taking set three 25-23. The 2A court was loud and active throughout the fourth, but the Cubs came out on top, 25-27 to advance to the third round. The loss for the Lady Bulldogs sent the team to the elimination bracket.
Friday's action put Haxtun on the court in a match up with 10th ranked Vail Christian, who had suffered a five set loss to Rye to enter the elimination bracket. Haxtun took that contest in four, 25-22, 25-18, 25-18 and 25-22. That put the Lady Bulldogs into the second round of the right side of the Colorado High School Activity Association's bracket, released last week based on the outcome of regional contests and data from RPI rankings. Haxtun earned a four set win over the next opponent, Hoehne, 25-22, 25-20, 17-25 and 27-17.
In their fifth game on the State Tournament courts, Haxtun was up against the Lady Tigers from Wiggins in Saturday morning action. At that time in the tournament, only six teams remain as the double-elimination bracket begins to send teams home on Friday. Teams playing in Saturday's opening matches are subject to CHSAA tradition of the chicken dance with officials, shaggers and the audience.
Despite their efforts, the Lady Bulldogs fell to their Lower Platte League opponent in three, ending the 2024 season short of a semifinals contest but as a top six State finisher.
"I thought our girls had a great State Tournament! You always want to finish better, but they played their hearts out! This group of girls have so much grit and determination. Seven games in six days was a lot but I felt they persevered through all the tough moments!" said Lady Bulldog Head Coach Don Schelling. "I think the biggest takeaway was that they never gave up! They believed the whole time that, regardless of who they played, they could win. I think the Simla game was a testament of that! They were neck and neck with a team who had only lost one game all season."
Wiggins went on to defeat Simla in four in the semifinals to meet up with Sedgwick County in the Championship match on Saturday night. The Lady Cougars from Sedgwick County earned the four-set win for the 2A State Title, the team's third in four years. On the 1A court, McClave took down Fleming in the final four to advance to the Championship game. They came out on top over Merino, ending the Lady Rams' run for a fifth straight Title.
"We have a brutal schedule and every loss we had this season, except for one, was in the State Tournament. We also beat two State Tournament teams. This team is an amazing group of young ladies and I'm super proud of everything they accomplished. Most importantly though, the thing I'm most proud of, is the way they represent their school and community!" Schelling said.
The 2024 Lady Bulldogs earned an overall 65.5 winning percentage with a final 19-10 record. Haxtun went 5-3 in the 2A/1A combined Lower Platte League, finishing fourth. At home, the Lady Bulldogs went 9-2 and on the road earned a 3-4 record. At neutral sites Haxtun sat 7-4. Throughout the end of August and most of September, the Lady Bulldogs went on a six-game win streak, their longest of the season including wins over Holyoke, Otis, Dayspring Christian Academy, Arickaree, Wichita County and Caliche.
This year's 31-member team will bid farewell to six seniors come spring commencement ceremonies including Jayleigh Bullard, Emily Anderson, Kennidee Koerber, Kelsie Hadeen, Bobbi Starkebaum and Maggie Kilgour.
At the conclusion of the State Tournament, several post-season honors were announced. Starkebaum and Kilgour received All-Conference honors and Kelsie Hadeen and Lilly Lemesany were named All-Conference, Honorable Mention. Starkebaum and Kilgour were selected to play in the Colorado Coaches of Girls Sports All-State games this weekend. Schelling was selected to coach the CCGS All-State games.
"My best memory of the State Tournament was just watching this team bond together underneath the Coliseum and watching them enjoy the moment! My favorite memory of the season is the Regional Tournament Championship, in the fifth set, when we won and qualified for the State Tournament, again," Schelling said, recalling the season. "What is special about this team is how they supported each other and genuinely love one another. We had great senior leaders that will truly be missed!"

The Frenchman Board of Education heard from a group of Fleming seniors in their final meeting of the fiscal year. The 12th grade students presented plans for the annual senior trip, which was given approval by the Board. In addition, board members approved mill levy and October count numbers in the Dec. 11 get-together.
Beau Ashburn, Peter Brekel and Savanna Taylor presented plans for the 2025 Senior trip, slated for mid-March to Miami, Fla. This year's class includes 10 seniors who plan to visit the beach, go to an escape room, play laser tag and take a boat tour through the Florida Keys. Amy and Jeff Brekel are senior class sponsors.
After the presentation, the Board voted to approve the trip, with Board Member Brekel abstaining from the vote.
Later, in action items, the local BOE in Fleming, approved the 2024-25 October student count data. According to Superintendent Steve McCracken, this year's data shows 222 students in Fleming. Last year the District had 221 students and they year before that, 201.
Additionally, the Board approved mill levy numbers. The total General Fund Mill Levy was set at 28.141.
In her report, Principal Kortney Firme said Fleming Schools received a local food program grant for $1,376. Those funds will be used to purchase a new salad bar for the food service program.
In other business the Board:
• Approved Brekka Richardson as a substitute teacher;
• Approved a quote from Bayley Mechanical for a heater in the construction trades shop;
• Approved Nate Japp as an Assistant Basketball Coach;

title: SC/F lady wrestlers claim team title at Marilyn Smith Invitational
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Sedgwick County/Fleming lady wrestlers traveled to Wray on Saturday, Dec. 21, for the second annual Marilyn Smith Invitational Wrestling Tournament, where they delivered an impressive performance,…
content:
(Courtesy photo) count
135-POUND ANNIE Wilson secured the Championship at the Marilyn Smith Invitational in Wray when she defeated Lauren Gdanitz of Wray by fall in 1:28.
The Sedgwick County/Fleming lady wrestlers traveled to Wray on Saturday, Dec. 21, for the second annual Marilyn Smith Invitational Wrestling Tournament, where they delivered an impressive performance, culminating in a team title victory. With a combined total of 72 team points, Sedgwick County/Fleming outperformed a competitive field that included teams such as Wiggins (55 points), Yuma (53.5 points) and Wray (44.5 points). The tournament featured a number of combined weight classes, including 100-105, 110-115, 120-125, 130-135, 140-145, and 155-170, showcasing a variety of talent and skill across the board.
Several SC/F athletes placed in the top positions in their respective weight classes, contributing to the team's overall success. Here's a breakdown of the individual performances for wrestlers competing out of Fleming and Haxtun:
Autumn Volkman faced some tough opponents in the 125-pound weight class, finishing with a 0-4 season record. Despite her losses, Volkman gained valuable experience competing at the tournament level. In round one, Volkman lost by decision to Heidi Vargas of Yuma, 5-2. In round two, she lost fall to Lexie Amendt of SC/F in 2:26. She lost to Sky Richards of Liberty /Joes in round three by fall in 1:23. She closed the day with a loss by fall to Christina Lopez of SC/F in 0:57.
Annie Wilson finished in first place in the 135-pound division, securing a perfect 4-0 record during the tournament and a 11-4 season record. Wilson earned victories by fall over Makena Crownover, Kinsleigh Jerman and Lauren Gdanitz, while also claiming a medical forfeit win over Ren Richards. She defeated Crownover of Wiggins by fall in 3:27; defeated Jerman of SC/F by fall in 3:38; won by medical forfeit over Ren Richards of Liberty/Joes; and defeated Gdanitz of Wray by fall in 1:28.
Kinsleigh Jerman placed fourth in the 135-pound weight class with a solid 9-5 season record. Despite facing tough opponents, Jerman secured a win in the first round over Ren Richards but struggled against her teammates and other competitors. Jerman won by fall over Richards Liberty/Joes in 0:45. She lost to Annie Wilson of SC/F by fall in 3:38. In round three, Jerman lost by fall to Lauren Gdanitz of Wray in 6:00. She closed the day with a loss to Makena Crownover of Wiggins by fall in 3:04.
Kaiya Hall had a challenging tournament in the 145-pound division, finishing with a 4-6 season record. Hall faced two tough opponents and was unable to secure any wins in the competition. She lost to Riley Erickson of Wiggins by fall in 1:11 and Lillian Miller of SC/F by fall in 0:57.
Olivia Stone earned a fifth-place finish in the 170-pound division, finishing with a 5-6 season record. Despite some tough losses, Stone earned key points for the team and showed resilience throughout her matches. She won round one by fall over Riley Torres of SC/F in 1:09. She suffered round two and three losses to Addison Mayer of Wiggins by fall in 2:59 and Bralynn Arroyo of Wiggins by fall in 1:57. Stone took medical forfeits to Kayle Stults of Wray and Sierra Brown of Yuma in her final two events of the day.
According to info on the team's Facebook page, the girls' team is scheduled to compete in a dual at Yuma on Thursday, Jan. 9 at 6:30 p.m. On Saturday, they are set to compete in the Garden County Invitational at Oshkosh, Neb. with matches beginning at 9 a.m.

title: HEA receives $1 million Federal grant for grid upgrades to mitigate wildfire risks
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Highline Electric Association has received $1.02 million from the United States Department of Energy to enhance wildfire protection and resilience in the communities it serves by making critical…
content:
Highline Electric Association has received $1.02 million from the United States Department of Energy to enhance wildfire protection and resilience in the communities it serves by making critical upgrades to its electric system. HEA is a member of a consortium of 38 electric co-ops and other rural utilities selected to receive federal funding through the Wildfire Assessment and Resilience for Networks project, or WARN.
'Highline Electric is pleased to have been awarded DOE WARN funding that will bolster our efforts to mitigate wildfire risk throughout our rural footprint. Funds will be used to help purchase and install electronic reclosers allowing our Engineering and Operations teams to remotely monitor and control line sections in high wildfire risk areas and avoid potential ignition during high wildfire risk events.' says Tad Huser, Manager of Member Services at HEA.
Visit HEA's Department of Energy WARN webpage to see more details about our wildfire mitigation efforts involved in this project at http://www.hea.coop/DOEMemberOutreach.
Led by Holy Cross Energy in coordination with NRECA Research, WARN will provide more than $145 million in wildfire mitigation funding to co-ops across 16 states in the central and western United States to drive energy resilience in high-risk rural areas.
'Electric cooperatives are focused on leveraging innovative solutions to meet tomorrow's energy needs,' said NRECA Chief Executive Officer Jim Matheson. 'This infrastructure funding is an important step as electric co-ops work to harden systems against wildfires and enhance the reliability of the grid. These projects hold tremendous potential for local communities as their co-ops unlock new ways to use technology to help mitigate wildfires and keep the lights on.'
Working together, consortium members will share lessons learned and expertise and provide real world data to create an advanced analysis tool to identify the likely impacts of utility-ignited wildfires on regional electricity supplies and local communities.
WARN funding comes from DOE's Grid Resilience and Innovation Partnerships program created by the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.

title: "Operation: Health Improvement" webinar scheduled for Friday, Jan. 31
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The new year is upon us and with it comes many resolutions or promises to ourselves to 'do better.' Often those promises are related to our habits and health. If only it were as easy to do as it is to…
content:
The new year is upon us and with it comes many resolutions or promises to ourselves to 'do better.' Often those promises are related to our habits and health. If only it were as easy to do as it is to say! Join Colorado State University Extension on Friday, Jan. 31 at noon for a webinar presentation by Karla Saffer to gain some insight and tools to help make doing better a more successful reality.
Karla Saffer, RN, CDCES, NBC-HWC, is a native of Colorado and has lived in Yuma County since 1998. Saffer currently coordinates the diabetes education and lifestyle medicine programs at the Wray Hospital and Clinic. These programs address whole-person health with special emphasis on behavior change to mitigate, manage and/or prevent chronic diseases. Saffer's approach is to blend tools of traditional medicine, lifestyle medicine and positive psychology, along with leveraging individual's habits of living, to achieve and sustain improved health. This in turn helps people reach a higher level of well-being, particularly when health behavior change is hard.
Saffer's webinar presentation will provide evidence-based research to help people approach health improvement in a potentially different way for lasting, positive health behavior change. She will also introduce tools that create motivation and increase power to change through visioning, goal setting, accountability and self-discovery that lead to 'best self.'
The 'Operation: Health Improvement' webinar is free but registration is requested by contacting your local host site listed below for in-person participation or you may attend virtually from your location by registering at http://diabeteswebinarjan2025.eventbrite.com.
Webinar host sites include: Kit Carson County, CSU Extension, (719) 346-5571; Logan County, CSU Extension, (970) 522-3200; Morgan County, CSU Extension, (970) 542-3540; Phillips County, CSU Extension, (970) 854-3616, Pueblo County, CSU Extension, (719) 583-6566; Wray Community District Hospital, (970) 332-2352; or Yuma Public Library, (970) 848-2368.

title: SC/F girls make strong showings at Elm Creek and Chase County
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Sedgwick County/Fleming girls wrestling team showcased their strength and determination at the Elm Creek Invitational 2025, with several athletes putting up impressive performances. While the team…
content:
The Sedgwick County/Fleming girls wrestling team showcased their strength and determination at the Elm Creek Invitational 2025, with several athletes putting up impressive performances. While the team faced tough competition, they made their presence felt across multiple weight classes. Results from wrestlers competing out of Fleming and Haxtun are as follows:
Bella Allen entered the 105-pound bracket with a 0-3 season record and battled hard throughout the tournament. After a quick loss in the quarterfinals to Laney Becker of Southern Valley/Arapahoe, Allen bounced back with a win by fall over Sonia Heinrichs of Thayer Central, and another victory over Renee Allen, Fillmore Central. Her comeback journey was cut short, however, when Dacie Henderson of Broken Bow pinned her in the third place match. Allen's performance earned her fourth place and 10 team points.
Annie Wilson made a strong push for the 130-pound title, securing victories in her quarterfinal and semifinal matches by fall. Wilson pinned Jeannie Hatterman, Fillmore Central, in just 28 seconds and Audrina Wall, Alma, in 27 seconds. In the finals, she met Braelyn Degenhardt, Thayer Central, and was pinned in 1:18. Despite the loss, Wilson's performance earned her second place and another 18 team points for SCF.
Kaiya Hall's 135-pound tournament was a challenging one. After receiving a bye in the first round, she was pinned in the quarterfinals by Ambie Custard of Southwest, the tournament favorite with a perfect 30-0 record. Despite a loss to Andrea Saravia, Cozad, in the consolation round, Hall continued to fight hard and contributed to the team's overall effort.
Olivia Stone faced tough competition in the 155-pound division, with three straight pins in her matches, ending in fourth place. Although she was unable to secure a win, the experience will undoubtedly serve as valuable preparation for future tournaments.
The SC/F girls' team showed remarkable promise at the Elm Creek Invite 2025, finishing with several top placements across multiple weight classes. With key performances from athletes like L.Torres, Amendt, Wilson and Lopez, the team showed depth and determination. While the team did not win the overall title, the individual placements helped rack up valuable points.
The 2025 Chase County Girls Invitational proved to be a showcase of strength and resilience for Sedgwick County/Fleming's female wrestlers. With several top finishes and standout performances, the team made their mark across a variety of weight classes. Leading the way were Lexie Amendt, Annie Wilson, and Christina Lopez, who all delivered impressive results, while others like Lily Torres and Olivia Stone demonstrated grit despite facing tough competition. Results from wrestlers competing out of Fleming and Haxtun are as follows:
Wilson, 21-6, mirrored Amendt's success in the 130-pound weight class, capturing the first place title with an undefeated run through the tournament. Her journey to the top was nothing short of dominant, winning every match by fall. She defeated Elina Decker, Southwest, in 0:51 in the first round, followed by quick pins of Olivia Barron-Berrelleza, Morrill, and Andrea Almanza, Wauneta-Palisade, in the second and third rounds. Wilson continued her momentum with falls over Joslyn Wyatt, Ogallala, and Aubrie Seybold, Southwest, to secure the top spot. Wilson earned 26 team points, contributing significantly to SCF's overall performance.
Autumn Volkman, 2-12, also demonstrated heart in the 120-pound class, where she earned seven team points and placed sixth. After receiving a bye in the first round, Volkman was pinned in the quarterfinal by Jadyn Lee, Sidney. She bounced back with a fall victory over Jalie Barnhill, Ogallala, in the consolation round. Unfortunately, Volkman was defeated by Alyssa Koch, Southwest, but finished strong in her final match, where she was edged out by Faith Lee, Leyton, in a 7-2 decision.
Stone, 11-12, had an impressive tournament in the 170-pound class, placing second and scoring 19 team points. After a tough opening-round loss to Saphira Whitley, Sidney, Stone came back with determination. She won her next four matches, including falls over Audrey Moorhead, South Platte, and Riley Torres, Sedgwick County/Fleming. Stone also claimed a major decision victory over Kaylee Hunter, McCook, and finished strong with another fall over Monro Stewart of Sidney. Her remarkable effort earned her a second-place finish, contributing significantly to the team's success.
Bella Allen, 2-10, faced a challenging road in the 105-pound class, where she placed sixth. Allen lost all five of her matches, each by fall, but her determination to continue fighting throughout the tournament was evident.
The girls are set to dual Wray on Thursday, Jan. 23 at 5:30 p.m. in Ovid. This will also be Parents' Night. They are then scheduled to travel to Littleton to participate in the Chatfield Warhorse Invitational on Saturday, Jan. 25 with matches beginning at 9 a.m.

title: SC/F girls dominant Wray; finish strong at Chatfield Invitational
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Sedgwick County/Fleming girls' wrestling team turned in a dominant performance against Wray, securing a 60-6 victory in a lopsided dual last Thursday. The team's deep roster and impressive…

(Courtesy photo) count
105-POUND FRESHMAN Bella Allen works for a pin against Samantha McWilliams of Broomfield in the consolation semifinals, but couldn't get the call and lost a close match, 15-12.
The Sedgwick County/Fleming girls' wrestling team turned in a dominant performance against Wray, securing a 60-6 victory in a lopsided dual last Thursday. At 105 pounds, Jamie Sharp of Wray delivered the first win for her team, pinning Bella Allen of in 1:16. Sharp's quick work on the mat gave Wray an early lead, but it would be their only victory of the day.
Olivia Stone competed at 155 pounds and continued her SC/F's dominance, pinning Kayle Stults at 2:23.
Throughout the dual, SC/F received numerous forfeits from Wray. 115-pound Autumn Volkman, 125-pound Kinsleigh Jerman, 135-pound Annie Wilson, 140-pound Kaiya Hall, all earned six points for their team via forfeit victories.
The team competed with determination and grit at the Chatfield Lady War Horse Invitational, showcasing a series of strong individual performances across multiple weight classes. While not every wrestler made it to the podium, the team displayed resilience, earning valuable experience and points along the way. T he team finished in 12th place with 46 points out of 39 teams. Individual results for wrestlers competing out of Fleming and Haxtun are as follows:
Kinsleigh Jerman (120 Gold) started her tournament with a tough loss by fall to Samantha Maestas, Alamosa, in 0:32. She quickly rebounded in the consolation rounds, winning by fall in 1:50 over Amaiah Aguilar of Central-GJ and securing a decision, 9-4, over Presley Pearson of Ponderosa. However, she was eliminated by a fall in 2:08 to Shyann Page, Central-GJ, finishing with four team points.
Annie Wilson (130 Gold) placed fourth, contributing 15 team points. She had an impressive start with two quick falls in the first and quarterfinal rounds. With several wrestlers gaining momentum in their respective weight classes, the SC/F girls' team looks poised to continue improving as they head into future tournaments. The team is scheduled to travel to Mitchell, Neb., for their final regular season tournament on Friday, Jan. 31.

title: BOE approves armed personnel policy following 83.9 percent approval
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Haxtun Board of Education officially approved policy and a resolution to allow the local school district to arm school staff. The approval of armed school personnel documents came in a Tuesday…
content:
count
The Haxtun Board of Education officially approved policy and a resolution to allow the local school district to arm school staff. The approval of armed school personnel documents came in a Tuesday evening, Jan. 21 meeting of the board of education.
Discussions regarding armed school staff began in late August when Superintendent Aron Jones provided board members with sample policy and resolutions for future consideration. He also gave board members insurance information, stating a quote for armed personnel insurance is just under $3,500 annually.
Since that time, the Board has discussed, researched and reviewed necessary information to make a sound decision on the matter. That included a survey that was sent to school staff, parents and community members regarding the topic.
In October, Jones presented findings from the survey, which showed an overall 83.9 percent approval for adopting such policy. From there, the board moved forward with proper paperwork and necessary steps to approve policy, which includes three policy readings and a final vote. That vote finally came in January with a unanimous vote of the Board minus Dean Michael, who was absent at the monthly meeting.
Now, Jones said he will reach out to staff to get a feel for who might be interested in carrying on school grounds. Those who apply will go through a vetting process and if passed, will then be recommended to the Board for approval and the training process will begin.
"We hope to use the FASTER organization to participate in the vetting and training processes," Jones said.
In addition to training staff, the District will also be responsible for necessary signage on school grounds indicating staff at the District are armed.
According to a recent article published in the Denver Gazette, more than 400 educators in 41 Colorado school districts carry guns today. The article says about 60 percent of those schools are rural districts and the other 40 percent are in suburban areas, mostly charter schools. Rural school districts have always been early adopters of armed school personnel policy, the article goes on to say, because of response time from law enforcement.
At the start of the January board meeting, members voted to approve a number of staff assignments including approving Ryann Briggs as a preschool teacher for the remainder of the 2024-25 school year; Emily Chaney as a certified substitute teacher; Kelly Price as a certified substitute teacher; and Kristi Boerner as a special education paraprofessional/long-term sub.
In his report, Jones said special education numbers have increased at Haxtun Schools since the beginning of the year due to new students arriving. The current case load, he added, is 45 students for one special education teacher.
Jones said the District will need to look into expanding the program for the coming year, but in the meantime, Boerner will assist Special Ed Teacher Jessica Hofmeister in delivering required special education minutes to students.
In other business the Board:
• Accepted a bid submitted by Terry Hadeen for bus three for $461;
• Approved a revised extra duty salary schedule to add a stipend for streaming games and increase mileage to 60 cents per mile;
• Approved a revised 2024-25 budget with minor changes. "This process is a routine conducted annually. From a financial standpoint, the District is in good standing and we are focusing on all the changes coming from the state for next year's budget," said Jones.

title: PC Board of Commissioners address various topics in recent meetings
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Phillips County Board of County Commissioners managed a large, varied amount of business matters during eight regular board meetings held Nov. 8, 2024 through Jan. 17. All three commissioners, Tom Timm, Terry Hofmeister and Garold Roberts were present at each meeting. Phillips County Clerk, Beth Zilla, and County Administrator/Planner, Andrew Nygaard, were present for each meeting with the...
content:
The Phillips County Board of County Commissioners managed a large, varied amount of business matters during eight regular board meetings held Nov. 8, 2024 through Jan. 17.
All three commissioners, Tom Timm, Terry Hofmeister and Garold Roberts were present at each meeting. Phillips County Clerk, Beth Zilla, and County Administrator/Planner, Andrew Nygaard, were present for each meeting with the exception of Zilla who was on vacation during the Dec. 31 meeting.
A separate reorganization meeting, always held at the start of the new calendar year, was held on Jan. 10. Timm was appointed to be the 2025 Chairman of the Board. The board adopted nine resolutions for county operations, recognizing holidays, making appointments of commissioners or employees or members of the public to various local and regional boards, setting salaries and wages, designating office hours, authorizing signers on behalf of the board of county commissioners, authorizing the county treasurer to deposit and invest funds, providing health and life insurance, and approving county fees and charges.
Below are the highlights of actions taken by the board from the Nov. 8 through the Jan. 17 regular meetings. Information is drawn from a combination of note-taking while present at meetings and the meeting minutes recorded by Zilla or Nygaard in Zilla's absence:
Public Hearings, Resolutions
• The Dec. 10 meeting was the only regular meeting that included public hearings and the adoption of resolutions. No one from the general public was present at either hearing to offer comments.
• A hearing was held to consider a Subdivision Exemption application by Rick Ensminger to divide a 2.97-acre parcel from a 157-acre parcel located in S5, T7N, R47W. The intent of the request was so that the parcel could be sold to an identified buyer. The request was tabled until more information could be obtained regarding the availability of water. The application was eventually approved at the Jan. 10 meeting.
• A public hearing was held pertaining to the county's 2025 budget. After the hearing was closed, the board approved Resolution 2024-12-10-01 to adopt the budget.
• The board also approved resolutions 2024-12-10-02 and 03 pertaining to appropriating amounts to various funds and spending agencies, and levying general property taxes, respectively.
• It also approved the Board of County Commissioners' 2025 meeting schedule.
Executive Sessions
• Two Executive Sessions were held on Dec. 31. Each one pertained to a personnel matter; one regarding the Sheriff's Office and the other Road and Bridge.
Appointments with
elected officials
• Phillips County Treasurer, Steve Young, provided the Board with an update on the Tax Lean Sale.
• County Assessor, Doug Kamery, discussed the need to recertify the levies and revenue to tax year 2024. Adjustments had been made by Sedgwick County regarding its portion of the Holyoke School District. The board authorized the chair to sign the recertification.
• Sheriff Michael Beard brought forward an unpaid 2023 invoice from Axon Enterprises that he was requesting to have paid from 2024 funds. He wasn't aware of it until recently because it had been sent to the previous sheriff's e-mail address. Beard assured the board that the goods and services received from Axon Enterprises were worth every penny. They supply things like tasers, charging blocks, body cameras and video storage for law enforcement agencies nationwide. The board approved paying the invoice for $9,072.
Appointments with
county-related staff
• Road and Bridge Manager, Kevin Scott, met with the board four times. One was for updates in general. Another was to update the board about the county's in-kind services for the construction of the Holyoke Community Childcare Center that included the delivery of loads of dirt and use of roll-off dumpsters. The third regarded repair bills from a Dec. 13 accident involving a road grader.
• Scott's fourth meeting included District 3 Road and Bridge Supervisor, Dave Salyards, to discuss tractor rentals. The Board approved Scott's request to rent three John Deer tractors from 21st Century Equipment for an estimated 350 hours at $15/hour for a total estimate of $15,750.
• The county Victims Advocate, Kelley Sullivan, discussed the Victims Assistance Law Enforcement grant and the Victims of Crime Act grant. Both have been awarded less funds than the previous year. The Board authorized the chair to sign the VALE grant at the Nov. 27 meeting. The VOCA grant was signed at the Dec. 31 meeting.
• Colorado State University Extension Agent Jessie Salyards provided updates on the 4-H program and other activity.
• County Emergency Manager, Broc Pelle, provided updates on the Emergency Management Planning Grant. The board approved the signing of various administrative forms associated with the receipt and management of the grant funds. It approved the contract between the board of commissioners, State of Colorado, and Broc Pelle as the County Emergency Manager. It also approved Pelle's job description.
• County Veterans Services Officer, Chris Kelley, along with Glen Marciniak from the Colorado Division of Veterans Affairs, discussed training, reports and other administrative types of support provided by the county.
Appointments with
the general public
• The board did not approve a request from Andrea Calhoon, Haxtun Conservation District, for the same discounted Event Center rental rate as a 501c3 nonprofit organization.
• The board approved the request from Jesse Ruiz, Jr., representing the Bridge Foundation, to serve alcohol at their dance to be held at the Event Center.
• Summer Kreider, the Holyoke Junior/Senior High School Counselor, and School District Superintendent Kyle Stumpf, provided information about placing student interns at local businesses.
• The board approved a request from Loren Hendrix to have a memorial bench placed inside the Bank of Colorado Pavilion.
• The board approved a request from Kendra Schlacter, Holyoke City Recreation Director, to allow alcohol at the Showdown on the Plains event.
• The board approved a request by Nici Akey, representing the Phillips County Economic Development Corporation, to waive the Event Center rental fees, as has been done in the past, for its Youth E-Fair event. Akey also provided updates about the status of filling the vacancy in its director's position and a vacancy in one of the commissioners' appointed director positions on the PCED board.
Purchases
• The board approved the following four purchases:
- for the Road and Bridge Department, two CTS bottom-dump trailers from Crossroad Trailer Sales & Service for $88,800 using American Recovery Plan Act funds; and,
- a truckload of cutting edges for road graders for $33,767, with the cost split between the remaining ARPA funds and the rest from the Road and Bridge fund;
- for the landfill, a Chevrolet Silverado 2500 pickup from Wolf Auto for $32,266; and,
- for the Sheriff's office, the installation by Platinum Technology of a controlled access door for an estimated $7,682.
Personnel and contractors
• The board approved the proposal from Kelley Law to provide legal services for Phillips County in 2025.
• The board created some parameters for the new Veterans Service Officer, Chris Kelley, to include providing quarterly reports and being personally available at his office on the second floor of the courthouse.
• The board approved the promotion of Walter Juarez to Supervisor of Road and Bridge District 1, and the associated wage increase.
• Grade and step increases on the county's pay scale were approved for eight employees as requested by department managers in road and bridge, maintenance, administration and also the sheriff's, assessor's and clerk's offices.
• Following a short meeting recess to discuss time off on Christmas Eve with the county's Personnel Board, the board approved observing the 2024 Christmas Eve paid holiday for the full workday instead of a half-day, to be reconsidered in 2025.
Board appointments
• Wyatt McCallum was appointed to the Phillips County Fair Board.
• The board reappointed the following individuals for additional terms of service: Jeanette Kingman and Matt Kleve to the Board of Adjustment; Jeanette Kingman and Gary Koch to the Planning Commission; Martin Olofson and Charley Triplette to the Weed and Pest Advisory Board; Tom Edwards to the West Phillips County Cemetery Board, and Jim Tomky to the Recreation District Board.
• Commissioner Tom Timm was appointed to be the representative to the County Health Pool with Andrew Nygaard as the alternate.
Contracts and agreements
• The board approved a roadway occupancy agreement with PC Telcom for underground construction of a fiber optic line along county road 47 between county roads 20 and 22.
• It also authorized the chairman to sign:
- a Division of Motor Vehicles Driver Services Portal letter, as presented;
- the contract amendment with the Colorado Department of Health Care Policy and Financing, as presented; and
- the Managed Service Agreement with Dominion Voting Systems, Inc., extending it through Dec. 31, 2030.
Miscellaneous
• The board approved the following actions:
- request from the 4-H Horse Club to waive the Sunday night BOC Pavilion fee from May - October 2025;
- a letter to be sent to collections in regard to non-payment of a landfill customer's bills;
- payment of the Colorado Counties Inc. annual dues of $12,000 for 2025;
- payment of the Colorado Counties Public Lands annual dues of $150 for 2025;
- the application for the July – December 2024 payment from the Colorado Division of Veteran Affairs that supports the county Veterans Services Officer; and
- acceptance of the annual CDOT Highway User Tax Fund report as presented.
Meeting minutes are available upon request from the county administration office, and at the county's website at: https://phillipscounty.colorado.gov/departments/county-commissioners.

title: Lady Bulldogs pull off 3rd win over the Lady Dragons this season
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Lady Bulldogs have proven that any time, any place, they can take on the Holyoke Dragons and come out with a win. The two teams met at the beginning of the season in Sterling, two weeks ago in…
content:
(Herald photo by Candie Fix) count
FRESHMAN Leah Edwards, #22, comes up with the ball near the baseline in Haxtun's home match up with Merino on Jan. 24.
The Lady Bulldogs have proven that any time, any place, they can take on the Holyoke Dragons and come out with a win. The two teams met at the beginning of the season in Sterling, two weeks ago in Haxtun and just last Friday in Holyoke and every time, it's the Lady Bulldogs who come out on top.
The most recent meeting of the two Phillips County teams took place at the home of the Dragons on Friday night LPAA basketball action. Despite a six point deficit after the first quarter, Haxtun racked up 12 points while holding Holyoke to four in the second quarter for a 19-17 lead at half time.
The Lady Bulldogs amped up the offense, putting 15 points on the board in the third quarter and an additional 12 in the fourth for a final 46-35 league win.
"Beating a team three times in a season is a really hard thing to do. We knew Holyoke would come with a different game plan for this matchup. They double-teamed Bobbi (Starkebaum) from the start which left one of our girls wide open," said Head Coach Alicia Schram. "We had some missed point opportunities due to some unforced turnovers during the first quarter. Things would've looked quite different if we had capitalized on those opportunities from the start of the game. Definitely something we need to work on."
The latest win puts the Lady Bulldogs at 7-8 on the season and 1-2 in league standings.
Three Lady Bulldogs hit double-digit figures in the scoring department led by senior Kelsie Hadeen with 12 points. She connected with five field goals and made two free throws to lead her team. Senior Jayleigh Bullard also hit five field goals and an additional free throw to rack up 11. Freshman Leah Edwards contributed 10 points off four field goals and two shots from the charity stripe.
Bullard led in rebounds with a total of eight. She nabbed five on defense and three on offense. Hadeen and senior Bobbi Starkebaum each pulled down six rebounds and Edwards tallied five.
Senior Emily Anderson registered seven steals and three assists. Hadeen totaled three steals while Bullard, Edwards and Emma Lemesany each tallied one. Bullard and Lilly Lemesany added two assists followed by Edwards and Hadeen, both with a single assist.
"Defensively, I was extremely happy with how aggressive we were. I was also pleased with the growth of our free-throw percentage. We have come such a long way. We were also able to put together a solid fourth quarter. That is something that we've needed to do. Now we can build from that," said Schram. "The stat that sticks out to me the most is that we had 30 deflections. That's a huge defensive effort for our team - it is by far a season high for our team. That goes to show just how much more aggressive we have become as a unit."
This week the schedule pits the Lady Bulldogs in a match up with Akron on Thursday and Brush on Friday. According to MaxPreps, the Lady Rams are 8-6 overall and 1-1 in league play. The Lady Beetdiggers hold an overall 11-4 record and are fifth at 4-2 in the 3A Patriot league.
"The rest of the season is going to be a fun challenge. Each game brings an amazing opportunity for our girls. As it stands right now, every single opponent we face for the rest of the year is a highly ranked team in either 1A, 2A or 3a (besides two possible games at the end of the season tourney). Each game is going to be a challenge, but we have to keep in mind that just playing those teams will help us in RPI. I truly believe that if the girls can put together solid games from here on out, we are right in all of those games. It's been fun to see them go from a 2-18 team to one full of confidence," Schram said.

title: Starkebaum commits to MCC
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Bobbi Starkebaum committed to McCook Community College to further her volleyball career on Wednesday, Feb. 9. The day is also marked as National Girls and Women in Sports Day. Starkebaum is a senior…
content:
(Herald photo by Candie Fix) count
HAXTUN SENIOR Bobbi Starkebaum signed a letter of intent to further her volleyball career at McCook Community College next year in front of family, friends, teammates and supporters on Wednesday, Feb. 5. Seated in front are (l-r), Barron, Bobbi, Sammi and Brian Starkebaum; back row (l-r), Haxtun High School volleyball coaches Marissa Chapdelaine, Don Schelling and Emma Heinz.
Bobbi Starkebaum committed to McCook Community College to further her volleyball career on Wednesday, Feb. 9. The day is also marked as National Girls and Women in Sports Day. Starkebaum is a senior at Haxtun High School and sealed her commitment to volleyball at the colligate level in front of friends, family, teammates and supporters last week.
"Bobbi has the work ethic to be better than what she already is. When you bring that as an individual, it will also bring that to the team," said McCook Head Volleyball Coach Hayley Kobza.
Starkebaum, who was named All-Conference and All-State, Second Team in her senior season, was a captain for the Lady Bulldogs and a starter on the team that finished top six in the 2A Classification at the Colorado State Tournament in November.
Starkebaum was also honored as a 2A player in the Colorado Coaches of Girls Sports All-State games at the conclusion of her high school career.
Throughout her time on the court as a Lady Bulldog, Starkebaum registered 837 kills at the net along with 274 total blocks, 171 of those solo. She also boasts a 91.6 serving percentage including 57 aces. As a setter, she racked up 703 assists.
Kobza said it was Starkebaum's height that first peaked her interest in the Haxtun senior but after that, it was her love for volleyball. "Her size, work ethic and dedication to the sport," she added.
At this time, Starkebaum remains undecided about her field of study while playing volleyball at the next level.
Starkebaum will reunite with former high school teammate Megan Walker, who just completed her first season as a setter for the McCook Lady Indians. The 2024 Lady Indians finished with a 21-13 record and a Region IX Tournament berth.
"As of right now, we will start her in the middle," Kobza said of Starkebaum's intended position on the team.

title: Wernsman & Walker appointed to two-year terms on the Fleming Town Council
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Fleming Town Council held their regular monthly meeting on Wednesday, Feb. 12. The meeting was called to order by Mayor Stefan Betley at 6:30 p.m. The following council members were present: Bill…
content:
count
The Fleming Town Council held their regular monthly meeting on Wednesday, Feb. 12. The meeting was called to order by Mayor Stefan Betley at 6:30 p.m. The following council members were present: Bill Langridge, Kamie Lambrecht and Bonnie Jackson. Milinda Hickey was absent. Also present were Josh Wernsman, Scott Walker, Joelle Gapter, Lewis Frank and Michelle Asfeld.
Additions/Corrections to the Agenda: Betley suggested amending the agenda due to the cold weather so that everyone could get home as soon as possible. He asked that the following be agenda items be tabled: maintenance, superintendent and clerk reports and discussion items: cost estimates for equipment building, RAISE grant and foot stones at the cemetery. It was moved and seconded to approve the amended agenda. The motion passed unanimously.
Public Comment: no public comment.
Consent Agenda: A motion was made and seconded to approve the consent agenda consisting of the January minutes and bills. The motion passed unanimously.
Oath of Office: Betley announced that there are two vacant council positions after Andrew Muller's resignation letter was read towards the end of the January meeting. He asked if there were individuals present who would be interested in filling said positions. Both Walker and Wernsman indicated their interest. Both shared a brief background of themselves and of their interest in serving on the Council.
It was moved and seconded to seat Wernsman on the Council for a two-year term. The motion passed unanimously.
It was moved and seconded to seat Walker on the Council for a two-year term. The motion passed unanimously.
Asfeld proceeded to administer the Oath of Office to the two new council members. Wernsman and Walker then joined the other council members at the table.
Treasurer's Report: Frank reviewed the financial reports that had previously been provided to the Council. It was moved and seconded to approve the Treasurer's Report. The motion passed unanimously.
Action Items:
• The Council reviewed Resolution #1-2025, Setting Day, Time and Posting Places of the Agenda. It states that regular meetings shall be held on the second Wednesday of each month, starting at 6:30 p.m. The official posting places for public meetings and hearings shall be the Fleming Town Hall, Fleming Post Office and on the Fleming website (flemingcolorado.us). It was moved and seconded to approve the resolution. The motion passed unanimously.
• The Council reviewed Proclamation #2-2025-America 250-Colorado 150 Proclamation. The proclamation engages the Town of Fleming in the commemorative activities leading up to and during the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence and Colorado's 150th anniversary. title: Wildcats add two wins; settle at 3rd in NC League
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Fleming Wildcats added two victories over the past week putting them on a four-game winning streak. They hosted Briggsdale on Friday night for the final league contest of the season and traveled to Lone Star on Saturday where they took a narrow, five-point win over the Longhorns. Friday night's match up saw Briggsdale on top by four after the opening quarter, 16-12. Fleming's...
content:
The Fleming Wildcats added two victories over the past week putting them on a four-game winning streak. They hosted Briggsdale on Friday night for the final league contest of the season and traveled to Lone Star on Saturday where they took a narrow, five-point win over the Longhorns.
Friday night's match up saw Briggsdale on top by four after the opening quarter, 16-12. Fleming's offense answered back with a 20-point second quarter while the defense held the Falcons to 14 points. Fleming held a two-point, 32-30, lead at halftime.
Fleming came out to dominate the third quarter, going up by another 10 points, and out scored the Falcons by four in the final quarter. The Wildcats remained on top at the final horn, 71-55.
Freshman Dylon Monroe led the Wildcats on the scoreboard with 22 points. He made 10 two-point shots and earned the remaining two on free throws.
Senior Travis Johnson followed with 19 points. In addition, he led the team in rebounds with 11 giving him a double-double for the night.
Sophomore Treyson Kirkwood also hit double digits on the scoreboard for the home team. He tallied 10 points which included six off three-points shots.
Saturday's game against the Longhorns started off slow for both offenses with Fleming owning a five-point lead at halftime, 16-11. The Wildcats out scored the Longhorns by one in the third, 14-13, and the Longhorns returned the favor in the fourth, 19-18, leaving Fleming on top by five at the final horn, 48-43.
Monroe led his team once again in scoring with 20 points for the night. Johnson followed with 13. He brought down 17 rebounds giving him another double-double.
The Wildcats are set to travel to Idalia on Friday, Feb. 21. Junior varsity boys are set to take the court at 4 p.m.
A season finale tournament between the North Central League and the YWKC is scheduled for next week beginning on Tuesday. Brackets for the tournament had not been determined as of press time.

title: Annual banquets deemed a success
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: A Caring Pregnancy Resource Center of Northeast Colorado is celebrating a successful banquet weekend raising more than $125,000 with over 1,100 people attending at their four locations - Brush,…
content:
(Courtesy photo) count
A CARING Pregnancy Resource Center of Northeast Colorado Board at the Brush 2025 Banquet, (l-r), Paula Crook, Teresa Munday, Pastor Paul Speicher, Roberta Bigalk, Barry Richardson, Debbie Eurich, Andrew Smith and Clint Johnson.
A Caring Pregnancy Resource Center of Northeast Colorado is celebrating a successful banquet weekend raising more than $125,000 with over 1,100 people attending at their four locations - Brush, Sterling, Yuma and Holyoke. All the banquets were nearly sold out, with the Yuma banquet being completely sold out. Two venues were moved this year: Sterling to the Northeastern Junior College Banquet hall and Yuma to Red Willow on Main, which allowed an increase of overall attendance.
A Caring Pregnancy Resource Center is almost entirely funded by individual community members and churches across the six counties it serves. All of their services are free to the public.
"Giving was down but I attribute that to the state of our economy. As a ministry we trust the Lord to provide for our needs as we serve those who so desperately need us, said Director Roberta Bigalk. "Our mission is to provide accurate information regarding the choices our clients must make, resources for during and after pregnancy and the support our parents need to choose life. We desire to walk with individuals through the first year of their babies lives. That gives us time to link them with community resources and ensure success in parenting.
When a woman finds herself pregnant, she only has three choices: parent her child, choose parents for her child or have an abortion."
"When she comes to us, she either thinks she is pregnant or has a baby in her arms. We provide information in the way of free pregnancy testing to ensure a woman is indeed pregnant, ultrasounds to determine the gestational age of the baby and the viability of the pregnancy. We also have giving closets that give parents everything from diapers and formula to car seats, pack n plays and clothing through size 2T and lastly, we can provide resources/referrals to assist women in choosing a parent for their child. We know if we can talk with them and do an ultrasound, we have a 90 percent chance of saving the babies life because all of this information assists the women in choosing life," Bigalk added.
This year's guest speaker was Tori Shaw, a woman who had an abortion as a teen. Shaw created Not Forgotten Ministries, a ministry to assist women who've had abortion find healing and restoration. A new anonymous confidential support program will be launched Feb. 27 via zoom link to support women who've experienced abortion. The link can be found on their website at http://www.acaringpregnancy.org under the abortion tab.
"We are thankful for the generosity of the communities, businesses and churches throughout northeast Colorado that allow us to do what we do. We are also thankful for the 112 volunteers that make the magic happen. If you're interested in volunteering, donating or in need of our services you can call (970) 842-4324 or visit http://www.acaringpregnancy.org.
"We're looking forward to a great year in 2025 serving those individuals and families in need throughout the northeast plains," said Bigalk.

title: Biesemeier reports on recent provider changes
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
