(Herald photo by Candie Fix) count
LMD SERVICES key players Dante Owens, Montrey Brown-Posey, Virginia Bahnsen and Lamar Wilbern in the Haxtun office located just off main street at 119 East Fletcher Avenue. Bahnsen serves as Chief of Administration, Western Division, overseeing the Haxtun office.
LMD Services, LLC has expanded into northeast Colorado, establishing an office in downtown Haxtun. The Nebraska-based company provides services and support for the developmental disabilities community. Virginia Bahnsen, who lives in Paoli, serves as the Western Division Chief of Administration, heading up the local Haxtun office.
With a mission to lead, motivate and develop skills for community integration, habilitation and vocational participation, LMD Services provides opportunities for individuals with mental health and developmental disabilities to experience, learn and participate in their communities, homes and vocations.
LMD Services first opened in Lincoln, Neb. four years ago under the direction of Dante Owens, Lamar Wilbern and Montrey Brown-Posey, all who bring with them years of experience in caring for individuals with disabilities.
Most recently, Bahnsen saw a need for such services in northeast Colorado and through connections, reached out to bring LMD Services to the area.
"It's our goal to give these individuals a better lifestyle," said Brown-Posey. "We make sure everyone is seen, heard and enjoys their life. And we're here to help society see that, too."
LMD Services specializes in the areas of residential support, supported employment and day support.
"We work with those who have developmental disabilities to put the staff and systems in place so that they can have the highest sense of normalcy," said Owens. He noted LMD Services does not limit to any disabilities and commonly assists those with fetal alcohol syndrome, autism, traumatic brain injuries and cerebral palsy.
"No two individuals are the same," Owens added. "We are here to help based on their level of need."
LMD Services and its staff allows family to be just that, providing support so that parents, guardians and caregivers have the ability to slip back into their roles as moms, dads, siblings or grandparents.
"We want to make sure families don't burn out, because burnout is something we see quite often," Bahnsen said.
Mentoring and day services are also available through LMD Services.
The local LMD Services office is located at 119 East Fletcher Street, Suite 3M and is fully staffed Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Bahnsen can also be reached by calling (402) 450-3640.
"This really is our passion and we hope we get the opportunity to collaborate with and enrich the community," Brown-Posey said.
For more information, visit lmdsne.com or find them on Facebook at LMD Services, LLC.

title: Excitement builds for Feb. 18 Girls' Night Out event in Haxtun
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Haxtun Health is excited to host an inspiring Girls' Night Out event on Feb. 18 from 5:30-8 p.m. at the Haxtun Community Center. This free event, focused on women's health and well-being, aims to…
content:
count
Haxtun Health is excited to host an inspiring Girls' Night Out event on Feb. 18 from 5:30-8 p.m. at the Haxtun Community Center. This free event, focused on women's health and well-being, aims to strengthen attendees' connection to their personal health.
This year's event will cover a range of important topics, including gut health, heart disease, preventative screenings, pain management, pelvic floor exercises and more.
Attendees can look forward to a delicious dinner and refreshing, on-theme mocktails provided by Saved by the Well, a company based in Ogallala, Neb. This unique establishment is known for its high-quality, feel-good drinks that are both delicious and health-conscious.
The event also features the Women's Wellness Award, recognizing a woman who has made significant contributions to the mental, spiritual or physical health and well-being of women in the community. Nominations for this award are open until Feb. 8 and can be submitted at bit.ly/4a6EPoC.
Haxtun Health's Girls' Night Out event is more than just an evening of learning; it's a celebration of women's health and a chance to foster a supportive community. The topics covered are crucial for every woman and the insights provided by esteemed speakers will be invaluable. One of Haxtun Health's Specialty providers, a general surgeon, Dr. Megan McKenna, joins the night's guest speakers to educate on gut health and will delve into how our digestive system impacts our overall health. She will also be addressing how her Ageless Aesthetics salon in Wray is helping women feel their best through services like Botox, which not only enhances appearance but also offers health benefits such as headache treatment.
Dr. Lila Statz's will walk through her breast cancer journey is expected to be both moving and enlightening. Her dual perspective as a patient and a provider will provide attendees with a comprehensive understanding of the challenges and triumphs associated with breast cancer.
Wendy Evans, MSPT will provide a brief overview of the pelvic floor's anatomy and its crucial role it plays in women's health. She will also guide attendees through a series of practical exercises designed to strengthen the pelvic floor muscles, which can help with issues such as incontinence, pelvic pain and sexual health.
Haxtun Health is thrilled to announce that Lauren Gerk, CRNA will join the speaker lineup to discuss the topic of pain management, adding another layer of valuable insight to the evening.
The evening will also include a segment on general preventative care and screenings, led by Reba Bean, a physician associate. This session will emphasize the importance of regular health check-ups and early detection in maintaining long-term health.
Additionally, the event will feature a group of panelists answering women's health-based questions for the audience. You can submit your questions here: bit.ly/4hfgNdh.
Organizers are incredibly excited about this event and believe it will be a significant benefit to the women of Haxtun and the surrounding area. Please plan to attend for an evening of learning, connection and celebration. Remember to RSVP at bit.ly/3DEbGVB to secure your spot.

title: Annual banquets to be held
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: A Caring Pregnancy Resource Center of Northeast Colorado is hosting annual banquets across northeast Colorado later this month. The organization is a non-profit providing no cost and confidential…
content:
A Caring Pregnancy Resource Center of Northeast Colorado is hosting annual banquets across northeast Colorado later this month. The organization is a non-profit providing no cost and confidential pregnancy confirmation, ultrasounds, giving closets, support services and resource referral.
This year's banquet theme 'Light Their Path' features speaker Tori Shaw, a woman who discovered she was pregnant at 16. In a rushed attempt to hide the pregnancy, Shaw had an abortion less than 24 hours after finding out the news. She left the abortion clinic completely different than when she entered and her life quickly spiraled downhill.
It took Shaw 17 years to come out of hiding and share her secret with others. Since doing so, she has created Not Forgotten Ministries providing support for individuals who've experienced abortion. Shaw now walks in complete freedom following her abortion and desires the same for others who have walked a similar journey.
'It's time we reach out to those affected by abortion. When a woman finds she's pregnant, she has only one of three choices. Carry to term and parent, choose parents for her child or have an abortion. Women facing an unplanned pregnancy need our support!' said Roberta Bigalk, Executive Director of A Caring Pregnancy Resource Center of Northeast Colorado. 'In addition to the services we regularly provide, we're launching a new after-abortion care support program that is online and anonymous. Each of our online leaders have had abortions themselves and understand the ramifications of that decision. Having served well over 300 women this past year shows us how valuable our organization is to the communities we serve in Northeastern Colorado. We'd like to double that number!'
A Caring Pregnancy Resource Center is a 501 (c)3 non-profit with five locations in Yuma, Wray, Sterling, Holyoke and Brush providing no cost and confidential pregnancy confirmation, ultrasounds, giving closets, support services and resource referral throughout Northeast Colorado.
Banquets are from 6 to 8:30 p.m. on four consecutive evenings with four locations to choose from including Friday, Jan. 24, Northeaster Junior College Ballroom in Sterling; Saturday, Jan. 25, Phillips County Event Center in Holyoke; Sunday, Jan. 26, Red Willow Event Center in Yuma; and Monday, Jan. 27, Morgan County Event Center in Brush.
All resources from the evening go directly to helping mothers, fathers, students, babies and families in Northeast Colorado. For more information about services or to reserve seating, call the Pregnancy Center at (970) 842-4324 or visit our website: neco-cpc.org/tickets.

title: Bulldogs break 3-game losing streak with one-point home victory
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Bulldogs ended a three-game losing streak with a one-point win over Merino at home on Friday night. Haxtun hosted two games on the home court last weekend, first facing Merino and then Burlington.…
content:
(Herald photo by Candie Fix) count
HAXTUN SENIOR #11 Ryland Wolff comes down with a rebound in first half action against the Merino Rams at home on Friday. Haxtun held on for a 56-55 win over the Rams.
The Bulldogs ended a three-game losing streak with a one-point win over Merino at home on Friday night. Haxtun hosted two games on the home court last weekend, first facing Merino and then Burlington. Just six games remain on the regular season schedule and right now, the Bulldogs hold a 6-8 overall record.
Friday's match up with Merino marked the first league contest for the Bulldogs, giving the team a 1-0 start in the 3A/2A Lower Platte. As of mid-week, Haxtun, Akron and Sedgwick County all hold a 1-0 record while Merino and Holyoke stand 0-1, according to MaxPreps.
Haxtun held an early advantage against the Rams and carried a lead clear into the fourth courter, but Merino fought back from the three-point line, making things interesting. In the end, Haxtun pulled out a 56-55 win for their first, and much needed, league win. The victory over Merino is just the second for the Bulldogs in their last eight games.
"I felt the boys executed our game plan well against Merino. We were able to build a solid lead in the fourth quarter but unfortunately we had some missteps that allowed them to get hot from three," said Jayden Stieb, Bulldog Head Coach. "The boys did a great job of keeping focus, even though at times it felt like we couldn't stop their shots from going in the basket."
Junior Chase Goddard racked up 19 points against the Rams to lead the team on the scoreboard. Sophomore Madden Larsen also hit double-digits, registering 13 points. Senior Ryland Wolff added nine, junior Colin Cone scored seven, junior Jaxsen Schram put up five and junior Kanin Koberstein added three.
Saturday's match up pitted the Bulldogs in a contest with the Burlington Cougars. The Cougars remain a Colorado 2A team despite having enrollment numbers in the 3A classification bracket.
Haxtun fell behind by double-digit figures early in the first but the Bulldogs continued to battle back to keep the game tight down the stretch. Key shots and free throws late in the game gave the Cougars a four-point win, 52-48.
"I felt like we came out very slow against Burlington. We were able to fight back into the game, but dug ourselves too big of hole. Our intensity needs to be high right out of the gate or we will allow teams to take early leads," Stieb said.
Three Bulldogs led under the basket with Wolff and Larsen combining for 28. The two each registered 14 points against the Cougars. Goddard scored 11 followed by Cone with five, Schram with three and Koberstein with one.
"My biggest take aways from the weekend were our ability to take care of the ball and lack of rebounding. I felt both nights we did a much better job of taking care of the basketball and limiting unforced turnovers. That's something we've spent a lot of time talking about, so it was encouraging to see it translate to games" said Stieb. "We struggled both nights tracking down lose balls on the rebound. It felt like we were only getting 30 percent of 50/50 balls. That's something we've been pretty good about all year, so we need to get back to getting in good position and selling out when the ball is lose."
This week the Bulldogs head to Holyoke for their second contest with the Dragons in just 13 days. The two teams met in Haxtun on Jan. 18; that contest went to the Dragons by a four-point margin.
On February 6th and 7th, Haxtun is set to travel to Akron to take on the Rams and then to Brush for a match up with the Beetdiggers. After that games with Idalia, Caliche and Sedgwick County remain on the schedule before post-season play begins.

title: Wagoner qualifies for Westminster Dog Show
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Kaylee Wagoner has again qualified for the Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show in New York City. This is her second qualification to the prestigious show. Wagoner shows a Cairn Terrier and is one of 10…
content:
Kaylee Wagoner has again qualified for the Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show in New York City. This is her second qualification to the prestigious show.
Wagoner shows a Cairn Terrier and is one of 10 talented kids from Colorado to qualify with the seven necessary "Best Junior" wins at an AKC Dog Show. Wagoner and her dog Brinkley were nationally ranked seventh in Terrier Group Junior Showmanship in 2024. The young showman travels all over the country competing.
The Westminster Dog Show is Feb. 10-11. Wagoner is daughter of Tony and Miranda Wagoner, Greeley, and granddaughter of Jerold and Stacy Wagoner, Paoli.

title: Wildcats take win over Genoa-Hugo
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Fleming Wildcats found their first victory of the season after a three-game week last week. The Wildcats fell to Akron and Peetz before taking a home victory over Genoa-Hugo in a make up contest.…
content:
(Herald photo by Spring Atchison) count
DYLON MONROE looks for an open shot against Otis.
The Fleming Wildcats found their first victory of the season after a three-game week last week. The Wildcats fell to Akron and Peetz before taking a home victory over Genoa-Hugo in a make up contest. The Wildcats now stand at 1-11 on the season.
The week's play opened on last Tuesday, Jan. 21 at home against Akron. The Rams took a 67-44 victory in that contest.
Senior Derek Houser led the Wildcats in scoring for the night with 10 points. He made good on three two-point shots, one free throw and sunk one of one attempt from behind the three-point arc. Junior Wyatt Sonnenberg and senior Travis Johnson added eight points apiece.
Johnson hit double digits in rebounds with 13 total. He brought down two offensive and 11 defensive to earn the team high. He also led in teals and blocks after taking three turnovers and five denied shots.
The Wildcats went on the road to Peetz on Friday, Jan. 24, where the Bulldogs jumped to an early 13-point lead after the first, 21-8, and went on to expand that advantage by another 12 before the half, 41-16.
Scoring in the second half looked a little more even with Fleming adding a total of 20 and Peetz adding 27. The Bulldogs maintained the lead for the 68-36 league victory.
Junior Jared Betley led on the scoreboard for the night with eight points. He shot 80 percent from the field sinking four of five two-point buckets. Johnson followed with six points off a pair of two-pointers and a pair of freethrows.
Johnson led his team in rebounds with seven. He brought down three offensive and four defensive boards. Sophomore Conner Marchant followed with six. His were split at two and four, respectively.
Freshman Jaron Monroe led the squad in assists and steals.
The Wildcats are scheduled for another three-game week. They'll play on their home court for all three games beginning with Stratton on Thursday, Jan. 30. The schedule lists a 4 p.m. tip off time on that day.
On Saturday, Feb. 1, Fleming is set to host Union Colony Prep with games beginning at 1 p.m.
Tuesday, Feb. 4, closes out the week's play when the Merino Rams come to town. A 4 p.m. start is listed for that day.

title: Lady Bulldogs drop to 6-8; head into final six games
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Lady Bulldogs dropped two games at home over the weekend, falling to 6-8 in the record category. Despite the losses, the team continues to battle, learn and grow, which will hopefully benefit the…
content:
(Herald photo by Candie Fix) count
SENIOR EMMA PAYNE, Haxtun Lady Bulldog #52, puts up a shot good for two points in the Lady Bulldogs home contest with Merino last week.
The Lady Bulldogs dropped two games at home over the weekend, falling to 6-8 in the record category. Despite the losses, the team continues to battle, learn and grow, which will hopefully benefit the girls in the final six games remaining on the regular season schedule.
Haxtun faced an undeniably top ranked team in all of Colorado basketball when the Lady Bulldogs took on Merino at home on Friday. The Lady Bulldogs fell, 63-20 to a fast, dominating Lady Rams team.
"The girls never gave up or gave in. They maintained their positive attitude and determination on the court. That was important for our team. Merino also gave us a really good indication of the things that we need to work on to finish out the rest of the season," said Lady Bulldogs Coach, Alicia Schram. "We knew that Merino was going to be the toughest opponent that we would see, so our game plan was to work through things offensively and defensively to help us prepare for the rest of the league games that we will see this season. I think we handled their press pretty well, but ended up having a lot of unforced errors that led to turnovers. That's something that we will continue to work on."
Freshman Leah Edwards led the Lady Bulldogs on the scoreboard with six points against Merino. She connected with three of seven field goals for her six. Unfortunately, in the final minutes of the contest, Edwards suffered an ankle injury that took her out of play the following day.
Senior Bobbi Starkebaum made two shots from inside the paint for four points followed by Kinsley Koberstein and Lilly Lemesany, each with three points.
Senior Jayleigh Bullard pulled down six rebounds, three on offense and three on defense. Starkebaum nabbed five rebounds, Lemesany and senior Kelsie Hadeen each brought down three and junior Reagan Jones and senior Emma Payne both tallied two.
Lemesany and Payne each totaled two assists and also led in steals, along with Edwards and Bullard, all of who registered a single takeaway.
Saturday's contest with the Burlington Lady Cougars was close throughout the first half but despite keeping up with the visiting team for the first 16 minutes of play, Haxtun fell 65-43. The Cougars are classified as a 2A team in Colorado basketball, despite having much higher enrollment numbers that should put them in the 3A classification.
"We wanted to use the intensity of the Merino game to help motivate us for Burlington and ultimately the rest of the season," said Schram. "We had a couple of injuries this week that left us a little shorthanded. We kept up with Burlington pretty well until half, but definitely missed the motor and court sense that Leah brings to the game."
Starkebaum put up a commanding 20 points for the Lady Bulldogs against Burlington. She made nine field goals and connected with two free throws. Senior Emily Anderson racked up 11 points, Lemesany added six and Bullard contributed four points.
Under the basket, Starkebaum brought down four offensive rebounds and nine defensive for a total of 13. Lemesany pulled down eight rebounds, Bullard registered five and Jones nabbed four.
Andersen added four assists in the contest and also lead in steals, along with Lemesany, each totaling three.
This week the Lady Bulldogs will step onto the court at the home of the Lady Dragons in Holyoke on Friday. The contest marks the third for the two teams; the first two going in favor of the Lady Bulldogs. The upcoming game will mark the 3A/2A League contest for the two teams.
The following week Haxtun is set to see Akron and Brush on the road before rounding out the regular season with games against Idalia, Caliche and Sedgwick County at home.
"Hopefully we get everyone healthy this week and be ready to get back to it," Schram said.

title: Wildcats host Stratton, Merino and UCP
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Fleming Wildcats played host for three contests over the past week. They opened with Stratton on Thursday, played Union Colony Prep on Saturday and closed with a Tuesday contest against Merino. Despite some season-high numbers from key players, the Wildcats fell in all three outings. The Wildcats kept pace with Stratton for the first half on Thursday. content:
The Fleming Wildcats played host for three contests over the past week. They opened with Stratton on Thursday, played Union Colony Prep on Saturday and closed with a Tuesday contest against Merino. Despite some season-high numbers from key players, the Wildcats fell in all three outings.
The Wildcats kept pace with Stratton for the first half on Thursday. They trailed by just seven at halftime. Stratton would go on to take a 56-40 win.
Freshman Jaron Monroe put over half of Fleming's tally on the scoreboard. He earned 22 of the team's points after shooting four-for-four outside the three-point arc. He shot 62 percent for the remaining 10 points on two-pointers.
Sophomore Treyson Kirkwood led the squad in rebounds with seven; all of those defensive boards. Jaron Monroe and senior Travis Johnson followed with six rebounds apiece.
Saturday night's game against Union Colony Prep found Fleming down by 15 after the opening half. They would go on to fall to the Timberwolves 62-40.
In this outing, Dylon Monroe, twin brother to Jaron, led on the scoreboard. He tallied 10 points on a pair of free throw and four two-point field goals.
Johnson came up big underneath with 16 rebounds. He brought down 10 defensive and six offensive boards. He also blocked five shots.
On Tuesday night, the Wildcats fell in a close contest to the Merino Rams. The final score put the Rams on top 49-39. Official stats were not available by press time on Wednesday.
The Wildcats are scheduled for back-to-back Friday/Saturday action this week. They're set to hit the road to Weldona on Friday, Feb. 7 for their third league match up of the season. The Warriors hold the number two spot in the North Central League at 1-0. Junior varsity boys open against the Warriors at 4:30 p.m. that night.
On Saturday they return to Fleming for contests against Denver Waldorf. The 2A Spartans are currently 12-2 on the season. Boys' JV is slated to begin at 2 p.m.

title: McCracken reports on HVAC and bus repairs
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The January meeting of the Frenchman Board of Education opened with staff reports and included just one item of business before moving on to first reading edits of administrative regulation policy.…
content:
The January meeting of the Frenchman Board of Education opened with staff reports and included just one item of business before moving on to first reading edits of administrative regulation policy. The Board held productive discussions on the polices, which took up a good portion of the meeting held in late January.
Brittany Pierce and Megan King opened the meeting, giving board members reports on their specific areas within Fleming Schools. Pierce is the Elementary Title I teacher. She works with a total of 18 students, specifically in reading and math. To do so, she uses the 95 Percent Group program as her curriculum. 95 Percent Group is an evidence-based literacy solution used by schools.
King serves as the Elementary Special Education teacher and her caseload includes 11 students. King assists them in being successful in their respective classrooms.
In her administrative report, Principal Kortney Firme told the Board that she and staff member Becky Harms attended CTE Director Credential Training recently. She also noted that discussions have started to prep for the 2025-26 school year.
Superintendent Steve McCracken rounded out staff reports, updating board members on the HVAC system, bus repairs and the new greenhouse.
McCracken said the District continues to work on individual heating units. Recently, he was forced to cancel school for two consecutive days due to heating issues. He said units in the kitchen and math room have been replaced.
The school district has now used all of the allotted snow days for the school year, so moving forward any additional school closures will be remote learning days to keep students on track.
The Superintendent also touched on bus repairs, noting that one of the route busses has been in the repair shop for quite some time, but the parts are now in and the mechanic is working to get them installed.
As far as the greenhouse, work continues on installing the natural gas supply line and installing the electrical system.
Throughout the rest of the meeting board members:
• Ratified the decision to start school at 10 a.m. on Jan. 21;
• Approved the 2024-25 revised budget to reflect changes in student count data;
• Jeff Brekel, board member, discussed the need for additional handicapped parking spaces in the school parking lot;
• Discussed the following administrative policy regulations as part of their first reading: Support Staff Vacation and Holidays, Part-Time and Substitute Professional Staff Employment/Qualifications of Substitute Staff, Instructional Staff Sick Leave, Transition Year for Retiring Teachers, Professional Staff Vacation and Holidays and Committee Structure.
The next board meeting is slated for Feb. 18 at 6:30 p.m.

title: Kilgour signs with Lamar
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Haxtun senior Maggie Kilgour celebrated National Girls and Women in Sports Day by signing a letter of intent to play volleyball at Lamar Community College on Wednesday, Feb. 5. Kilgour was surrounded…
content:
(Herald photo by Candie Fix) count
MAGGIE KILGOUR, Haxtun High School senior, committed to play volleyball at Lamar Community College next year in front of family, friends, teammates and supporters on Wednesday, Feb. 5. Seated in front are (l-r), High School volleyball coaches Don Schelling and Marissa Chapdelaine, Maggie Kilgour and High School Volleyball Coach Emma Heinz; back row (l-r), Ron, Amy and Alli Kilgour.
Haxtun senior Maggie Kilgour celebrated National Girls and Women in Sports Day by signing a letter of intent to play volleyball at Lamar Community College on Wednesday, Feb. 5. Kilgour was surrounded by family, friends, supporters and teammates as she put the finishing touches on her commitment to continue her volleyball career.
"We believe that Maggie will bring a lot of energy and high expectations to our program. We believe that she will be a contributor to helping us have a successful season," said Lamar Head Volleyball Coach Dave Tacklenburg.
"I watched some highlights of her playing and her high school coach spoke very highly of her. I also talked to Maggie on the phone and I liked what she had to say."
Kilgour was a key component of the Lady Bulldogs 19-10 season that finished with a Colorado State Volleyball appearance. Haxtun finished as a top six team in the 2A Classification and following that season, Kilgour was named All-Conference along with being selected to participate in the Colorado Coaches of Girls Sports All-State games. She was also named All-State, Honorable Mention at the conclusion of her senior year.
In her time wearing a Lady Bulldog jersey, Kilgour racked up 487 kills and 21 blocks at the net. Behind the service line, she earned a 88.9 percent serving percentage which included 58 aces. On defense she tallied 472 digs and on serve receive he registered 587 receptions.
"We think that Maggie will be a six rotation player and hit on the outside for us," Tecklenburg said.
While playing volleyball for the Lady Lopers, Kilgour plans to study Early Childhood Education.
"When Maggie came on her campus tour and tryout, we really liked her attitude, work ethic and how coachable she was. She has the warrior mentality and will be a great fit to our program," said Tecklenburg. "The assistant coaches and I are really excited to have the opportunity to work with Maggie and have her be part of our Volleyball family."

title: Wildcats tack on league win over Warriors; defeat Denver Waldorf
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Fleming Wildcats tacked on two in the win column last week with victories over the Weldon Valley Warriors and the Denver Waldorf Spartans. The wins bring the Wildcat squad to 3-14 on the year with…
content:
(Herald photo by Spring Atchison) count
FLEMING SENIOR Travis Johnson goes up for a shot with Denver Waldorf's Josh Stanley defending the basket. Johnson currently leads his team in points per game averaging 8.2 and rebounds per game averaging 12.5.
The Fleming Wildcats tacked on two in the win column last week with victories over the Weldon Valley Warriors and the Denver Waldorf Spartans. The wins bring the Wildcat squad to 3-14 on the year with just three games left on the regular season schedule.
Friday's contest put the Wildcats on the road to Weldona for league action with the Warriors and despite the victory, Fleming remains one spot behind Weldon Valley in league standings. The two teams sit in numbers three and four. Weldon Valley has yet to meet up with the league's top two teams, Prairie and Peetz.
The Wildcats took a sizable victory over the Warriors Friday night at 59-43. Senior Travis Johnson eaned a double-double in the outing after leading the team in rebounds with 20 and adding 12 points on the scoreboard. He brought down 13 defensive boards and seven on offense.
Freshman Dylon Monroe led Fleming's offensive efforts for the night. He scored 25 points after sinking seven two-point buckets, one three-pointer and eight free throws. He followed Johnson under the basket in rebounds with five total. Sophomore Conner Marchant also added five rebounds in the game.
Saturday's contest against Denver Waldorf saw the Wildcats in the lead by eight after the first, 15-7. The visiting Spartans narrowed that lead to four by the close of the half, 22-19. The Wildcats would go on to outscore the Spartans by two in the third and fourth quarters to earn a 44-37 victory.
Johnson earned a double-double for the second consecutive night. He led the Wildcats in rebounds with 23 and added 12 points to the scoreboard. He brought down 16 defensive and seven offensive boards.
The Monroe twins, sophomores Dylon and Jaron, topped their team's scoring with 14 and 13 points, respectively. They made nearly identical efforts, each scoring off one three-point shot and four two-point buckets. Dylon made good on three attempts from the charity stripe; Jaron added two off free throws.
The Wildcats are scheduled to play on the road for the remaining three games of the regular season. This weekend takes them to Briggdale on Friday for a league contest against the league's fifth ranked Falcons. Girls' varsity is scheduled to begin at 5 p.m.
Saturday takes the team to Lone Star to take on the 7-6 Longhorns. Junior varsity boys are set to take the court at 2 p.m. that day.

title: Subdivision exemptions, courthouse security & records requests, among matters addressed by Phillips County Commissioners
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: In the past few months, a variety of matters have come before the Phillips County Board of County Commissioners that have required discussions across two or more meetings. Research has been needed…
content:
In the past few months, a variety of matters have come before the Phillips County Board of County Commissioners that have required discussions across two or more meetings. Research has been needed between the meetings in order to make an informed decision. Not all matters are time-sensitive so some decisions are still pending.
The board considered a subdivision exemption application from Rick Ensminger to divide a 2.97-acre parcel from a 157-acre parcel located in S5, T7N, R47W. Questions arose about to what degree the availability of water needed to be addressed before it could be approved because the purpose of the exemption was so that the parcel could be sold for an eventual residence. Typically, a plan for water is known prior to an exemption request being made if the use includes a need for water. In this case it was unknown.
The buyer was followed up with by both Ensinger and County Administrator/Planner, Andrew Nygaard. Based on the information they brought back to the board, the request was approved on Jan. 10.
Going forward, however, the board identified a need for better clarity should similar requests be made in the future. Of concern to the board was whether or not there could be any liability incurred on the part of the county for certain types of decisions, avoiding any overreach of its authority and ensuring the county complies with statutes and regulations.
Exemptions are regulated by state statute and land use codes that are aligned to state statutes. Statutes also allow for some exemptions. The building permitting process can also address the need-to-know details before approval. The County planning commission also plays an integral role in the development of the land use codes and ensuring compliance with them. All things considered, the board wants to know if any revisions are needed to current regulations.
The board visited with staff in the Assessor's office. It also consulted the law firm Sullivan, Green, Seavy, Jarvis LLC about county regulations and what they know about how other counties deal with similar situations. This firm was the one used to help draft the land use code adopted on June 30, 2023 that replaced the former zoning regulations.
Staff from the law firm held a virtual meeting on Jan. 17 with the board, assessor's office staff and the administrative and planning staff. They discussed options and offered an example of how another county approached the water-related regulations that included making use of one of the exemptions allowed in the statute.
The guidance received from the virtual meeting will be taken under consideration by the planning commission and the board of county commissioners.
A need to upgrade security at the Phillips County Courthouse has resulted in the installation of new locks and cameras. The programming of the locks is still in progress.
Discussions were had with Sheriff Michael Beard about the installation of new door locks for the courthouse, Event Center and sheriff's office building. At this time there will not be new installations at the Event Center but there could be in the future.
The board also met with County Attorney Tammy Kelley, Beard, and Undersheriff Jack Wieland regarding concerns about loitering and trespassing in public buildings.
The board places a high priority on ensuring all staff and visitors in the building feel safe and that areas are appropriately secured.
A local governmental agency made a rare records request from the Phillips County Communications Center. It prompted questions about who has the authority to request records and under what circumstances. The board requested Kelley to research the Colorado Open Records Act for any additional advice or guidance. Kelley later shared that an inter-governmental agreement could be a way to cover such requests in the future. The communications center will continue following the Colorado Open Records Act.
Commissioner Roberts informed the other commissioners that a Holyoke Lions Club member let him know that the club no longer had any use of their concession stand at the fairgrounds. It has not been operational for several years. The building had become an empty shell because the club cleaned out its contents. They deemed the building to be unsalvageable, including the concrete floor. They were ready to let it go and it could now be demolished.
The board agreed to allow the county to carry out the demolition. The club is now exploring the possibility of putting up a picnic shelter where the building once stood. It has funds to commit toward all or a partial cost to do so. The board will get additional input about this idea before making a decision.
The County road and bridge shop operating in Amherst no longer has a use for the Quonset-style storage building in Amherst. The board has been contemplating whether or not the building and lot should be sold.
The board has had the property appraised. It also investigated the location of the water well, which also serves two other residences in the vicinity. The Assessor's office has assisted them with other particulars about the property.
An actual price is not yet known should the board decide to have it put up for sale. It also intends to explore whether or not it would be allowable to put any conditions on a sale.
There is no particular timeline for making a final decision on what to do with this property.

title: Sedgwick County-Fleming wrestling teams shine at State Tourney
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The 2025 Colorado High School Activities Association (CHSAA) State Wrestling Championships showcased the talent and determination of the Sedgwick County/Fleming wrestling teams. With tough competition throughout the weekend, several athletes made notable performances, despite the challenges they faced on the mats. Annie Wilson had an eventful tournament in the G130-4A division but did not place....
content:
The 2025 Colorado High School Activities Association (CHSAA) State Wrestling Championships showcased the talent and determination of the Sedgwick County/Fleming wrestling teams. With tough competition throughout the weekend, several athletes made notable performances, despite the challenges they faced on the mats.
Annie Wilson had an eventful tournament in the G130-4A division but did not place. She started strong with a fall victory over Evelyne Cope from Gunnison Girls in 1:09. However, in the quarterfinals, she was pinned by Ella Splitter from Lamar Girls in just 1:04. Wilson picked up another win in the consolation bracket, pinning Makayla Ward from Holy Family Girls in 1:09. Unfortunately, she was eliminated after a fall to Eleanor Thorson from Canon City Girls in 1:40.
Olivia Stone was unable to secure a victory at the state tournament in the G155-4A division. She started with a tough loss to Maliyah Sandoval from Pueblo Central Girls, who pinned her in 1:21. Stone was then eliminated after being pinned by Callah Caperton from Moffat County Girls in 0:43 in the consolation round.
Among the highlights from the boys' wrestling team, was Scotty Engle's remarkable victory in the 144-2A weight class, where he claimed the state title, capping off an exceptional performance with a state championship and a sixth place finish in the team race.
Scotty Engle, with a season record of 44-5, became the 2025 2A State Champion in the 144-pound weight class. Engle's tournament journey was flawless, as he dominated his matches from the start. In the opening round, he pinned Wyatt Meyer from Highland in just 45 seconds. In the quarterfinals, Engle secured a close 13-11 decision over Forrest Craddock of Colorado Springs Christian. His semifinal performance was equally impressive, defeating Andree Meraz from Center by a 9-2 decision. In the first place match, Engle faced Jason Hemsath from Custer County. The championship bout was intense, but Engle proved too much for Hemsath, pinning him in 6:00 to claim the state title. Engle's victory marked an outstanding achievement as this win by pin was Engle's 100th high school career pin.
Grant Statz showed incredible resilience in the 165-pound weight class, ultimately earning fifth place with a record of 20-5. Statz started the tournament strong, winning his opening match with a quick fall over Ryder Weber from Hayden in just 32 seconds. He followed up with another pin, this time over Marcos Villegas from Rocky Ford in 30 seconds. However, Statz was narrowly defeated by Lincoln deKay of Ignacio in a thrilling semifinal match, falling 15-12 in sudden victory. In the consolation semifinals, Statz lost by fall to Jacob Pacheco from Monte Vista. Nevertheless, Statz bounced back to win the fifth-place match with a decisive fall over Martin Palma from Center in just 23 seconds.
Austin Knox, with a season record of 31-18, had a rollercoaster ride in the 132-pound weight class. After being pinned in the first round by Taylor Torres from Walsenburg Jr/Sr High School in 0:58, Knox quickly regained his momentum in the consolation rounds. He won back-to-back falls, first against Brandon Pecina from Holly in 2:48 and then over Kaleb Grauer from Akron in 2:51. However, his tournament ended in the third round of consolation, where he was pinned by Jadiss Rodriguez from Rocky Ford in 4:08.
Ryan Davis (19-13) faced a challenging field in the 190-pound weight class, where he fell short but showed his resilience. Davis began the tournament with a tough tech fall loss to Chason Turner from County Line (19-1 in 3:46). In the consolation rounds, Davis earned a tech fall victory over Caleb Colclasure from Peyton (16-1 in 5:00), keeping his hopes alive. However, his tournament came to an end with a fall to Kai Wilcox from Colorado Springs Christian in 2:30.
While not all wrestlers from the Sedgwick County/Fleming team walked away with medals, their effort and determination were evident. The teams showed grit in the face of tough competition. The coaching staff and the wrestling community continue to support these athletes, who have a bright future ahead of them.

title: Bulldogs pick up two home wins & take 2024-25 LPAA League title
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Haxtun Bulldogs moved to 11-8 with recent home court wins over Idalia and Caliche last week. With the recent victories, the Bulldog are on a five-game win streak and have clinched the Lower Platte League title. Haxtun picked up a 29-point win over the Idalia Wolves on Friday and topped the Buffs by 13 on Saturday in back-to-back home court contests. Coming out on top against the Caliche Buffs...
content:
The Haxtun Bulldogs moved to 11-8 with recent home court wins over Idalia and Caliche last week. With the recent victories, the Bulldog are on a five-game win streak and have clinched the Lower Platte League title.
Haxtun picked up a 29-point win over the Idalia Wolves on Friday and topped the Buffs by 13 on Saturday in back-to-back home court contests. Coming out on top against the Caliche Buffs leaves the Bulldogs with a 4-0 league record and despite the outcome of this week's match up with Sedgwick County, the 2024-25 LPAA title.
According to Colorado High School Activities Association RPI rankings as of this week, the Bulldogs sit 11th in Colorado 2A.
Others from the Lower Platte who hold slots within the top 15 include Sedgwick County at 10 and Akron at 12.
"The team has been focusing on just taking steps forward and trying to get better every day so that when the end of the season comes around we are playing our best basketball and doing the little things right," said Ryland Wolff, Bulldog Co-Captain. "We have to just take it one game at a time and can't overlook anyone."
Haxtun had an impressive start against the Wolves on Friday, racking up 17 points in the first quarter alone while defensively holding Idalia to just four. The Bulldogs added double-digits to the scoreboard in all four quarters for a final 59-30 win.
Junior Chase Goddard registered 17 points on Friday. Sophomore Madden Larsen put 12 points on the scoreboard. Others who contributed include Kanin Koberstein with nine points and Wolff with eight.
Under the basket, Wolff pulled down 11 rebounds followed by junior Colin Cone with eight and Goddard, who tallied seven.
Saturday's action pitted the Bulldogs against the Buffs from Caliche. The final of that contest left the Bulldogs on top, 62-49.
Goddard and Larsen again led the Bulldogs, this time Goddard with 19 and Larsen with 17. Wolff also registered double digits in the scoring department, adding 13.
Goddard bought down 14 rebounds, the team high, followed by Cone with eight, Wolff with six and Larsen with four.
"This year instead of being goal oriented, the team decided to focus more on progress every day. Our focus on progressively getting better every day has shown to help us improve more than set goals," said Wolff's Co-Captain, Tate Michael. "The team has done a good job at taking each day as an opportunity to get better and play our brand of basketball every game."
This week the Bulldogs are set to host the Sedgwick County Cougars in league action Friday night.
MaxPreps puts the Cougars at 12-5 this season. One of their five losses came from the Bulldogs in mid-December in tournament play at Northeastern Junior College. Haxtun took that contest by a five-point spread.
As for the rest of the season, Michael said his team will need to just focus on improving every time they step on the court.
"The team will need to focus on getting better every day at practice, staying healthy and to keep playing with confidence and intensity," Michael said.
Next week Haxtun will compete in a season-end tournament with play beginning for the boys team on Wednesday in Limon. Junior varsity is set to tip off at 4:30 p.m. followed by varsity at 6 p.m.
From there, the Bulldogs will take part in tournament play in Akron on Friday, Feb. 28 and Saturday, March 1.
According to information on CHSAANOW, 2A Regional/State brackets are set to be released on March 2 with Regional play set for March 7-8 with higher seeds hosting.
"When it is playoff time, we need to take every game seriously and need to focus on one team at a time. And overlook no one," Wolff said.

title: Haxtun's captains weigh in on season success and the post-season
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Lady Bulldogs played host to both Idalia and Caliche last week with back-to-back games on Friday and Saturday. Despite two losses in very close match ups, one in overtime, the Lady Bulldogs are…
content:
(Herald photo by Candie Fix) count
SENIOR AND CO-CAPTAIN Bobbi Starkebaum, #50, puts up a shot between Caliche defenders #3 Hallie Lewis and #10 Kendyll Armstrong in a Saturday afternoon match up at the home of the Lady Bulldogs.
The Lady Bulldogs played host to both Idalia and Caliche last week with back-to-back games on Friday and Saturday. Despite two losses in very close match ups, one in overtime, the Lady Bulldogs are pressing forward while focusing on putting in 100 percent effort and maintaining a positive attitude.
"Coming off of last year, we wanted our goals to be something that we put effort into every day to make ourselves better. These goals, like putting in 100 percent effort and having a positive attitude, have contributed to our success this year," said senior Kelsie Hadeen, one of three Lady Bulldog captains this season. "Our focus for the rest of the season is making every moment count. Every practice showing up to make each other better and pushing ourselves and our teammates to success."
As of mid-week, the Lady Bulldogs hold an overall 8-11 record and stand at 2-2 in the Lower Platte League. The 50/50 league record puts the team in the middle of LPAA standings ahead of Akron and Holyoke, according to MaxPreps. As of Feb. 17, Haxtun sits at 21 out of 58 teams in Colorado High School Activities Association 2A RPI standings. Fellow LPAA teams Merino and Sedgwick County hold the top two spots in those same standings.
On Friday Haxtun hosted the Lady Wolves from Idalia, a top four team in 1A State rankings, according to CHSAANOW. The Lady Bulldogs trailed by two after the first quarter and were down by just by just four at half time.
The home team came out hot after the half, scoring 16 points to even things at 30 all heading into the fourth quarter. The Lady Wolves edged a nine-point advantage for a final 46-37 win.
Senior Kelsie Hadeen put 10 points on the scoreboard, the team high. Junior Lilly Lemesany added nine, senior Bobbi Starkebaum put up eight, senior Jayleigh Bullard contributed six and freshman Leah Edwards scored four.
Starkebaum and Bullard combined evenly for 24 total rebounds. Hadeen registered six and Lemesany brought down five.
Lemesany led the Lady Bulldogs in assists with two while Bullard and Hadeen racked up three steals apiece.
The following night, Haxtun jumped to a two-point advantage after the first quarter of play against the Caliche Lady Buffs. The Bulldogs added 13 in the second for a 27-19 half time advantage. Things heated up in the second half, Caliche outscoring the Lady Bulldogs by five in the third and three in the fourth to send the game into overtime. The Lady Buffs edged their way to a seven point win in overtime, 58-51.
Three Lady Bulldogs put double-digits on the scoreboard against Caliche; Starkebaum racked up 17 points, Bullard registered 13 and senior Emily Anderson added 12.
Three also earned top markings in the rebounding department led by Starkebaum with 17 total, Edwards with 12 and Hadeen with 10.
Hadeen registered four assists and Emma Lemesany tallied two.
"So far our team has been pretty focused on getting better every day. We also have worked a lot on our press and I think it really shows in games how much focus we have put on that. To add onto that, I think we have also focused a lot on limiting our mistakes in games and working on learning how to fix them during practice," Emily Anderson, Lady Bulldog Co-Captain, said. "Our team will need to focus on moving the ball fast and well. We will also have to limit turnovers and focus on communication on both defense and offense."
This week, the Lady Bulldogs host the top ranked Lady Cougars from Sedgwick County on Friday. Recently, the Lady Cougars topped Merino, ending the Lady Rams 40+ game winning streak. MaxPreps puts Sedgwick County at 14-3 this season and undefeated in league standings.
After Friday night's contest, the Lady Bulldogs will advance to an end of the season tournament with play beginning on Tuesday, Feb. 25 in Burlington. Junior varsity action is set to begin at 4:30 p.m. followed by varsity at 6 p.m. The tournament continues Friday, Feb. 28 and Saturday, March 1 in Akron.
According to information on CHSAANOW, 2A Regional/State brackets are set to be released on March 2 with Regional play set for March 7-8 with higher seeds hosting.
"We need to start every game strong and continue that until the very end," said Bobbi Starkebaum, the third of the Lady Bulldog captains. "All of our players need to give 100 percent effort to have a strong finish to our season."
The senior leader went on to share her highlights of this season so far. "I have enjoyed getting closer with my teammates and seeing so much improvement in each girl from last year to now. I loved beating Akron during the last play of the game in their own gym," Starkebaum said.

title: Bullard signs with Cobras
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Haxtun's Jayleigh Bullard plans to continue her volleyball career at Coker University in Hartsville, S.C. next fall. The high school senior signed a letter of intent with the D II college on Tuesday,…
content:
(Herald photo by Spring Atchison) count
HAXTUN SENIOR Jayleigh Bullard, seated center, signed a letter of intent to play volleyball at Coker University next year in front of friends and family on Tuesday, Feb. 11. Those pictured are front row, (l-r), the Bullard family, Taivyn, Tom, Jayleigh, Jessica and Cooper; back row Haxtun Volleyball Coaches Don Schelling and Marissa Chapdelaine.
Haxtun's Jayleigh Bullard plans to continue her volleyball career at Coker University in Hartsville, S.C. next fall. The high school senior signed a letter of intent with the D II college on Tuesday, Feb. 11 with friends, family and teammates in attendance.
Bullard, a varsity starter, played four seasons for the Lady Bulldogs. In that time, she racked up 482 kills boasting a .174 hitting percentage her senior season. Bullard registered 124 total blocks at the net in her high school career.
Along with impressive numbers at the net, Bullard served up 41 aces as a high school varsity player. She also tallied 157 digs and 210 passes on serve receive.
Coker University Head Coach Stephanie Dragan said she was first intrigued by Bullard's athleticism.
"Athleticism and we need depth to our outside hitter position. I'm hoping she will challenge our returners daily in practice and work to beat someone out," Dragan said.
Bullard was a part of the Lady Bulldog volleyball team that made several state tournament appearances throughout her four years. The Bulldogs finished with an overall 19-10 record and as a top six team in Colorado 2A her senior season.
While playing volleyball at Coker University, Bullard plans to major in pre-law and minor in business.
"I like to recruit good people. Kind people. Jayleigh checks both of those boxes," said Dragan. "I like to surround myself with different personalities that bring different things to the program."

title: Wildcats fall to Otis in crossover tourney; set to take on Lone Star Friday
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Despite the break in their recent winning streak, the season continues for the Fleming Wildcats who fell to Otis in a crossover tournament on Tuesday. The Wildcats closed the regular season on a five-game winning streak with a win last Friday on the road at Idalia. The Wildcats were closely matched with the Wolves in their final regular season game before tournament play last week. They fell to...
content:
Despite the break in their recent winning streak, the season continues for the Fleming Wildcats who fell to Otis in a crossover tournament on Tuesday. The Wildcats closed the regular season on a five-game winning streak with a win last Friday on the road at Idalia.
The Wildcats were closely matched with the Wolves in their final regular season game before tournament play last week. They fell to an eight point deficit in the first quarter, 15-7, but closed in on two points of that gap in the second to trail by six at the half.
The Wildcats cranked up the intensity in the third quarter and added nine points to their side of the scoreboard while the defense gave up just two points to the Wolves. Heading into the final quarter of play, the Wildcats held a single-point advantage.
The two teams battled for the victory in the final quarter, but in the end it was the Wildcats who came out on top. They added their fifth consecutive win with a two-point lead over Idalia, 33-31.
On Tuesday, Feb. 25, the Wildcats took on Otis, the top team in the YWKC, in an NC/YWKC crossover tournament at Northeastern Junior College in Sterling.
The Otis Bulldogs took control on the scoreboard early in the contest and jumped to a 32-16 lead in the first half. They continued to dominate for the remainder of the game which closed at a score of 72-31.
The Wildcats now fall into the consolation side of the crossover tournament bracket. That puts them in a contest against Lone Star on Friday, Feb. 28 at 3:30 p.m. The game is set to take place at Wally Post Gymnasium in Sterling.
Fleming and Lone Star met up just two weeks ago. In that contest, Fleming earned a hard-fought, five-point victory.

title: Fleming's season closes after 2-point loss to Caliche
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Fleming Wildcat boys' basketball team will hang up their jerseys for the season following 1-2 performance in the end-of-season crossover tournament held last week in Sterling. Fleming entered as…
content:
(Herald photo by Spring Atchison) count
FLEMING WILDCATS Treyson Kirkwood and Conner Marchant reach for a rebound in Saturday's season-ending contest against Caliche at Sterling High School's Tigers' Den.
(Herald photo by Spring Atchison) count
TRAVIS JOHNSON, Fleming Wildcat senior, goes up for a lay up in Saturday's game against the Caliche Buffaloes. Johnson led his team in several categories this season including scoring at 9.4 points per game and rebounds averaging 13 boards per game.
The Fleming Wildcat boys' basketball team will hang up their jerseys for the season following 1-2 performance in the end-of-season crossover tournament held last week in Sterling. Fleming entered as the eighth ranked team out of 12 competing teams; the top six moved into the regional/state bracket.
The Wildcats opened with a 58-30 loss to the top-ranked Otis Bulldogs. Otis would go on to win the tournament and enter the post-season bracket as the second ranked team in Colorado 1A.
Senior Travis Johnson led the Fleming squad against Otis in scoring and rebounds. He earned a double-double for his contributions in the two categories with 12 points and 12 boards. Johnson also led in assists with two.
Freshman Dylon Monroe in steals with five. Sophomore Conner Marchant added another four steals.
Tuesday's loss to Otis put Fleming up against Lone Star on Friday. The Wildcats and the Longhorns met in the regular season with Fleming taking a five-point victory. This time the Wildcats earned the win by a greater margin, 48-32, after holding the Longhorn offense to just two points in the second quarter.
Johnson earned another double-double in the second outing of the tournament. He scored 16 points and pulled down 17 rebounds.
Sophomore Treyson Kirkwood also hit double digits on the scoreboard with 11 points. Defensively, he stole the ball three times.
Monroe followed Johnson's efforts under the net. He brought down seven rebounds.
Junior Wyatt Sonnenberg led in steals with five.
The win on Friday pitted the Wildcats against the Caliche Buffaloes on Saturday. The two teams met in mid-December before Christmas break when Caliche took a three-point victory on their home court.
The most recent contest ended in the same fashion, with Caliche on top, but this time by an even slighter, two-point margin. The Buffaloes took a hard-fought game to advance into the post season by two points.
Kirkwood led the Wildcats on the scoreboard with 14 points; nine of those off three-point shots.
Johnson led under the net in rebounds with 14 boards; six offensive and eight defensive.
The season closes for the Wildcats at 7-16. They went 2-2 in league play for a third place finish. The top two teams out of the North Central League, Peetz and Prairie, have advance into post season play.
Watch future editions of the Herald for the announcement of All-Confernce honorees.

title: District court judge & clerk visit with Phillips County commissioners
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: During the Feb. 10 regular meeting of the Phillips County Board of County Commissioners, the Chief Judge of the 13th Judicial District, Carl S. McGuire III, and the Clerk of the Court, Kathy Browning,…
content:
count
During the Feb. 10 regular meeting of the Phillips County Board of County Commissioners, the Chief Judge of the 13th Judicial District, Carl S. McGuire III, and the Clerk of the Court, Kathy Browning, met with the board. The purpose was so that McGuire and the Commissioners could be personally introduced to each other. McGuire was recently assigned to District Court duties for Phillips and Sedgwick counties after district Judge Justin Haenlein was placed on a temporary paid suspension in November of 2024. Haenlein's performance is under review by the Colorado Commission on Judicial Discipline.
McGuire expressed his appreciation for the support of the Phillips County Sheriff's Office and the staff who provide court security when in session. He described the relationship with Sheriff Beard as a great partnership. He also thanked the Commissioners for their support.
McGuire remarked about the workability of the Webex system that allows people to attend court remotely. Participants appear on a large computer monitor located in the courtroom, as do some attorneys or others needing to testify. McGuire believes that, although there are advantages to having defendants appear in person and that is preferred, Webex works well for those who are detained elsewhere in county jails.
The recent relocation of the magnetometer, often referred to as a metal detector, was discussed . On days when court is in session, it has been situated at the east entrance of the courthouse whereas all visitors to the building must enter only through that door. It has been moved to the third floor near the courtrooms.
McGuire stated that if there are any needed security upgrades, he's aware of grant funding specific to courtroom security.
"The County would have to be the applicant, not the court, but I can assist with information if you're interested in knowing more," McGuire said."
McGuire and the Board both commended Browning for being especially proficient with the Clerk duties and all the support and expertise she provides. Employed by the 13th Judicial District, Browning serves as a Clerk for both the District and the Phillips County court because it's considered to be a combined court. She spends most of her time in Phillips County but also fills in occasionally in Sedgwick County, which is also a combined court.
The discussion concluded with the sentiments of how much everyone looks forward to working with each other going forward.
Updates and discussions
Jessie Salyards, Colorado State University Extension Agent, met with the Board to update it on recent 4-H activities and other work being done in her office. She reported that 97 youth are enrolled in 4-H this year. That is a decrease from 125 last year. The most common reason cited for not returning to 4-H is because of participating in sports.
The Board learned that the person who had been enrolled in the law enforcement training academy for a future Sheriff's deputy position discontinued the training and moved out of state. Sheriff Beard is exploring options to get someone else hired sooner than later because of the anticipated retirement of Undersheriff Jack Wieland in a few months.
The Board learned of a forthcoming vacancy in the Department of Human Services and another one in the Phillips County Communications Center.
The law firm assisting the county to address the availability of water in subdivision exemption applications recommended language for two different options for the Board to consider.
Commissioner Garold Roberts learned recently from Beard that some of Colorado's sheriff's departments are paying officers' personal liability insurance. This is in response to Senate Bill 20-217 that made peace officers more personally liable in certain situations. Some instances exempt them from Qualified Immunity and also from being indemnified by the law enforcement agency. Beard is researching these other agencies to learn more about this.
Roberts followed up with residents in Amherst whose water is supplied by a well on county property to discuss options if the property should be sold.
Roberts also learned that the County will not receive one of the possible Homeland Security-related grants to fund a new generator at the Phillips County Event Center. However, other Homeland Security-related grants may be applicable, as well as other state agency grants. The county emergency manager is exploring options.
Business decisions
The Board proposed amending the Phillips County Land Use Code section 10-105.B.5, as follows: "Approval of a subdivision exemption plat does not constitute any finding by the County regarding whether a well permit will be issued by the State Engineer or whether water is available on the parcels." The proposed amendment will go before the Planning Commission for a public hearing and then before the Board of County Commissioners for a public hearing.
The Board approved contributions of $200 each for the Haxtun and the Holyoke high schools after prom events.
Three bids for the construction of the Pleasant Valley Road and Bridge storage building were accepted, as follows: Heath Weiss Electric, LLC for electrical services; Phillips Drilling and Pump, to provide water well-related work; and VAP Construction to provide building, concrete and door-related work.

title: Amherst property to sell; grants & gas wells on commissioners' agenda
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Following a few months of information gathering, the Phillips County Board of County Commissioners, at its Feb. 18 regular meeting, decided to sell through a bid process the Road and Bridge Department…
content:
count
Following a few months of information gathering, the Phillips County Board of County Commissioners, at its Feb. 18 regular meeting, decided to sell through a bid process the Road and Bridge Department storage building in Amherst. The minimum bid will be $50,000. County Administrator/Planner Andrew Nygaard was charged with pulling details together for a formal announcement to elicit bids.
The property consists of a 5,500 square foot Quonset building, another 1,200 square foot building, a 1,000-gallon propane tank and a domestic well that also serves two residential properties. The quonset was originally the Amherst school's gymnasium and the smaller building was the bus barn. After the school closed in the mid-1960s, the property was managed by the Amherst Volunteer Fire Department. During that time it included a storage area for farm implements and a community room where many meetings and events were held on a regular basis. When it was no longer feasible to manage the property, the AVFD sold it to Phillips County for storage, which is no longer needed.
The Board met with Kent Vance, the Grant Navigator for the Northeast Colorado Association of Local Governments. He discussed the availability of grants, as well as grant funds that may be on hold indefinitely due to the current freeze or elimination of federal program funds by the Department of Government Efficiency.
Toby Thompson, Deputy County Assessor, discussed the possibility of tagging three Omimex gas well compressors with restraint orders so they cannot be removed until taxes owed are paid. The Assessor's office needs to get a model number and determine to whom to send the tax bill. Legal counsel will be contacted regarding next steps.
Kendra Calderon, the new Phillips County Economic Development Director, was introduced by PCED board member, Nici Akey. Chairman Tom Timm invited Calderon to attend the NECALG meetings for the information exchange and because other area economic development directors are often present.
The Board met with Bill Andrews, Landfill Manager, to discuss repairs to the roll-off truck's motor. He received an estimate from one business. A couple of others approached were not interested in pursuing the work. He described the possibility of modifying another vehicle to handle what the roll-off truck does. Andrews will get firm estimates on that alternative for advisement at a future meeting. The Board also discussed discontinuing having roll-off dumpsters for rent.
Subdivision exemptions
Following a public hearing without any comments received, the board approved a subdivision exemption application from Harvey and Nancy Colglazier to sell 5.44 acres to Coltin and Phawn Houghtelling from a 161-acre parcel located in the NE ¼ of Section 17, Township 6 North, Range 44 West.
The board also approved a boundary line adjustment application from Tracy Schroth, as presented. It reduces to 4.16 acres the 5.7-acre parcel that was approved on Nov. 8, 2023 in a subdivision exemption request. The acreage is located in the NW ¼ of S15, T7N, R44W.
Reports by commissioners
Based on public comments at the previous meeting, Timm spoke with Weed and Pest Manager Kerri Doleshall about contacting individual landowners regarding spraying weeds on their property.
Garold Roberts reported on the Feb. 20 Northeast All-Hazards Region board meeting in reference to homeland security-related grants. The Holyoke Police Department, the Phillips County Sheriff's Office and Melissa Memorial Hospital are all applicants for funds.
Roberts also reported that the permit on the well at the Pleasant Valley site for the Road and Bridge building had been revoked in 2000 on the grounds that a logbook that was to have been kept had not been received by the State. Efforts were being made to locate the logbook. If it cannot be found, the county will have to obtain a permit.
Discussion and decisions
The Board discussed raising the current $2,000 purchasing limit for department heads whereas higher amounts require board approval.
Department managers' purchase requests were approved for the following items:

title: Bulldogs clinch #10 seed in CHSAA playoff bracket; face #23 seed
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The final 2A boys' basketball playoff bracket is out and the Colorado High School Activities Association ranks the Haxtun Bulldogs at #10. Haxtun finished with a 2-1 record at the conclusion an end-of…
content:
(Herald photos by Candie Fix) count
JUNIOR CORBIN ANDERSEN, #32, fights for a rebound with Badger defender Daniel Forristall in a home contest with Limon last Thursday. The Bulldogs pulled out a 55-43 win over the Badgers.
count
Ryland Wolff
The final 2A boys' basketball playoff bracket is out and the Colorado High School Activities Association ranks the Haxtun Bulldogs at #10. Haxtun finished with a 2-1 record at the conclusion an end-of-the-season tournament last week.
Overall the Bulldogs hold a 14-9 record and as the #10 seed are set to face #23 seeded Del Norte at Dakota Ridge High School in round one of post-season play.
End-of-the-season tournament action kicked off last Wednesday as the Bulldogs hosted Limon in game one. The Bulldogs dominated on both sides of the court for an impressive 55-43 finish over the Badgers. The win pitted Haxtun in a match up with Sedgwick County on Friday in Akron.
For the second time in a week, the Bulldogs met up with the Cougars. The match up marked number three for the two teams this season. Up to this point, Haxtun came out on top in the first two. And yet again, the Bulldogs did it in game three as the red and black went on to claim a 59-47 win over Sedgwick County.
A victory over the Cougars put the Bulldogs in the tournament championship and on the court with the Byers Bulldogs, a team in green and white. Byers is the number two seeded team from the Union Pacific League behind that League's top team, Stratton.
Byers went up by three after the first quarter of play but the Bulldogs continued to fight, putting 11 points on the board in the second. Haxtun outscored the opponent by one in the third and throughout the fourth, continued on a quest for a lead. The Bulldogs fell short by 10 at the final buzzer, 52-42.
As the 10th seeded team, Haxtun will take on Del Norte, who holds an overall 11-10 record. The Tigers finished second in the Southern Peaks League with a 3-2 league record. The two teams will meet on Friday, March 7 at 7 p.m. at Dakota Ridge High School.
The winner of that match up will advance to the Sweet 16 slated for Saturday, March 8 and face the winner of Golden View Classical Academy and Belleview Christian. The Sweet 16 contest is set for 12 p.m., also at Dakota Ridge. Golden View Classical Academy entered the 32-team playoff bracket as the seventh seed; Belleview Christian is the 26th seeded team.
Saturday's winner will advance to the State Tournament set for March 13-15 at Blue Arena in Loveland. Colorado High School 2A basketball finals are set for Saturday, March 15.

title: Dorris Scott
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Doris Jean (Schaefer) Scott passed away in Haxtun on March 3, 2024 at the age of 86. Doris was born on Aug. 27, 1937 in Sterling to Ben and Martha (Brekel) Schaefer. Doris graduated from Fleming High…
content:
Share Tweet 0 Comments March 13, 2024 Dorris Scott Doris Jean (Schaefer) Scott passed away in Haxtun on March 3, 2024 at the age of 86. Doris was born on Aug. 27, 1937 in Sterling to Ben and Martha (Brekel) Schaefer. Doris graduated from Fleming High School in 1955. She received her nursing degree and became an RN in 1956. She married Wayne Scott on Aug. 24, 1957 in St. Peters. After working as a nurse for a few years, Doris began her career in the Post Office in 1969. She was the Post Master of Holyoke when she retired in 1992. In 1994 Doris started her own vending business known as "Bubbles, Etc." She was crowned Mrs. Colorado in 1968. Doris also spent her life on the family farm raising crops and cattle. Doris is survived by her husband Wayne; children Julie and husband John McGrath and Dona and husband Jack Willmeth; grandchildren Brandon and Taylor Abraham, Jake, Jessica and Kent and Dawson Willmeth. She is also survived by her sister Mary Lu Moline, Aurora. Doris is preceded in death by her parents, Ben and Martha Schaefer, and daughter Terrie Scott Abraham. Funeral services were held on March 8 at Christ The King Catholic Church in Haxtun. Father Jerry Rohr officiated the service. Baucke Funeral Home was entrusted with the arrangements. title: Alan Dick
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Alan Richard Dick (Schultz), a devoted husband, loving father and cherished grandfather, passed away peacefully on March 7, 2024 at the hospital in Provo, Utah. Alan was born on Nov. 16, 1947 in…
content: Alan Richard Dick (Schultz), a devoted husband, loving father and cherished grandfather, passed away peacefully on March 7, 2024 at the hospital in Provo, Utah. Alan was born on Nov. 16, 1947 in Gresham, Ore., to proud parents Clarence and Christine Dick. He was the eldest child and grew up alongside his brother Gary and sisters Kathy and Vicki. In 1954, athe family moved to Colorado eventually settling in Haxtun, where Alan spent his formative years. A proud graduate in 1967 of Haxtun High School, where he played football alongside his younger brother. In September 1967, Alan met the love of his life, Rebecca Kay Schwaderer, and their romance led to marriage on Nov. 24 of the same year. Their union was blessed with three children: Martin, Lana and Erin. In January 1968, Alan answered the call of duty and proudly served his country in the United States Army during the Vietnam War. Stationed in Virginia, he served as a skilled helicopter mechanic in Vietnam, contributing to the war effort with dedication and courage. After his honorable discharge, Alan and his family relocated to Murray, Utah in 1973 until settling in Price, Utah in 1974 where he worked tirelessly in the coal mines for many years until his retirement in 2012. Despite the demanding nature of his work, Alan always made time for his family and pursued his passions. In his free time, Alan found joy in being a part of a pit crew for the local stock car races with his close friends that became his second family, shooting his black powder rifle with the Bookcliff Muzzleloader Club and cherished moments spent fishing with loved ones. Alan was a beloved Papa to eight grandchildren, 10 great-grandchildren and many others who adopted him to be their Papa, which all brought immense joy and pride into his life. He is survived by his brother Gary and wife Rose Dick, sister Kathy and husband Eddie Gallegos; children Martin and wife Anna Dick, Lana Dick and Erin Rolfsness; as well as all of his grandchildren and great-grandchildren. Alan will be deeply missed by all who had the privilege of knowing him. His legacy of love, strength, and compassion will live on in the hearts of his family and friends forever. He is preceded in death by his parents; his loving wife of 53 years Rebecca; daughter-in-law Jackie Dick; and baby sister Vicki Akin and her husband Gary Akin. Friends and family are invited to pay their respects at the memorial service, which will be held on April 19 at 11 a.m. at the Utah Veterans Cemetery & Memorial Park located at 17111 1700 W. Bluffdale, UT 84065. Following the service, a gathering will take place at Good News Lutheran Church, at 3281 N. 1120 E. Lehi, UT 84043. Condolence cards can be sent to 1777 E. West Pinion Circle, Eagle Mountain, UT 84005.

In brief, Holyoke has had a telephone service in one form or another since 1888, when the first telephone switchboards were installed. A telephone line between Haxtun and Holyoke was completed in October 1903, the culmination of much effort. Immediately, there were plans to extend the lines. In 1962, mobile radio telephones were installed, and in 1965, the rural users started to give their lines to the company to maintain and improve. In 1982, with financing from the Heginbotham Trust, a paging system was installed on the company property. In 1990, Phillips County Telephone Company at a cost installed Northern Telecom switching equipment and cut over to new fiber optic toll facilities.
