title: Wildcats fall to South Platte, Neb. and Otis
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Fleming Wildcats came within two points of their first victory on Friday night against the South Platte Blue Knights out of Big Springs, Neb. The Wildcats hosted the Blue Knights and the Otis…
content:
(Herald photo by Spring Atchison) count
JARON MONROE, Fleming Wildcat freshman, stops short of the hoop and looks for an open teammate on Saturday against Otis. The Wildcats opened the weekend's play with a two-point loss to South Platte and fell to Otis 72-31.
The Fleming Wildcats came within two points of their first victory on Friday night against the South Platte Blue Knights out of Big Springs, Neb. The Wildcats hosted the Blue Knights and the Otis Bulldogs last weekend falling on both occasions.
Friday night's game opened with Fleming down by just three after the first quarter, 17-14. They came back and gained control of the scoreboard in the second quarter adding 15 and holding the visiting team to just six. Fleming led at the half, 29-23.
The Blue Knights answered back with 18 points in the third quarter. They regained control of the scoreboard by a single point after holding the Wildcat offense to 11 points, 41-40.
The two teams battled in the fourth quarter, but the Wildcats fell just short at the final horn. South Platte outscored the home team by one point to take the two-point win, 56-54.
Senior Travis Johnson earned a double-double for the night leading his team in both scoring and rebounds. He tallied 18 points, all off two-point buckets, and brought down seven offensive and five defensive boards for 12 total rebounds. He also led the team in steals with five.
Sophomore Conner Marchant followed with 15 points and seven rebounds. He score 14 off two-point shots and went one-for-two at the free-throw line.
Junior Jared Betley matched Marchant under the basket with seven rebounds. Sophomore Treyson Kirkwood led in assists with six.
Saturday night's fast-paced contest opened with the Otis Bulldogs out in front by 10, 16-6. The Bulldogs added another 16 in the second half and gave up 10 to the home team putting Otis on top 32-16 at the half.
Otis' defense shut the Wildcats down in the second half allowing just 15 points throughout the third and fourth quarters. The Bulldogs tacked on 40 points in the second half for a 72-31 win.
Johnson led the Wildcats in the scoring and rebound columns for the second consecutive night. He tallied eight points and grabbed eight rebounds split at four offensive and four defensive.
Marchant and freshman Dylon Monroe each contributed four points. Monroe also pulled down five offensive boards.
League play opens this week for Wildcats on Friday when they host Prairie. The Mustangs enter at 3-6 on the season. Boys' junior varsity is slated to begin at 4 p.m. that day with girls' and boys' varsity to follow.
Saturday's contests put the Wildcats on the road to Genoa-Hugo/Karval for a non-league match up with the Pirates. The Pirates currently stand at 1-7 on the year. JV boys are set to take the court at 3 p.m.
The Wildcats will close the week on Tuesday, Jan. 21 with non-league home games against Akron who sits at 4-5 overall. Tip off is listed for 4 p.m.

title: Lady Bulldogs pick up back-to-back wins, 1 at home, 1 on the road
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Lady Bulldogs picked up a pair of wins last week with a victory on the road in Kimball, Neb. and another in a home court contest with Prairie. The back-to-back showings puts the team at almost 50…
content:
(Herald photo by Candie Fix) count
HAXTUN LADY BULLDOG Jayleigh Bullard, senior #1, holds onto the ball while surrounded by Lady Wildcat defenders in an early December contest at home. Teammate Bobbi Starkebaum, senior #50, is pictured entering from the right for assistance.
The Lady Bulldogs picked up a pair of wins last week with a victory on the road in Kimball, Neb. and another in a home court contest with Prairie. The back-to-back showings puts the team at almost 50 percent on the season with just 10 games left on the schedule before post-season.
Friday's contest pitted the Lady Bulldogs in a match up with the Lady Longhorns in Kimball, Neb. It was all red and black from the start as Haxtun jumped to an early advantage, allowing both varsity and junior varsity players time on the court. Haxtun pulled away with a 51-40 victory.
Senior Bobbi Starkebaum led the Lady Bulldog offense in Kimball. She connected with nine field goals and made four free throws for a total of 22 points. Senior Kelsie Hadeen scored eight points while senior Jayleigh Bullard and freshman Leah Edwards each contributed six.
Under the basket, Starkebaum pulled down 14 rebounds, the team high. She nabbed 10 on offense and four on defense. Hadeen and Bullard brought down seven rebounds apiece and junior Katiegh Cody and Edwards tallied four each.
Edwards and Anderson registered a combined eight assists against the Lady Longhorns. Bullard, Edwards and Anderson each had two steals.
The following day, Prairie came to town as the Lady Bulldogs hosted one of the top-ranked teams from the 1A classification. Haxtun went up by one after the first and added another 13 to the board to hold a 27-21 lead at the half. The Lady Bulldogs scored just five points in the third but commanded a win with 16 points in the fourth for a final 48-37 contest.
Anderson and Edwards put double digits on the scoreboard in Saturday's home matchup, both racking up 12 points. Bullard contributed nine followed by Lilly Lemesany with eight.
For the second, consecutive night Starkebaum led her team in rebounds, pulling down 14 total. Bullard registered 11 rebounds, Edwards tallied nine and Hadeen brought down five.
Anderson racked up three assists and one steal. Hadeen and Starkebaum each had two steals.
"We have been working hard on being intentional and focused in all aspects of our game. The coaching staff has seen a shift in the intensity of our offense and defense during practice and have talked a lot about doing things that are outside of our comfort zone. How being uncomfortable in our play is the only way we can continue to grow," Head Coach Alicia Schram said of her Lady Bulldogs' performances last week. "Prairie was a huge win for our program. Not only because we were able to put a 'W' in at the end of the night, but we were able to prove that we could play with, outlast and sometimes outperform a seventh-ranked team. That did a lot for our confidence. The girls took a lot of risks during that game and they paid off!"
This week the Lady Bulldogs traveled on Tuesday night to take on the Lady Bulldogs in Otis. The team fell 45-36 on the road in a tight, competitive match.
On Friday, Haxtun is set to take on Peetz on the road and then the following day, host Holyoke at home. According to MaxPreps, the Lady Bulldogs from Peetz are 2-7 overall. The same site lists the Lady Dragons of Holyoke at 3-6. Haxtun took down Holyoke in December in the annual Holiday Tournament by a score of 53-38.
"We are going to continue to work on confidence and execution in every game, no matter the opponent. We can't underestimate an opponent and have to continue to play hard, regardless of what the score is. We have some fun games coming up and will just work hard to continue to make strides!" Schram said.

The Lady Bulldogs are on a winning streak, taking victories in five of their last eight games. Overall, the Haxtun team is 6-6 heading into the final few weeks of the regular season. A record with six wins already checks off one of this year's team goals; to win more games than the season before.
"The girls are starting to play a little out of their comfort zone. Along with that risk, comes greater rewards. We are starting to see all the little things that we've worked on all year, start to click. We are shooting better, doing the little things right, and figuring out what works for our team," said Alicia Schram, Lady Bulldog Head Coach.
In a busy week of action, the Lady Bulldogs hit the road to Peetz on Friday and turned around to host the Lady Dragons from Holyoke the following day. Haxtun nabbed a 56-20 win on the road over the Lady Bulldogs in green and topped the Lady Dragons 47-34 at home.
The two wins last weekend gives the team a two-game win streak, but the Lady Bulldogs have picked up four wins in their last five games. Since Dec. 20, Haxtun has clinched wins over Holyoke, twice, Kimball, Neb., Prairie and Peetz while suffering losses only to Akron, Wiggins and Otis.
"One of our main goals as a team and as a coaching staff was to win more games than we did last year. Once we got over that mental goal, I think the girls finally saw their potential," Schram said. "Our team has definitely grown closer over the last three weeks, and that has driven their success. The family atmosphere has been fun to see."
Haxtun put on a dominating performance in Peetz, going up 24-4 in the first quarter. The Lady Bulldogs put 13 points on the board while holding Peetz to just two in the second to hold a 37-6 advantage at half time. Haxtun added 15 points in the third and four in the fourth for a final 56-20 showing.
Senior Jayleigh Bullard led Haxtun on the scoreboard with 13 points in Peetz. She connected with six field goals and a free throw for her double-digit performance. Kinsley Koberstein racked up eight points, Katiegh Cody put up seven and Kelsie Hadeen and Emily Anderson each added five.
Bobbi Starkebaum, a senior, pulled down eight total rebounds, the team high. She nabbed seven on offense and one on defense. Anderson brought down seven rebounds, Cody pulled down six and Reagan Jones totaled five.
Hadeen led in assists with three followed by Anderson, Starkebaum, Jones, Leah Edwards and Lilly Lemesany, each with two assists. Edwards and Anderson each had five steals.
Saturday's contest was much the same as the night before with Haxtun gaining an early advantage, 19-3 in the first quarter. The Bulldogs put 19 points on the board for a 32-12 lead at the half. Another 15 points in the second half gave the home team a 13-point win; the Bulldogs second over Holyoke this season.
Starkebaum connected with eight field goals and a single free throw for 17 on the night. She also led in rebounds with six, four offensively and two defensively. Anderson scored eight points followed by Bullard and Hadeen, each with seven.
Hadeen brought down five rebounds, Jones and Anderson each pulled down four and Lemesany and Bullard both tallied three. Anderson registered six steals and also led in assists with six.
"A fun stat from last week is that 13 out of 14 of our girls scored last week in varsity games and everyone recorded minutes," Schram said. "It was good to see some of the younger girls get to be successful in a varsity game and so fun to watch the normal starters support them with so much excitement from the bench. It will probably be something I remember for a very long time."
This week the Lady Bulldogs are set to host Merino on Friday and Burlington on Saturday. From there, the team still has match ups with Holyoke, Akron, Brush, Idalia, Caliche and Sedgwick County remaining on the regular schedule, many of those marking Lower Platte League contests.
"We have a tough couple of weeks coming up, for sure. There are a lot of very winnable games left on our schedule. We will just continue to prepare them with as much ammunition as possible and give them the best shot at being successful. We will continue to work on the little things - especially finishing. They are a very intelligent team with a lot of drive, it will be fun to watch them find a way! It's hard to believe that there are more games behind us than what we have left," said Schram.

title: Haxtun suffers two close, single-digits losses to Peetz and Holyoke
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Haxtun took on two tough teams in green last week; first on the road Friday in Peetz and the other against Holyoke at home on Saturday. The Bulldogs and Dragons proved to put on demanding performances…
content:
(Herald photo by Spring Atchison) count
MADDEN LARSEN, Haxtun sophomore #12, drives past two Holyoke Dragon defenders on his way to the hoop in a home contest on Saturday. Larsen recorded a career high of 19 points against the Dragons.
Haxtun took on two tough teams in green last week; first on the road Friday in Peetz and the other against Holyoke at home on Saturday. The Bulldogs and Dragons proved to put on demanding performances but despite-hard-fought battles in both contests, Haxtun fell short by single digits. Half of the Bulldog's remaining eight regular season games will mark league matchups for the team, including another with Holyoke again just next week.
Haxtun held an early four-point advantage after the first quarter of play in Peetz on Friday. The Bulldogs in red put another 12 points on the board in the second for a 25-24 tally in favor of the home team at half time. Peetz scored one more than Haxtun in the third to control the lead heading into the fourth. The Bulldogs in green dominated the fourth quarter, putting 20 points on the board to Haxtun's 13 for a final 63-54 win.
Junior Colin Cone racked up 21 points on the road in Friday's contest. Senior Ryland Wolff also hit double-digits, putting 14 points on the board. Sophomore Madden Larsen and junior Chase Goddard each scored six followed by Kanin Koberstein with five.
The following day, Haxtun hosted Holyoke for Phillips County showdown one of the season. The two teams will meet again on the 31st, which will mark the league match up for the two teams.
The Bulldogs controlled much of the game, and the scoreboard, until the final minutes when Holyoke pulled out an advantage and held it for a four-point, 60-56 win on Haxtun's home court.
Larsen led his team on Saturday with a total of 19 points. Two others, Wolff and Goddard, also racked up double-digits; Wolff with 16 and Goddard with 10. Cone added eight points while Jaxsen Schram contributed three.
"Despite the losses, the boys kept their head in each game. They did a good job of keeping each other in the game even if things weren't going our way," Head Coach Jayden Stieb said. "We still need to limit our turnovers and clean up some of our offensive sets. Colin had a career high 21 points on Friday, hopefully that will spark him offensively the rest of the year. Madden had a career high 19 against Holyoke."
This weekend Haxtun will stay home and host Merino on Friday and Burlington on Saturday. According to MaxPreps, the Rams are 2-7 overall and the Cougars hold a 0-6 record.
After that, the Bulldogs will face Holyoke, Akron, Brush, Idalia, Caliche and Sedgwick County to round out the regular season schedule.
"I think all of our league game will be close. In those close games we need limit our mistakes and take advantage of each possession," Stieb said.

title: Colo. CattleWomen announce scholarship
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Colorado CattleWomen announce the 2025 Cattle Women Legacy Scholarship. The Heather Hays Stinnett Memorial Scholarship honors Colorado CattleWomen Past President Heather Stinnett and will be…
content:
The Colorado CattleWomen announce the 2025 Cattle Women Legacy Scholarship. The Heather Hays Stinnett Memorial Scholarship honors Colorado CattleWomen Past President Heather Stinnett and will be awarded to a woman pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree.
Heather was a staunch advocate for the beef industry and a proud fifth generation Coloradoan who traced her cattle industry heritage to early Colorado statehood and ranches homesteaded by ancestors on both sides of her family. Heather's agricultural credentials include serving as Colorado FFA Reporter, judging livestock at Seward Community College and graduating from Oklahoma State University with degrees in Animal Science and Agricultural Communications. She and her family owned a feed store, raised commercial cattle and operated a custom grazing enterprise. Heather served as the President of the CCW from 2017 to 2019. She then served as the Chair of the Board of Directors for the American National Cattlewomen in 2019.
Applications are being accepted for the scholarship until April 15 and the scholarship will be awarded in June at the 2025 Colorado CattleWomen annual meeting in Steamboat Springs. Women who are a Colorado resident, a juunior, senior or a graduate student at an accredited four-year university or college, majoring in agriculture or an agricultural related major aspiring to work in or advocate for the beef industry are encouraged to apply.
More information on the Heather Hays Stinnett Memorial Scholarship and past recipients can be found on the Colorado CattleWomen's website at https://coloradocattlcwomcn.org/colorado-cattlcwomen­ legacy-scholarships/. For more information, email [email protected].

title: Haxtun picks up two road wins; currently on a 3-game win streak
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Haxtun Bulldogs are on a three-game win streak an currently holding the top spot in the Lower Platte League. Just three games remain on the regular season schedule and Head Coach Jayden Stieb says…
content:
(Herald photo by Candie Fix) count
HAXTUN JUNIOR Chase Goddard battles for a ball on the ground with two Merino defenders in a late January home game. The Bulldogs pulled out a one-point win over the Merino Rams.
The Haxtun Bulldogs are on a three-game win streak an currently holding the top spot in the Lower Platte League. Just three games remain on the regular season schedule and Head Coach Jayden Stieb says his team needs to be prepared to play their best games yet.
The Bulldogs traveled to Akron on Thursday for a week-night League match up with the Rams. The two teams met in the Holiday Tournament just before Christmas break and in that contest, Haxtun took a five-point win. Last week's contest was even closer.
Haxtun added 11 points in the first quarter and tacked on another 12 in the second for a 23 point total at the half. Down the stretch in the fourth quarter, the Bulldogs and Rams traded single-point advantages but coming out of a time out with just under a minute and a half remaining Akron led by one.
The Rams attempted to stall with a passing game outside the arch but senior Ryland Wolff managed a steal from the top of the key. Wolff took the ball to the hoop and put up a shot, which was good to put Haxtun up on the board by one. The Rams wasted nearly a minute off the clock in their final possession and attempted a last second shot that fell short of the rim, giving the Bulldogs a 39-38 win.
Haxtun took a total sweep in Akron, both the boys' and girls' varsities winning by a single point.
Wolff and junior Chase Goddard put up a double-digit performance against the Rams. Wolff led with 11 points followed by Goddard with 10. Kanin Koberstein racked up eight points, Colin Cone scored six and Madden Larsen contributed four.
Under the basket, Wolff pulled down seven rebounds. He grabbed three on offense and four on defense. Goddard registered four total rebounds followed by Cone with three and Larsen with two.
Wolff and Goddard both tallied three steals off the Rams.
"Akron was a tough game. The Rams did a great job controlling the tempo and taking care of the ball. They slowed the game down to a halt at times," Stieb said. "Although we weren't able to find a good pace or rhythm most of the game, we were able to make plays when we needed to."
The following night, the Bulldogs traveled west to the home of the Brush Beetdiggers where they put on a dominating performance for a final 70-59 win. The back-to-back wins last week leaves Haxtun 9-8 overall and 3-0 in league play, according to MaxPreps.
"Against Brush, we were able to keep the game at our pace. Offensively, we did a great job getting the ball inside on their zone. Chase and Ryland both worked hard in the paint and our guards were able to hit outside shots when the ball got kicked back out," said Stieb.
Three Bulldogs combined for 50 of Haxtun's 70 points in Brush. Goddard and Larsen both racked up 20 points and Cone added 10. Wolff put nine points on the scoreboard and Schram added eight.
The Bulldogs are set to be at home this week, hosting Idalia on Friday and Caliche on Saturday. Stieb said his team will need to be ready to go on game day.
The following week, Haxtun rounds out the regular season with a final League contest with Sedgwick County.
"This week we need to stay focused on improving. We've hit a nice little stride here the past few weeks and we can't lose our momentum. In our two games this week, we need to play our best game of the season on Friday and then play our best game of the season on Saturday," the Coach said. "Going down the stretch here, we need to do a better job on the boards and taking care of the ball. I feel like our guards have grown a lot this year and we've really cut down our turnovers. Our rebounding needs to be a little more consistent these next few games."

title: Healing close to home: Haxtun Health's Inpatient Rehab program
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Imagine being in a place where you're not quite ready to return home, but you no longer need the intensive care of a hospital. This in-between stage can be challenging, but Haxtun Health's Inpatient…
content:
count
Imagine being in a place where you're not quite ready to return home, but you no longer need the intensive care of a hospital. This in-between stage can be challenging, but Haxtun Health's Inpatient Rehabilitation program offers the perfect solution. Nestled in the heart of Haxtun, this program provides a comforting and familiar environment where patients can continue their recovery journey with the support of dedicated healthcare professionals.
At Haxtun Health, the Inpatient Rehab program is more than just a place to heal; it's a haven where patients can regain their strength and independence. With the guidance of skilled providers, nurses and rehabilitation specialists, patients receive personalized care tailored to their unique needs. This program ensures that individuals can recover close to home, surrounded by the people and community they trust.
Individuals may be eligible to participate in the program if their needs cannot be met at home, but their condition no longer demands a hospital stay. The goal of the program is to provide extra care to those who still need day-to-day assistance to build independence before going home; for example, post-surgery patients prone to falling or those who still need IV therapy.
"There are many reasons why a stay at Haxtun Health can be so helpful and beneficial to patients. Our Inpatient Rehab program offers a unique blend of medical expertise and compassionate care, ensuring that each patient receives the attention and support they need to recover fully," said Stacey Higgins, RN, Case Manager at Haxtun Health. "They can receive this type of care right here at home. Now, they don't have to go to the Front Range for the care they need."
Details about Haxtun Health's Inpatient Rehab program
"Our Inpatient Rehab program at Haxtun Health is truly exceptional. Our physical therapists, speech therapists and nursing team work tirelessly to provide the highest level of care and support to our patients," said Higgins. "Their dedication and expertise ensure that each patient receives the precise help that they need. It's incredibly rewarding to see our patients regain their strength and independence, knowing that they are in the best hands. We are proud to offer such a comprehensive and compassionate program right here in our community."
Each patient receives customized care to fit their exact needs, which could include; physical therapy, up to five days per week, occupational therapy, speech therapy, 24-hour access to on-site providers, 24-hour nursing care, activity programs tailored to the patient, no visitor restrictions - families can visit patients in the hospital at any time, visits from a provider at least three times each week, access to visiting specialty providers and on-site Laboratory, Pharmacy, Radiology, and wound care certified nurses.
The Inpatient Rehab program at Haxtun Health is designed to bridge the gap between hospital and home, ensuring patients receive the care they need in a familiar and supportive environment. By offering comprehensive rehabilitation services and personalized care plans, Haxtun Health helps patients regain their independence and return home safely.
"Our team is dedicated to making each patient's recovery as smooth and effective as possible. We take pride in our ability to provide high-quality care that is both compassionate and goal-driven. Seeing our patients regain their independence and return home safely is the most rewarding part of our purpose," Higgins said.
For more information about the Inpatient Rehab program visit haxtunhealth.org/services/inpatient-rehabilitation or contact Higgins at [email protected].

title: Haxtun Town Council increases annual salary for chief of police
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Town of Haxtun continues to work on the hiring process of new police chief. In addition to acting on several items of business related to the search of a new chief, council members approved a…
content:
count
The Town of Haxtun continues to work on the hiring process of new police chief. In addition to acting on several items of business related to the search of a new chief, council members approved a resolution regarding flex time for police officers, an airport grant agreement and economic incentive application in February's regular monthly meeting.
The hiring committee tasked with finding a new police chief gave a report to the Council and additionally discussed a chief salary adjustment so the job posting could be published.
At the recommendation of the committee, and after reviewing cost of living and wages from surrounding agencies, council members voted to make the Police Chief's starting salary range between $71,000 and $81,000 a year, depending on qualifications.
The Council also opted to give the hiring committee authority to make a conditional offer to an applicant that has successfully gone through two interviews and the authority, at that time, to close the application process.
"Giving the committee authority to do so will streamline the process without waiting for the next Council meeting," said Haxtun Town Clerk Kelsey Harms.
The Police Chief Hiring Committee is made up of Council members Ryan Horton and Jon Brammer along with others with law enforcement backgrounds including former council member Rob Martinez, Colorado State Patrol Trooper Marc Bornhoft, former Colorado State Patrol Trooper Brandon Biesemeier and Holyoke Police Chief Doug Bergstrom.
Darrell Smith is currently serving as Interim Police Chief for the Town of Haxtun, a role he was appointed to in early January. Smith has been with the local department since September 2022.
In keeping with police department business, the Council also voted to approve Resolution 2025-1, adopting amendments to the Town of Haxtun Personnel Rules and Regulations, specifically regarding flex time for police officers. These changes apply specifically to police officers at agencies that employ less than five employees. Those agencies are exempt from overtime and compensatory time off.
The new policy adopted this month allows officers to accrue flex time in excess of their 90 hours that includes on-call time.
"This Council hopes that this will allow for a good work-life balance," Harms said.
The Haxtun Town Council also approved a second resolution, one pertaining to an airport grant agreement. That resolution is titled 2025-2.
Superintendent Ron Carpenter applied for a grant through the Colorado Department of Transportation's Aeronautics/Colorado Aviation department for a new concrete airport apron and helicopter pad. That grant was approved as a 90/10 agreement. The total project is estimated to cost $87,000; the grant will cover $78,300 and the Town will add $8,700 to the project.
Additionally, the Town Council approved an Economic Incentive application from Phoenix Beauty Bar, submitted by owner Amanda Wilson. Wilson's application asked for incentives for real property tax, use tax, building permit fees and materials relating to main street beautification such as windows, doors, an awning, stucco and lumber. The application states the downtown business would, "bring more foot traffic to town and make the downtown curb appeal beautiful."
Council members voted to approve $9,790.50 in incentives for materials for façade improvements, waiver of Haxtun use tax and the building permit fee.
In other business the Council:
• Held a public hearing for and approved ordinance 2024-8 to adopt the most recent edition of the Colorado Model Traffic Code;
• Approved a 2025 engagement letter for the 2024 financial audit with Lauer, Szabo and Associates;
• Agreed to use a donation of $1,000 from Colorado Highlands Winds towards the frisbee golf activity at the park and other parks/recreation use;
• Approved the following building permits: Justin Stone, 525 East Strohm Street to close in a porch; Wyatt Workman, 602 West Fletcher Street for new siding; Ryan Kanode, 527 South Utah for a shed and Amanda Wilson, 107 South Colorado Avenue for a remodel.

title: Haxtun Health announces physician transitions, reaffirms commitment to community healthcare
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Haxtun Health has announced upcoming changes to the provider team as the organization navigates a time of transition in medical staff while remaining steadfast in the commitment to providing high…
content:
count
Haxtun Health has announced upcoming changes to the provider team as the organization navigates a time of transition in medical staff while remaining steadfast in the commitment to providing high-quality healthcare for our community.
Dr. Adam Hansen, DO joins the team as a full-time provider
Haxtun Health announced this week that Dr. Adam Hansen, DO, has signed on as a full-time provider. Dr. Hansen comes to Haxtun with experience in Internal Medicine with years of experience in geriatric care. He is already on site at Haxtun Health. Over the next few weeks, he will be working closely to on-board with current providers to ensure uninterrupted care for patients.
"We look forward to introducing him to the community. Be on the lookout for more information soon!" said Haxtun Health Interim Chief Executive Officer Julia Biesemeier.
Dr. Amy Seinfeld's
transition home
Dr. Amy Seinfeld will be departing mid-March to return to her home state of Florida, where she will be closer to her family. When she joined our organization, she anticipated staying in Haxtun for three to five years. That time has now come, and after much consideration, she has made the decision to move back to be closer to her parents, daughters and extended family, recognizing that this is where she is needed most.
"We understand that some things in life go beyond a better financial offer, persuasion or convincing and family is one of them. We respect and support Dr. Seinfeld in her decision and we appreciate the time she has spent serving our patients. One of the unique advantages of rural healthcare is the ability to build strong, personal relationships between providers and patients and Dr. Seinfeld did exactly that with many of those she cared for," said Biesemeier. "We are grateful for her contributions and wish her the best as she moves into this next chapter."
Dr. Dana Morgan
embraces an opportunity ahead
Dr. Dana Morgan, who has been serving as our Interim Chief of Staff, will be departing mid-May after accepting a once-in-a-lifetime career opportunity in Montana.
"While her time at Haxtun Health has been just under a year, the impact she has made has been profound and will be deeply felt across our community," Biesemeier said. "Dr. Morgan quickly developed an immediate and meaningful connection with her patients, especially in the area of hormone replacement therapy and women's health, where she has provided life-changing care to so many. Her warmth, expertise and ability to listen deeply to patient concerns have made her irreplaceable in the eyes of many."
The Interim CEO said Haxtun Health made every effort to retain Dr. Morgan, but despite that, respects and celebrates this incredible opportunity for her.
"Dr. Morgan has shared with us that our community has made a tremendous impact on her life, coming at a much-needed time in her personal and professional journey. She leaves with nothing but gratitude for the relationships she has built here and we know she will carry the spirit of our town with her as she moves forward," Biesemeier added.
Dr. Morgan will remain at Haxtun Health through mid-May ensure continuity of care for her patients. Patients who have been under her care are encouraged to schedule follow-up visits as needed while staff will work to ensure a smooth transition for patients.
Our commitment to the future
Rural healthcare is facing immense challenges across the country and Haxtun Health is not immune to those difficulties. However, the organization is committed to putting forth every effort to ensure that our community emerges from this transition with healthcare it deserves.
• Haxtun Health is conducting an aggressive and focused search for additional providers who are the right long-term fit for our community.
•With the support of long-term partner, Docs Who Care, Haxtun Health has a solid lineup of providers scheduled to ensure the clinic, emergency room and hospital are fully covered during this transition.
• Haxtun Health administration is taking this opportunity to redefine how the organization delivers care, ensuring sustainability and access to essential services.
"This is not just about filling positions - it's about finding the right people, building a sustainable future and ensuring that healthcare in our community remains strong and accessible for years to come," said Biesemeier. "We know these transitions may cause concern and we understand the uncertainty that comes with change. However, we ask for your continued trust and support as we work diligently to secure the future of healthcare in our community."

title: Calderon steps into new role as PCED Director
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Kendra Calderon is the new Director of Phillips County Economic Development. Calderon took her place at the helm of the local organization mid-February and in her first few months plans to acquire a…
content:
(Courtesy photo) count
Kendra Calderon
Kendra Calderon is the new Director of Phillips County Economic Development. Calderon took her place at the helm of the local organization mid-February and in her first few months plans to acquire a knowledge and understanding of the needs of Phillips County and specifically the world of economic development.
Calderon was born and raised in Holyoke. After graduating from Holyoke High School in 2004, she moved to Texas where she worked as a dog groomer for seven years. Calderon returned to Holyoke in 2015, later moved to Haxtun in 2016 and since then has worked in healthcare purchasing for nearly a decade. She spent time at Melissa Memorial Hospital, Wray Community District Hospital and most recently with Haxtun Health as the head of the purchasing department.
"After many years of being away, I returned home to Northeastern Colorado, where I raised my children Azariah and Avian Calderon," she said. "My daughter is now in college at Regis University in Denver and my son is a senior at Haxtun High School."
In her free time, Calderon said she likes to craft and travel. She also enjoys attending school sporting events, supporting her son and fellow athletes. Calderon is in her first year as the Haxtun High School Cheer Coach, another new adventure she is excited about.
Calderon said as her children are growing and graduating high school and college, she's spent time reflecting on what life without kids at home would like. When thinking about what she wanted to do in this next stage of life, she said she wanted to do something that would make an impact in her community.
"I just knew I wanted to make a difference in my lifetime," she said. "When I saw this opportunity I knew I had to go for it. To be able to make positive changes to help our communities just gave me a passion that I had not yet experienced."
Since its establishment in 2000, PCED has been dedicated to advancing the common economic objectives outlined by the visionary leadership of Phillips County. Calderon said PCED collaborates with local chambers of commerce, youth and service organizations, regional partnership councils, private businesses and local and state government divisions and is a resource-driven catalyst that contributes to the overall economic growth of Phillips County.
"Our mission is centered on providing essential resources and information to create jobs, retain and expand businesses and encourage the development of youth apprenticeships and entrepreneurship," said Calderon.
As Phillips County Economic Development Director, Calderon can be reached by calling (970) 580-3614. At the moment, she is primarily in the Holyoke office, located at 127 East Denver Street, Suite B, in Holyoke, but as she gets her footing, she will be setting up an office in Haxtun as well. Watch Phillips County Economic Development Corporation on Facebook for schedule updates and other information as it is released.
"My goals and priorities for the next few months are to learn the needs of Phillips County, to understand the world of Economic Development and make connections that will help not only benefit my goals but the goals of the communities," Calderon said. "I am very excited to dive into the world of Economic Development where I will be able to give back to these communities that do so much."

title: Bulldogs finish 5-0 in LPAA; tourney action in Akron this weekend
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Haxtun Bulldogs won the LPAA League title outright with an impressive win over Sedgwick County on Friday night. The game marked parents' night, when players honor their supporters at half court…
content:
(Herald photo by Candie Fix) count
MADDEN LARSEN, Haxtun Bulldog #12, puts up a shot between two Sedgwick County defenders in a home contest on Friday night. Larsen had 22 points, six rebounds, six assists and two steals in the match up.
The Haxtun Bulldogs won the LPAA League title outright with an impressive win over Sedgwick County on Friday night. The game marked parents' night, when players honor their supporters at half court before game time. Haxtun is 5-0 in league play and is now set to compete in an end-of-the-season tournament slated for this weekend.
The Bulldogs took on the Cougars for the second time this season and match up number two went the same as the first, but by a larger margin. Haxtun edged out a single-digit win in mid-December at Northeastern Junior College.
This time, at the home of the Bulldogs, the Cougars gained a three-point advantage after the first quarter. Haxtun amped up the pressure in the second, putting 17 points on the scoreboard while defensively holding the visiting team to just seven.
The Bulldogs went on to score 16 in the third and 18 in the fourth for a final 65-53 win in front of their home crowd.
Three starters put up double-digit figures in the match up. Sophomore Madden Larsen racked up 22 points, junior Chase Goddard added 19 and senior Ryland Wolff scored 13. Larsen went 12 for 12 from the free-throw line, recording a perfect percentage at the charity stripe.
Goddard earned a double-double while also pulling down double digits in the rebounding department. He totaled 11 against the Cougars. Wolff brought down eight rebounds followed by Colin Cone with seven and Larsen with six.
Larsen also tallied six assists and two steals.
This week the Bulldogs were set to host Limon in the first round of end-of-the-season tournament play at home on Wednesday night. That game was not complete as of press time.
Haxtun will continue tournament play on Friday and Saturday in Akron. For a complete bracket and updates, visit the Haxtun School District Facebook page.

title: Haxtun Health's Girls' Night Out: An inspiring evening amidst the blizzard
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: On the evening of Tuesday, Feb. 18, community members gathered for Haxtun Health's annual Girl's Night Out event and what an unforgettable night it was! Despite the fierce blizzard, sub-zero…
content:
(Courtesy photo) count
WENDY EVANS received the Wellness for Women Award in honor of her widespread influence on the Haxtun community and surrounding areas.
On the evening of Tuesday, Feb. 18, community members gathered for Haxtun Health's annual Girl's Night Out event and what an unforgettable night it was! Despite the fierce blizzard, sub-zero temperatures and treacherous icy roads, organizers were heartened to see so many courageous souls who braved the elements to attend.
The evening was made even more enchanting with delightful mocktails from Saved by the Well, an establishment founded by Kaelyn Armstrong in Ogallala, Neb. Their inventive and refreshing beverages were a resounding hit among the attendees. The hospital's dietary team, led by Sue Razo, curated the perfect meal paired with a variety of tea sandwiches, salad and a creamy soup that had everyone abuzz.
The night was imbued with elegance and enlightening conversations. Attendees were privileged to have several esteemed speakers join the event virtually. Dr. Ehrin Armstrong, a cardiologist specializing in women's heart health, imparted invaluable wisdom in maintaining a healthy heart. Dr. Megan McKenna, a general surgeon, underscored the significance of a healthy waistline and the necessity of regular colonoscopies.
Adding to the evening's charm, Wendy Evans, Haxtun Health's Director of Health and Wellness, enlightened us on the importance of the pelvic floor with a delightful exercise that sparked much lighthearted laughter from the audience. Lauren Gerk addressed the prevalent issue of back pain among women and educated us on the impactful changes we can make in daily lives to prevent and treat such pain that afflicts many.
Attendees were also graced by the presence of Reba Bean, a Haxtun Health physician assistant, who emphasized the importance of routine cancer screenings for women. The final speaker of the night, Dr. Lila Statz, introduced a breast cancer screening tool that everyone can use at home to assess their risk of developing breast cancer. To utilize the online tool, visit bit.ly/418cVWi.
With the exception of Dr. Statz, community members can schedule a visit with any of the providers that visited with the event at Haxtun Health. If you have questions about your heart health, routine screenings, chronic back pain or would like to schedule some one-on-one time with one of our providers, call the clinic at (970) 774-6187.
In addition to hearing from several wonderful speakers organizers also use this time to celebrate and lift up the women in the community with the Wellness for Women Award. The Wellness for Women Award honors individuals who positively impact the mental or physical health of women in our community, either by being outstanding wellness role models or overcoming their own health challenges. Each January, an anonymous committee reviews the nominations and selects the recipient. This year, we had four incredible nominees who exemplify inspiration, grit, and dedication: Jessie Cochran, Wendy Evans, Linda Falk and Salix Gurnsey.
• Cochran demonstrates dedication to wellness through her coaching, nursing career, and encouragement through various health/weight loss challenges she sponsors among the Haxtun Health team. Her compassionate approach and commitment to professional and personal growth continues to have a positive impact on our region.
• Evans exhibits tremendous commitment to wellness and unwavering support for others, even in the midst of fighting her own health battles. She hosts numerous classes to help others achieve their health goals. Her resilience, kindness and expertise have profoundly impacted countless lives.
• Falk's dedication to her profession and community has significantly impacted many lives. She continuously thinks outside of the box to ensure her patients are taken care of. She walks alongside them during their journey to health ensuring they receive the best care possible.
• Gurnsey's exceptional massage therapy practice has greatly enhanced the community's well-being. Her dedication to helping people feel good in their skin and body reflects her genuine commitment to improving mental, physical and nutritional health.
At the end of the night, the Wellness for Women Award was presented to Evans in honor of her widespread influence on the Haxtun community and surrounding areas.
Haxtun Health eagerly anticipates hosting this event each year. It is a cherished time when women can connect with one another in the community while gaining valuable insights into health and optimal wellness. This event serves as a poignant reminder that none of us are alone, and there are exceptional resources available right here at Haxtun Health.

title: Looking at effects of ADHD in adulthood
author: Sara Huss Haxtun Health
description: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder isn't just a childhood issue—it persists into adulthood, affecting millions worldwide. Let's delve deeper into this complex condition and explore its impact on…
content: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder isn't just a childhood issue—it persists into adulthood, affecting millions worldwide. Let's delve deeper into this complex condition and explore its impact on adults. Together, we will look at treatments and tools to encourage productivity. The science behind ADHD ADHD involves structural and functional differences in the brain. Neurotransmitters like dopamine play a crucial role in attention regulation. Another contributor is your genetics. ADHD tends to run in families. There are also environmental factors to consider. The three faces of ADHD First, we have the Inattentive Type. This type will struggle with forgetfulness, disorganization and will get lost in daydreams. Next, we have the Hyperactive-Impulsive Type. This is the restless, impulsive, filter-less type that can't seem to sit still. Lastly, we have the Combined Type — it's the blend of distractedness and hyperactivity. Fleeting focus Those with ADHD struggle to focus. Focusing on mundane tasks feels like herding cats. To be successful and productive it helps to break tasks into smaller chunks. Using tools such as planners, sticky notes and timers can set them up for success. Structured routines have been proven to help those who are struggling. Amid the whirlwind of thoughts, mindfulness offers an anchor. Impulsive decisions Impulsivity, a pillar of ADHD, manifests as spontaneous actions without consideration of the consequences. What is the science behind impulsiveness? It is linked to the 'happy' hormones, Dopamine and Serotonin. Dopamine is the motivational coach, urging action. Serotonin is the Zen monk, signaling contentment and restraint. ADHD causes the delicate levels of Dopamine and Serotonin to become imbalanced, leading to procrastination and indecision letting impulsive thoughts take center stage. The time warp Those that struggle with ADHD have a different perception of time. Minutes can feel like hours when their thoughts are distracted. Hours can fly by once they are hyper focused on a project. New ideas can capture their full attention causing them to be enveloped by them. Hyperfocus heights Now, it's important to recognize that not all aspects of ADHD are bad or should be looked at negatively. Those with ADHD have an astounding capability to hyperfocus on subjects and problems. When they hone-in on this superpower they can leverage the hyperactivity to achieve productivity. The difficulty presents itself in finding the balance between intense concentration and the difficulty of focusing on the task at hand. Rapid-fire Emotions People diagnosed with ADHD often experience intense emotions. They can fall victim to emotional dysregulation which includes outbursts, frustration and heightened stress. This imbalance affects relationships with friends, family and colleagues. While ADHD isn't a mood disorder, its impact on emotions is significant. Seeking professional guidance and practicing coping techniques can make the emotional journey more manageable. Treatment options ADHD can be managed with various treatment options. Let's quickly look at a couple of options. Medication is widely available and used to help manage symptoms of ADHD. There are two different types of medications that are prescribed; stimulants such as Adderall and non-stimulant medications like Wellbutrin. However, medication isn't always for everyone. Another treatment one might pursue is Behavioral Therapy. Structured counseling can help manage behavior and improve thinking patterns. Other treatments include the application of many behavioral strategies, adjusting lifestyle and routines. These strategies may incorporate time management techniques, organizational skills, a healthy diet, avoiding sugary treats and caffeine, and adopting an exercise regimen. It's important to work with your primary care physician to develop an individualized plan that works best for you. It's possible to reach your goals of productivity. Haxtun Health works alongside individuals that may be struggling to get where they want to be in their health journey. Hopes are to help patients reach their optimal wellness. To schedule a time to visit with one of our trusted providers call (970) 774-6187. Appointments are available in Fleming and Haxtun.

title: Frechman BOE renews Firme's contract for 2024-25
author: Candie Fix Managing Editor
description: An hour-long March meeting of the Frenchman Board of Education focused on preparing for the upcoming year. Following administration reports, board members voted to approve Principal Kortney Firme's…
content:
An hour-long March meeting of the Frenchman Board of Education focused on preparing for the upcoming year. Following administration reports, board members voted to approve Principal Kortney Firme's contract and salary schedules for Fleming in 2024-25.
In her report to the Board, Firme gave an update on spring sporting events, field trips, concerts and contests. She said plans are in the works for end-of-year assessments. Looking forward, the Principal is focusing on the student handbook and registration, which will be online for next year.
Superintendent Steve McCracken said the District canceled the junior varsity baseball schedule and three students are participating at Caliche this season. He also talked about two bills regarding conceal carry in schools that are making their way through the legislative process at the Capitol. Fleming Schools is one of several in Colorado which arms staff on school premises.
In approving the consent agenda, board members approved canceling school on March 7 due to hazardous driving conditions.
Later, in action items, board members voted to approve Firme's contract for the coming year. No other changes were made to her contract, which is renewed on a year-to-year basis, McCracken said in later follow up.
The Board also voted to approve the 2024-25 certified and classified salary schedules.
'The base salary on our certified salary schedule was increased from $38,000 to $40,000,' McCracken said. 'The classified schedule was not changed. We amended the classified schedule in January as result of the increase in the minimum wage for Colorado.'
The 2024-25 Extra Duty Salary Schedule was also listed on the agenda under action items but was tabled until April.
'We want to add assistant junior high coaches salary, cross country and E-sports coach's salary,' said McCracken.
The next Frenchman Board of Education meeting is slated for April 11 at 7 p.m. in the Fleming School/Community Library.

title: Ruth Laverne Starkebaum
description: Ruth Starkebaum, affectionately known as Laverne, was born on Oct. 1, 1929 to Ruth and Carl Englehart at Cortez. Our Heavenly Father called Laverne home on March 5, 2024 at the age of 94. She died at…
content:
Ruth Laverne Starkebaum
Ruth Starkebaum, affectionately known as Laverne, was born on Oct. 1, 1929 to Ruth and Carl Englehart at Cortez. Our Heavenly Father called Laverne home on March 5, 2024 at the age of 94. She died at home surrounded by family and her caregiver.
Laverne attended schools in the Lewis/Cortez area, followed by studying at the University of Northern Colorado until her marriage to Clark Starkebaum on Aug. 14, 1949, after meeting on a blind date. She attended Colorado State University until Clark's graduation, finishing a semester short of her degree. Clark and Laverne farmed for many years east of Haxtun with his father and later with their son, John. Clark and Laverne were also business owners operating the Haxtun Locker Plant for a number of years. Laverne also raised dogs. They moved into Haxtun in 1997.
Laverne was involved with numerous civic organizations in the community. She was a member of the Haxtun United Methodist Church where she served on committees, was active in the ladies auxiliary and taught Sunday school. She was a member of PEO and served on the Haxtun Town Board. One of her proudest accomplishments was as a hospice volunteer bringing words of comfort and encouragement along with a hug to those in need.
Laverne's family was the joy of her life and she took great pride in supporting her children and grandchildren in their varied activities. Clark and Laverne attended hundreds of sporting events, along with school concerts and activities. She served many years as a room mother, and along with Clark, they were frequent class parent sponsors. During the summers they would watch their family's livestock and horse shows at local and state fairs. Clark and Laverne were honored as Grand Marshals of the Haxtun Corn Festival parade and the Phillips County Fair parade.
Laverne was a strong woman. She did it all, from farm hand, vet, chief cook to family peacekeeper. Her respite was Sunday night when it was popcorn and pop, a tradition that continues. She was a loving wife, mother and friend. She was quick witted and a patient listener. She told wonderful stories. She was warm and welcoming to strangers and always willing to help a neighbor. She was the rock of the family.
Laverne is survived by four of her five children including Deborah and husband Rick, John and wife Julia, Steven and Kari; sister Karla Wiescamp; 16 grandchildren and 18 great-grandchildren. Colleen Jedlicka and Roxanne Martinez were her caregivers.
Laverne is preceded in death by her husband Clark; son Larry; daughter-in-law Debbi; and brothers Stanton, James and Charles.
Memorials can be directed to St. Jude Children's Hospital, the Haxtun United Methodist Church Memorial Fund or Hospice of the Plains.
A celebration of life will be held on April 13 at 10:30 a.m. at the Haxtun United Methodist Church with internment following at the Haxtun Cemetery. The service will be officiated by Pastor Jeri Soens.
The service will be live streamed at Baucke Funeral Home website - look for Ruth Laverne Starkebaum obituary, there will be a link at the top of the obituary.
Baucke Funeral Home is in charge of arrangements.

title: Bulldogs take 4 of 5 last week; advance to 8-4 overall
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Haxtun Bulldogs took a win in four of their last five outings. Over the past week, Haxtun took on Otis, Merino and Sedgwick County, all on the road. As of mid-week, the Bulldogs hold an overall 8-4 record. The Bulldogs kicked off their road series at Otis last Thursday. The visiting team put two runs on the board in the first, five in the fourth and four in the fifth for an 11-1 win in five...
content:
The Haxtun Bulldogs took a win in four of their last five outings. Over the past week, Haxtun took on Otis, Merino and Sedgwick County, all on the road. As of mid-week, the Bulldogs hold an overall 8-4 record.
The Bulldogs kicked off their road series at Otis last Thursday. The visiting team put two runs on the board in the first, five in the fourth and four in the fifth for an 11-1 win in five innings.
Madden Larsen and Colin Cone led at the plate, both batting 1.000. Cone hit a home run giving him three runs-batted-in, the team high. Larsen tallied two RBIs and Kaiden Schelling registered one. On the mound, Kanin Koberstein took the win. The sophomore pitcher struck out three of nine batters. Schelling also pitched for the Bulldogs; he sat down four of eight batters.
Saturday pitted the Bulldogs on the road to Merino for a double-header with the Rams. Haxtun picked up the early lead, putting one run on the board in the top of the second and another in the top of the third. The home team Rams added two runs in the bottom of the third to tie the contest at two all. Merino added three runs on the board in the third to take their first advantage. The Bulldogs answered back with three runs in the top of the seventh but the home team's last chance at bat gave the Rams a single run to take the win, 6-5.
Grant Statz batted 1.000 in the first contest with Merino. Koberstein registered a .667 average at the plate. Koberstein also tallied two RBIs.
Both Schelling and Koberstein threw for the Bulldogs. Schelling saw 14 batters, sitting down three. Koberstein sat down one of 16 batters.
The second contest against the Rams went to the Bulldogs as the visiting team put four runs on the board in the second, four in the fifth and one in the seventh. Haxtun earned the 9-6 victory following a seven inning contest.
Schelling led his team at the plate going .667 in game two. Cone and Ryland Wolff each batted .500. Larsen earned a .400 average followed by Statz and Mason Bornhoft, both going .333 at home plate. Cone led in RBIs with two.
Larsen earned the win on the mound. He struck out six of 29 batters.
The Bulldogs hit the road again on Monday, this time north to face off with Sedgwick County. Haxtun took a 17-5 win in game one and an 11-4 victory in game two for a sweep over the Cougars.
According to information on MaxPreps, Merino currently leads the Lower Platte League with a 6-0 record. Akron comes in second at 5-1, Yuma sits third with a 3-1 league record and the Bulldogs hold the fourth seat at 4-3.
This week Haxtun is set to face Wray at home on Friday. Double-header action starts at 2 p.m. Two double-headers remain on the schedule following the Wray match up including those against Akron and Caliche next week.

title: PCFES dedicates Hall of Education to Shirley Krogmeier on April 18
description: Family, friends and staff gathered at Phillips County Family Education Services on April 18 to celebrate the dedication of the Shirley Krogmeier Hall of Education. This honor was given in recognition…
content:
(Courtesy photo)
PHILLIPS County Family Education Services recently honored Shirley Krogmeier for her dedication to the County. Pictured above are Linda Jelden, Director of PCFES, Bill Krogmeier, Dolores Haskell and Tiffany Watson PCFS Board Chair.
Family, friends and staff gathered at Phillips County Family Education Services on April 18 to celebrate the dedication of the Shirley Krogmeier Hall of Education. This honor was given in recognition of Shirley Krogmeier who touched the lives of countless students and families through education.
Linda Jelden, Executive Director of PCFES, summarized the career and achievements of this dedicated educator and expressed gratitude for her significant contributions to the organization. Krogmeier entered the teaching profession with a degree in English, Literature and German from the University of Colorado and a master's degree in German and Education from the University of Minnesota. Her teaching career began in 1956 as an elementary teacher in Amherst and concluded as a GED instructor in Holyoke in 2017. Between her work in Amherst and Holyoke, Shirley literally circled the globe through France, Germany (Rhode Scholar Teacher Exchange), Thailand and numerous schools in Colorado, Minnesota and South Dakota. She taught English, German and geography at several junior and senior high schools, coordinated Title IV ESL/Bilingual grants, developed curriculum and trained ESL teachers overseas and taught evening ESL classes.
Shirley believed the basis of all continuing education throughout life was a high school diploma or a general education diploma. She served as a GED instructor at PCFES from 2007 to 2017. Former colleagues noted that she set the pace of teaching with encouragement and student accountability and she was exceptionally proud of each of her students. In 2015 she received the Employee of the Year Community Excellence Award from the Holyoke Chamber of Commerce. Known for her lifelong service to others, she shared her passion for education through her teaching and also with a generous estate gift to PCFES. The philanthropic impact of this gift will last for generations with a partnership with the Eastern Colorado Community Fund. This mission to continue adult education and family literacy support in Phillips County will proudly continue as it has for over 30 years.
Special guests at the dedication included Shirley's siblings, Bill Krogmeier and Dolores Haskell, both of Holyoke. Bill Krogmeier handcrafted the dedication plaque which is now displayed in the PCFES hallway. John Chapdelaine and Brenda Brandt, representing the Eastern Colorado Community Fund, also attended. The community is invited to visit the Phillips County Family Education Services office to view the Hall of Education featuring program highlights and acknowledgement of donors.

title: Seger signs for softball with LCC
author: Candie Fix Managing Editor
description: Haxtun senior Samantha Seger signed a letter of intent to play softball at Lamar Community College next fall. Seger sealed her commitment with friends and family by her side in signing ceremonies at…
content:
(Herald photo by Candie Fix)
SAMANTHA SEGER, middle front, signed a letter of intent to play softball at Lamar Community College last week. With her are, front left mother Sharon Seger and Holyoke Softball Head Coach Kendra Schlachter, front right; back row (l-r), brothers Seth and Stellan Seger, dad Dustin Seger and Haxtun Athletic Director Don Myers.
Haxtun senior Samantha Seger signed a letter of intent to play softball at Lamar Community College next fall. Seger sealed her commitment with friends and family by her side in signing ceremonies at Haxtun High School last week. Seger played four softball seasons with the Lady Dragons in Holyoke.
"Samantha has a great personality and loves the game of softball, said Greg Cary, Softball Coach of the Lamar Lady Running Lopes. "She will bring that personality with her and also her athleticism to help us offensively."
In her time with the Lady Dragons, Seger earned a .450 batting average and a .530 on base percentage. She registered 77 hits, 38 runs batted in and 79 runs. Seger also boasts a .904 fielding percentage.
In her high school career, Seger played first base primarily but also spent some time on third base.
As a senior, Seger helped lead her team to the 2023 3A State Softball Tournament. The Lady Dragons finished with an overall 12-12 record.
"She will compete for a spot in the infield and give us whatever she can," Cary said of Seger's position on the college team next year. He added that qualities that will make her an asset to the Lopes team include her energy, passion and competitiveness on the field.
While playing for the Lopes, Seger plans to study nursing in hopes of becoming a hospice nurse.
Seger is the daughter of Dustin and Sharon Seger and the granddaughter of Darwin and Ellie Jeffers and Leland and Pauline Seger, all of Haxtun.

title: HH partners with HPRN to offer training on mental health conversations
author: From Haxtun Health
description: Haxtun Health, in partnership with the High Plains Research Network is hosting a free COMET training on Wednesday, June 12, from 12-1:30 p.m. at the Haxtun Community Center at 125 East Wilson Street…
content:
Haxtun Health, in partnership with the High Plains Research Network is hosting a free COMET training on Wednesday, June 12, from 12-1:30 p.m. at the Haxtun Community Center at 125 East Wilson Street in Haxtun.
COMET (Changing Our Mental and Emotional Trajectory) is a unique program developed in rural eastern Colorado. It equips community members with seven simple guiding questions to initiate conversations about mental and emotional well-being with someone they might be concerned about.
'We all know that mental health is just as important as physical health,' says Julia Biesemeier, CCRO at Haxtun Health. 'This training provides participants with the tools and confidence to have caring conversations that can make a real difference in someone's life.'
The COMET training is designed for anyone who wants to feel more comfortable talking about mental health. It is ideal for community members, educators, business owners, agricultural workers, veterans and anyone who interacts with others on a regular basis.
Benefits of attending
the COMET training:
• Learn the seven COMET questions to initiate supportive conversations
• Gain confidence in approaching someone you're concerned about
• Understand how to listen actively and offer support
• Discover resources available in your community
Lunch will be provided for those participating. RSVP to [email protected] or call Julia Biesemeier at (970) 774-6123. Together, we can create a more supportive environment for mental health in Haxtun.

title: Dr. Dana Morgan comes to Haxtun Health
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Dana Morgan, MD, has over 30 years of experience as a primary care physician. She began her training in Microbiology at the University of Montana in 1983 and once she earned her bachelor's she headed…
content:
(Courtesy photo) count
(Courtesy photo) count HAXTUN HEALTH'S new provider and others from the organization (l-r), Morgen Budde, PA, Monica Schmidt, RN, Krystle Magaña, RN, Dana Morgan, MD.
Dana Morgan, MD, has over 30 years of experience as a primary care physician. She began her training in Microbiology at the University of Montana in 1983 and once she earned her bachelor's she headed west to University of Washington in Seattle, earning her Doctor of Medicine degree in 1993. In 1993, she began her residency in Fort Collins, which led to her fondness for Colorado. She even spent time working along the eastern plains at Yuma District Hospital from 1997-1999, which showed her a different side of Colorado. Since her time on the eastern plains, she has spent most of her adult life in and around the Front Range practicing medicine, raising her family and co-founding her own practice.
Dr. Morgan was a co-founder of Balance Health in Greeley Colorado, a Family Practice Direct Primary Care facility. Dr. Dana continued further and founded another FPDPC, H.O.P.E., in 2022. H.O.P.E. stands for Hormone Optimization Practice and Esthetics where she focuses on a persons' hormone levels.
When you get the chance to meet Dr. Dana, you will see just how passionate she is about overall wellness. She treats patients of all ages.
"I provide family medicine services for patients of all ages including well-women checks, well-child checks and sports physicals," Dr. Dana said,
The team at Haxtun Health couldn't be more excited to welcome her to the campus. Her knowledge and expertise will benefit the entire community. Dr. Dana joined the Haxtun Health team at their annual Health Fair on June 1, where she met more of the team she will be working with and many community members who attended the fair. While at the Health Fair, she volunteered at the skin check station, where she examined several patients concerned about abnormal spots on their bodies. In June, she will start seeing patients three days a week once credentialing has been completed.
"We are thrilled to have Dr. Dana Morgan here in Haxtun," said Dewane Pace, Haxtun Health CEO. "She has a skill set that is highly sought after by those who call Northeastern Colorado 'home.' We are excited to bring her knowledge to Haxtun, Fleming and the surrounding areas. She is excited to land here in town and dive into patient care as quickly as possible. With her addition, we will be able to provide more consistent care in both Fleming and Haxtun."
Providers at Haxtun Health
Haxtun Health has a well-rounded team of providers. Our providers take an interest in our guests' lives. When you choose Haxtun Health, you are choosing to be more than just a chart. At Haxtun Health, you get to be in charge of your own health. Call to schedule an appointment today at (970) 774-6187.

title: Sallie Munson
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Sallie Munson passed away on June 24, 2024 at the Sedgwick County Nursing Home in Julesburg at the age of 98. Sallie was born on Aug. 22, 1925 in Norphlet, Ark., the daughter of W.H. Murphy and Maggie…
content:
count
Sallie Munson
Sallie Munson passed away on June 24, 2024 at the Sedgwick County Nursing Home in Julesburg at the age of 98.
Sallie was born on Aug. 22, 1925 in Norphlet, Ark., the daughter of W.H. Murphy and Maggie Elva Sullivan. She grew up in a large family with three sisters and six brothers. Sallie attended school in Norphlet, graduating in 1942. After high school, she attended secretarial school in El Dorado, Ark. In 1944, she went to work for a local lawyer for a short time, then went to work for the War Dept. in Washington, D.C. In 1944, while on the train to Washington, D.C., she met a soldier from Sedgwick who was stationed on the East Coast. That meeting would change her life forever.
Sallie married that soldier, 2nd Lt. Layton Munson, in her hometown of Norphlet, on Nov. 4, 1944. She continued working for the War Dept. while Layton returned to Army duty with the Signal Corp on the East Coast. Layton was sent overseas six weeks after marriage, serving in England, France and Germany.
After Layton returned from the war in September 1945, the couple could finally start their married life together. They returned to Sedgwick and bought the farm that adjoined his birthplace on the high hill five miles south of Sedgwick. They resided on their farm for the next 69 years and became parents to five children: twins Sharon and Shirley were born in 1947, Joan in 1948, Janet in 1950 and Swain in 1953.
Sallie was a member of the Prairie View Club on the South Table during the 1950s. She was a member of the Sedgwick Presbyterian Church, the center of her life. She was a Sunday School teacher and Supt. of the Sunday School for many years. Sallie was an active Presbyterian Women's Association member, holding many positions over the years. Besides raising her family and church activities, Sallie enjoyed sewing, doing hand work and embroidery, quilting, gardening and tending her flowers.
Layton and Sallie enjoyed many trips over the years, mainly back to Arkansas to visit Sallie's family, but also trips west to California, where Layton had participated in Mojave Desert maneuvers during WWII and Louisiana.
Sallie is survived by her children Sharon and husband Rich Cobourn, Powell, Wyo., Shirley Salyards, Sedgwick, Joan and husband Darrel Salyards, Cheyenne, Wyo., Janet McGaughey and spouse Jim Long, La Junta, and Swain Munson, Sedgwick. Sallie's legacy also lives on in her large family of 11 grandchildren, 24 great-grandchildren, 14 great-great-grandchildren; brother-in-law Charles Bales, Arkansas, along with many nieces and nephews. The strength of these family ties is a testament to the love and unity that Sallie fostered.
Sallie is preceded in death by her husband Layton in March 2016; grandson Michael McGaughey; son-in-law; parents; six brothers and three sisters.
Funeral services were held June 28 at Well Of Hope Church in Julesburg with Pastor Larry Nail officiating. Interment followed at the Sedgwick Cemetery.
In lieu of flowers, memorials may be made to either Sedgwick County Nursing Home or the Sedgwick Presbyterian Church. Condolences may be shared at prairiehillsjulesburg.com.
Prairie Hills Funeral Home of Julesburg is in charge of arrangements.

Fleming School is adding a Construction Trades program for high school students. The addition of construction course work comes following a vote in a late-June meeting by the Board of Education.
According to Superintendent Steve McCracken, the construction trades class will teach students the skills needed to enter the carpentry industry. Students will learn all phases of residential home construction including foundation preparation, framing, electrical, plumbing and finish work.
"We are excited to see the program get started," McCracken said.
Nate Japp will serve as the instructor for the newly added construction trades program in Fleming.
In the same June meeting, board members approved an invoice from Code Red Audits for $17,954. That, McCracken said, is for the installation of new security cameras throughout the building. In a meeting the month before, the Board agreed to purchase the new cameras from Verkada for $31,000.
McCracken said the cameras system is being installed now. The project includes new, upgraded security cameras with the option to add more in the future. The Superintendent is in the process of applying for grant funds to help with the cost of the system and installation.
The monthly meeting, that lasted only an hour, also included staff reports and the approval of the consent agenda.
In her report, Principal Kortney Firme said the master class schedule is complete and that students would be in to register soon.
McCracken told the Board, in his report, that the District purchased some equipment for the kitchen form a restaurant that recently went out of business. He said the District purchased a six-burner gas stove, a halo slow cooker, flat griddle and other miscellaneous items including silverware and storage containers.
In other business the Board:
• Approved the resignation of Jeneva Withers as an assistant cook;
• Added Kally Kirkwood as a substitute teacher;
• Approve the 2024-25 budget with appropriations;
• Approved an engagement letter with Scott Szabo to conduct the annual audit.
The next Frenchman Board of Education meeting is slated for July 25 in Fleming at 6:30 p.m.

title: 37th annual Old-Fashioned Saturday Night set for July 20

content:
It's mid-July and that means Haxtun's Old-Fashioned Saturday Night is just around the corner. The 37th annual event is slated for Saturday, July 20 in downtown Haxtun and promises the popular car show as well as town-wide garage sales, poker run, vendors, burnout competition, valve cover races, beer garden and more.
Saturday morning's activities kick off with town-wide garage sales. Thus far, more than 33 locations have registered to host garage sales around Haxtun. Maps for garage sale sites will be available the day of at Haxtun Super's and Zip Trip.
To register your sale, contact Chris Kuehn at (970) 580-9101 or visit welcometohaxtun.com.
The Poker Run will take off from the Haxtun Fire Hall at 11 a.m. Riders should be registered by 10:45 a.m. The run will begin in Haxtun and take riders throughout northeastern Colorado before the final card is drawn back in Haxtun. Prizes will be awarded for the top three bikers.
Proceeds from this year's run will benefit the Haxtun Park Disk Golf Course.
Action downtown kicks off in the afternoon featuring vendors, tricycle races and valve cover races. Registration for valve cover races as well as vendor registration can be found at visit welcometohaxtun.com.
Official rules for the Valve Cover races are available on the Old-Fashioned Saturday Night Facebook page and at town hall. The self-built, unmotorized cars will race on a track from Northeastern Junior College.
Car show registration begins at 2 p.m. in downtown Haxtun. The car show is set for 3-7 p.m. and will feature awards for People's Choice, Rodder's Choice, Mayor's Choice and Best Golf Cart. This year's awards will be custom created and donated by Gordon's Upholstery. All types of vehicles are welcome.
'We are asking for pre-registrations so we can get a rough estimate of how many cars we will have,' said Chamber Director Jessica Ayala. However, same day registration will be available.
The Haxtun Fire Hall will be the site for the annual burnout competition at 6:30 p.m. The burn out boasts $1,000 in prizes and is sponsored by Wilson's Repair, Haxtun Locker Plant, SmokeTrails, S&W Auto Supply-Napa and G&S Sandblasting and Fabrication. Cash prizes will be awarded to the top five winners, trophies will be given to the top three. Registration for the event will be at the Haxtun Fire Hall.
Throughout the event, Miss Dottie VonVelvet and the Luscious Ladies plan to host a Queen of the Car Show Contest. Entrants are asked to arrive hair and make-up ready and dressed in their favorite era. Those participating in the contest should register at the same location as the car show registration no later than 5 p.m.
Winners will be picked based on best dressed, stage presence and how well questions are answered. Each entrant will be provided a question at check in to prepare their answers. Titles and prizes will be awarded to the top three in each category including Queen and Princess. The queen contest is ages 15 and up and Princess is 14 and under. To register or find out more information, visit welcometohaxtun.com.
Queen of the Car Show, Princess of the Car Show and car show awards will be announced immediately after the burn out.
Other activities include kiddie land from 4-8 p.m., the annual hog roast sponsored by the Haxtun Volunteer Fireman from 5-7 p.m. and beer garden with a DJ from 4 p.m. to midnight.
The sign-up sheet to volunteer to help serve and run the gate at the beer garden is on the Old-Fashioned Saturday Night Facebook page or can be found by contacting Chamber Director Jessica Ayala at (970) 466-5540. You can also email [email protected] to get on the list.
