title: Bulldog basketball set to face Sedg.Co.
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Haxtun Bulldogs are set to compete in the Holiday Tournament at Northeastern Junior College this week. Teams should see play Thursday, Friday and Saturday before heading into a two-week break for…
content:
The Haxtun Bulldogs are set to compete in the Holiday Tournament at Northeastern Junior College this week. Teams should see play Thursday, Friday and Saturday before heading into a two-week break for Christmas and New Year's. The Bulldogs hold a 1-2 record heading into tournament play following a 66-30 loss at Highland over the weekend.
Saturday's action pitted the Bulldogs against a higher classified Highland Huskies in Ault. The night before, Highland took down Merino 64-28.
The Huskies' starting five flaunts players six feet and above who took a noteworthy advantage over the Bulldogs. Highland's full-court press paired with a fast-paced offense made for a 33-19 home team advantage at the half. Despite attempts to slow the game down and handle the ball with better control, the Bulldogs fell by 36 in their only outing last weekend.
"In the first half we did a good job getting into our offenses and executing. Defensively we played pretty well, but struggled finishing possessions with a rebound," Bulldog Head Coach Jayden Stieb said in a re-cap of his team's performance. "The biggest stat that stood out was rebounding. Highland secured 70 percent of their defensive rebounds while we were just over 50. They controlled the glass throughout the game. With bigger players across from us we need to do a better job fighting for position and getting rebounds."
According to stats from the book provided by Stieb, junior guard Chase Goddard led the Bulldog offense with 12 points on Saturday. Junior Colin Cone put five points on the board followed by Kanin Koberstein with four points. Senior Ryland Wolff registered three points, as did senior Tate Michael, followed by Jaxsen Schram with two points and Madden Larsen with one.
This week the Bulldogs will face Sedgwick County in day one action of the annual Holiday Tournament. That game is set to be played on Thursday evening at 7 p.m. According to MaxPreps, the Cougars are undefeated at 3-0 early this season. Over the past two weeks, Sedgwick County picked up wins over Fleming, South Platte and Wiggins.
"These three games are the most important we've had. Our previous three, we played some good competition, but we've yet to play a team in our classification. This week we have a good chance of not only playing thee teams in our classification, but three teams in our league. I'm excited to see how we perform. As a team we've been looking forward to this tournament since our first practice," Stieb said.
A win puts the Bulldogs on the court at 8:30 p.m. on Friday night, a loss would set the team up for a 1:30 p.m. Friday contest. Game play continues into Saturday depending on the outcome of matches the day before.
"In our two losses we've struggled with turnovers and rebounding. That's something we need to get fixed. Cleaning up those two areas of the game will be our main focus," said Stieb. "I'm really happy with how guys handled these first two weeks. Obviously there are a few things to clean up, but given the circumstances, I like where we're at as a team."

title: Bullard moved to Sgt.; Smith named Interim Chief
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Haxtun Town Council made significant changes to the structure of Haxtun Police Department personnel in a Monday night, Jan. 6 meeting. The Council voted to appoint Darrell Smith as Interim Police…
content:
(Herald photo by Candie Fix) count
DARRELL SMITH took an oath of office to serve as Interim Chief of Police at the Haxtun Town Hall on Monday evening, Jan. 6. Mayor Mike Ensminger administered the oath of office.
The Haxtun Town Council made significant changes to the structure of Haxtun Police Department personnel in a Monday night, Jan. 6 meeting. The Council voted to appoint Darrell Smith as Interim Police Chief. Smith took his oath of office the same evening.
The January meeting opened with regular business, in which two of the four action items listed on the agenda related to changes in the local police department. Council members voted to appoint Smith to the Interim Chief position while also addressing next steps to fill the lead role permanently.
Mayor Mike Ensminger said the need to make changes stems from a recent executive session and due to former Chief Tom Bullard expressing his interest in seeking other employment. The Council held a special meeting to enter into executive session in late December to discuss matters related to police department personnel. That meeting lasted just over an hour and no further discussion or action was taken following the closed-door meeting.
Over the past few weeks, Ensminger said he spoke with Smith, who agreed to fill in the Chief role for the time being. Smith has served as an officer with the Haxtun Police Department, working under Bullard as Chief, since September 2022.
Along with the decision to appoint Smith as Interim Chief, the Council voted to move Bullard to a Sergeant position; one he held before being appointed Chief in 2023. The changes in title also means a change in salary. As Chief, Bullard's salary was set at $66,560 per year. In changing ranks to Sergeant, the Council opted to change Bullard's annual salary to $55,000. When he was a sergeant in 2023, Bullard was taking in $48,000 per year. Bullard has been with the local police department for 12 years, beginning as an officer.
Over the past few months, in efforts to find a third officer for the local police department, the Council has reviewed data from other area agencies and made necessary changes to bring the department's wages within a competitive range.
The promotion to Interim Chief will bring on a significantly new role for Smith and along with that, the Council opted to increase his annual salary. As an officer, Smith's salary was set at $53,000 per year. On Monday night, after some discussion, council members voted to increase that number to $60,000.
Moving forward, the Council opted to form a police chief hiring committee, which will include Council Members Ryan Horton and Jon Brammer along with others with law enforcement backgrounds including former council member Rob Martinez, Colorado State Patrol Trooper Marc Bornhoft, former Colorado State Patrol Trooper Brandon Biesemeier and Holyoke Police Chief Doug Bergstrom. The committee plans to meet soon to go over the current job description and sample listing of the job announcement for posting. Once all necessary paperwork is in line, plans are to move forward in posting the open position and seek applications.
Council member Horton thanked Smith for his willingness to step up and fill the Interim Chief role and told him moving forward, he sees the Council being more involved and helping when they can.
"No one's going to stick their nose where it doesn't belong, but we plan to be a little bit more involved," Horton said. "That way things won't slip by and we have these issues again."
Later, during staff reports, Smith gave an overview of the Haxtun Police Department's stats for 2024. Total calls for service last year was 1,022 and includes 28 citations, six misdemeanor arrests, six felony arrests, 12 accidents, six fire calls and 73 medical assists. Calls for service increased from 2023 by 79.
As an update in the search of a third officer, Smith said the department recently received two applications and interviews were set up with both parties. One, he said, ended up having to cancel due to a doctor's appointment and the other was interviewed by a selected panel. Smith said he has some reservations about the individual interviewed and their potential to stay long term.
Smith also told the Council he plans to increase transparency with the department and council members while he is in the lead role. In doing so, he plans to attend all Council meetings and meet regularly with Mayor Ensminger.
In her report, Clerk Kelsey Harms said she and Superintendent Ron Carpenter recently requested funds from the Phillips County Rec District to finish construction at the basketball court near the new pool. The Rec District awarded the Town of Haxtun just over $5,000 to paint basketball and pickle ball lines, purchase a pickle ball net, trash cans and bleachers.
In other business the Council:
• Designated the front door of the Town Hall as the designated public posting location for 2025. All meeting notices will be posted on the front door of town hall;
• Designated Carpenter as the Town's Colorado Association of Municipal Utilities. Dave Green will serve as an alternate;
• Approved the following building permits: Marilyn Michael, 120 North Lava Avenue to replace siding; Haxtun Hospital, 235 West Fletcher Street to replace windows; Steven Wright, 205 South Washington Avenue for a re-roof and to remove/replace existing solar panels.

title: SC/F wrestlers compete at 62nd annual Bob Smith Invitational to close out 2024
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The 62nd Annual Bob Smith Invitational Wrestling Tournament, held recently, saw a strong showing from the Sedgwick County-Fleming wrestling team earning multiple podium finishes. Grant Firme took…
content:
The 62nd Annual Bob Smith Invitational Wrestling Tournament, held recently, saw a strong showing from the Sedgwick County-Fleming wrestling team earning multiple podium finishes.
Grant Firme took sixth at 120 pounds. He had a challenging run in his class but finished strong with a earning 11 team points. Firme began with a quick win by fall over Zack Confer of Dayspring Christian Academy, but was pinned by Drew Godsey of Wray in the quarterfinals. He earned a win by fall over Kace Chamberlain of Wray in the consolation round before being edged out in a sudden victory loss to Raegan Torres of Akron in the semifinals. Firme's tournament ended with a 2:01 fall loss to Traysen Rosane of Holyoke in the fifth place match.
Maddox Herskind faced stiff competition at 132 pounds, and although his results did not see him place, he earned 4 team points. Herskind began his tournament with a tough 18-1 loss to Merek Charney of Akron, but found success in the second round, pinning Danny Sontay of Limon High School. He was eliminated after a quick fall by Kaleb Grauer of Akron.
Scotty Engle claimed fourth at 144 pounds. He made a strong push to the podium, earning 16 team points. Engle opened with a pin over Dillon Keller of St. Francis HS/Bird City-Cheylin HS and a hard-fought 7-5 win over Atlas Grosch of Chatfield in the quarterfinals. Engle was then pinned by Andrew Buoy of Wray in the semifinals. He continued to fight in the consolation rounds, pinning Tayshaun Thomas of Akron, but lost to Atlas Grosch of Chatfield in the third place match by decision.
Austin Knox also claimed a fourth place finish. He competed in the in the 150-pound class, contributing 16 team points. Knox received a bye in the first round and then won by fall over Shiloh Dellamia-van Overmeiren of Chatfield in the quarterfinals. After being pinned by Logan Clark of Dayspring Christian Academy in the semifinals, Knox earned a win by fall over Owen Erker of Wiggins School District in the consolation round but fell short in the third place match against Isaac Coronado of Chatfield.
Ryan Davis fought valiantly in the 175-pound bracket, finishing in sixth and earning 11 team points. Davis started with an impressive fall over Wyatt Kapke of Chatfield, but was defeated by his teammate, Levi Reichman, in the quarterfinals. He earned two more wins, including a pin over Aiden Mayer of Wiggins School District, but was eliminated by Zach Carr of Limon High School in the consolation semifinals. Davis ended his tournament with a medical forfeit in the fifth place match.
The SC/F wrestlers finished fifth as a team with several standout performances. Nathan Gonzales, Owen Harris, and Levi Reichman were particularly impressive, each securing third place finishes in their respective weight classes. While some wrestlers faced tough competition, the team's overall effort demonstrated their growth and potential heading into the remainder of the season.
The squad is scheduled to compete in a dual at Yuma on Thursday, Jan. 9 and the Garden County Invitational on Saturday, Jan. 11 at Oshkosh. Saturday's matches begin at 9 a.m.

title: Fleming seeks first season victories on home court this weekend
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Fleming Wildcats are off to a rocky start to this year's basketball season suffering two losses in the final two outings of the 2024 portion of the year. They stand at 0-6 before entering contests…
content:
count
The Fleming Wildcats are off to a rocky start to this year's basketball season suffering two losses in the final two outings of the 2024 portion of the year. They stand at 0-6 before entering contests against the South Platte Blue Knights out of Big Springs, Neb., and the Otis Bulldogs this week.
Fleming played a close contest at Caliche on Friday, Dec. 20. They trailed by two after the first quarter and by seven at the half, but brought it back to a two-point contest in the third quarter. The Wildcat defense shut the Buffaloes down to just five points in the third while the offense upped the tally by 11 points to bring the score to 28-27, Caliche. Although the Wildcats kept pace with Caliche in the fourth, they fell short at the final horn and the score settled at 43-40.
Senior Travis Johnson earned a double-double for the night after bringing down 27 rebounds and scoring 11 points. Johnson's board tally hit double digits in both the offensive and defensive columns with 12 and 15, respectively. He also contributed team-high numbers in assists, steals and blocks with three in each category.
Sophomore Conner Marchant led on the scoreboard with 14 points. He scored 12 points on two-point field goals and two from the charity stripe.
Saturday, Dec. 21, brought Fleming back to their home court for a contest against Arickaree that would close the 2024 part of this year's basketball season. The Bison held the Wildcats in the single digits on the scoreboard for the first and second quarters, giving up just 11 to the home team in the first half. The Bison offense out up 30 on their side of the scoreboard.
Fleming topped Arickaree in the third quarter, 11-8, but let the Bison back in, 12-10, in the fourth quarter. The Wildcats fell 50-32 at the final horn.
Johnson led his team on the scoreboard with 10 points for the night. He also contributed six rebounds; all of those defensive.
Sophomore Treyson Kirkwood led the Wildcats in rebounds with seven total. He brought down three offensive and four defensive boards while also contributing nine points on offense.
Marchant followed on the scoreboard with eight points and brought down six defensive rebounds.
Heading into this weekend's home contests, Kirkwood leads the team in points per game with 7.7. The team as whole is averaging 34 points per outing.
Johnson currently leads the squad in rebounds, averaging 11.7 per game, over one-third of the team's total average of 32.6.
The Wildcats are set to go up against the South Platte Blue Knights from Oshkosh, Neb. on Friday. The Blue Knights enter at 4-5 overall averaging almost 50 points per game. Two quarters of boys' junior varsity is set to tip off at 4 p.m. followed by girls' varsity and boys' varsity.
On Saturday night, the Wildcats host the Otis Bulldogs. Otis stood at 2-2 overall at the beginning of the week. They currently average just over 50 points per game. A boys' JV contest is set for 1 p.m. followed by girls' and boys' varsity action.

title: Lady Cats add wins over Blue Knights and Bulldogs; advance to 7-1
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Fleming Lady Wildcats moved on to 7-1 with recent wins over the South Platte Lady Blue Knights out of Big Springs, Neb. and the Otis Lady Bulldogs. Fleming served as host for both events last…
content:
(Herald photo by Spring Atchison) count
LADY WILDCAT junior Siena Donnelson pulls down a rebound and looks to go up strong for a shot in Saturday's victory over Otis. Donnelson contributed 10 points and five rebounds for the night.
The Fleming Lady Wildcats moved on to 7-1 with recent wins over the South Platte Lady Blue Knights out of Big Springs, Neb. and the Otis Lady Bulldogs. Fleming served as host for both events last Friday and Saturday nights.
The Lady Wildcats came out with a narrow, four-point lead after the first quarter on Friday night against the Lady Blue Knights. The widened that scoring gap to nine points by the close of the half, 26-17. They took their most commanding lead of the contest throughout the third quarter, going up by 17 heading into the fourth. Despite being out scored by the visiting team by three points in the final quarter, Fleming maintained the lead and took a 49-35 win.
On Saturday night, the Lady Wildcats defeated Otis by a 29 point deficit. Fleming held the Lady Bulldogs to single digits in the opening two quarters and held a 40-9 lead at the half. Scoring looked more even in the second half and the Lady Wildcats walked away with at 65-39 victory.
Junior Brooke Schaefer led her team in scoring for both nights. She hit double digits on both outings with 22 against South Platte and 15 against Otis.
Sophomore Hadley Stull and junior Siena Donnelson followed Schaefer's offensive efforts on Friday night with nine and eight points, respectively.
On Saturday night, junior Ciana Lousberg and Donnelson contributed double digits on the scoreboard with 13 and 10, respectively.
Stull led in rebounds on Friday with nine. Senior Ashley Bornhoft added another eight.
On Saturday night, Donnelson and Bornhoft led under the net with six and five rebounds, respectively.
The Lady Wildcats are scheduled to play in three contests over the next week. They open with a league match up against the Prairie Lady Mustangs on Friday at Fleming. Saturday's action takes them on the road to Genoa-Hugo/Karval and they'll round out the week with a home contest against Akron. Junior varsity boys' contests will open on all three occasions. A 4 p.m. tip off scheduled for Friday, Jan. 17 and Tuesday, Jan. 21. Saturday's games at Genoa-Hugo are set to begin at 3 p.m.

title: SCF girls defeat Yuma in dual; take team title at Garden County
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Sedgwick County/Fleming girls wrestling team secured a decisive victory over the Yuma girls' squad in an intense match-up on Thursday evening. The final score was 42-29, with SCF outpacing the…
content:
count
The Sedgwick County/Fleming girls wrestling team secured a decisive victory over the Yuma girls' squad in an intense match-up on Thursday evening. The final score was 42-29, with SCF outpacing the home team with a series of dominant performances across the weight classes.
The evening kicked off with the 170-pound weight class, where Olivia Stone took on Sierra Brown of Yuma. Stone pinned Brown in just 1:36 to score the first points of the night for her team.
Yuma's Taelynn Robinson defeated Bella Allen in just 16 seconds by fall in the 105-pound division.
At 120 pounds, Kenya Arvizo of Yuma pinned Autumn Volkman in 2:47.
SCF received a few more forfeits, including at 130, 135 and 140 pounds. A final double forfeit at 145 pounds rounded out the competition, sealing Sedgwick County/Fleming's victory at 42 points to Yuma's 29.
The SCF girls' wrestling team delivered an impressive performance at the 2025 Garden County Invitational, bringing home the team title and showcasing the depth and skill of their athletes. The team was well represented across several weight classes, and their standout performances were pivotal in capturing the team championship. Results of wrestlers competing out of Fleming and Haxtun are as follows:
Though Bella Allen (0-3) did not place in the tournament, her performance was one to be noted. Competing at 105 pounds, Allen began with a tough loss to Mattaya Mills of Sutherland, falling in just 17 seconds, and was eventually eliminated after another fall to Lillyan Sheets of Sandhills Valley.
Autumn Volkman faced a tough road in the 120-pound bracket. After two losses by fall in the opening rounds, Volkman rallied to win by decision in her final match against Faith Lee of Leyton, securing a third place finish.
Annie Wilson (14-5) placed second in the 130-pound bracket with dominant performances in the early rounds. Wilson won by fall in both her quarterfinal and semifinal matchups, but in the final, she was outmatched by Jenifer Banister of Gordon-Rushville, who won by major decision.
The SCF girls' wrestling team proved to be a strong force at the Garden County Invitational, with numerous top finishes and an impressive overall performance. With the season in full swing, SCF continues to prepare for their next challenges as the team will travel to Elm Creek, Neb. on Friday, Jan. 17 and then Imperial, Neb. on Saturday, Jan. 18.

title: Producing with Pride
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: For several years now, I have been contributing content to various ag publications. I suppose it goes back to the Ag Teacher that remains deep within my psyche. I still have this aching desire to…
content:
For several years now, I have been contributing content to various ag publications. I suppose it goes back to the Ag Teacher that remains deep within my psyche. I still have this aching desire to promote, defend and preserve the ag industry and more specifically our beneficial use of water. Perhaps the time has come for me to let this cat out of the bag and share some of these insights with my own community, so from time to time, you may find my articles included in the pages of our local newspaper.
This initial piece is a reprint from the Winter 2024 issue of Coastal Grower. I hope you enjoy reading it as much as I enjoyed writing it.
In early November, several thousand irrigation professionals from around the world gathered to attend the Irrigation Association's annual Show and Education Week. As always, it was a great opportunity to attend classes and listen to presentations, while networking with industry specialists, friends and colleagues. Attendees gathered new information, learned of innovative ideas, got a pulse on the status of the industry and gained insights into the coming season.
Personally, I came away with an increased sense of optimism for the coming 2025 season and a greater desire to share our message. Afterall, if we Aggies don't tell our story, who will?
There is no doubt that producers throughout the United States, especially in the West, are facing pressure to reduce water usage and increase efficiency. In desert regions of California, like Imperial County, producers have already begun to voluntarily participate in programs designed to compensate growers for reducing irrigated production acres.
The goal is to decrease the impact on our stressed surface and groundwater supplies during the most critical times of the year. It is certainly not a perfect solution, but it is much better than fallowing land without any form of reparation to the grower, as we consistently hear of these impending reductions in irrigated acres.
Having been involved in the Ag water industry for over 40 years, I often find myself pondering this water scarcity dilemma. How do we continue to feed a hungry world? Can we maximize efficiency and production while simultaneously minimizing acreage? For example, with California producing approximately 90 percent of the U.S. supply of leafy greens in addition to over 400 other crops, cutting back on those acres without negatively affecting consumers could prove problematic.
Pondering this dilemma while standing in our kitchen on a rainy afternoon last spring, I had an epiphany of sorts. As I glanced from shelf to shelf, the critical role of water in the production of fruits, vegetables, nuts, bread and other staples that filled our pantry became overwhelmingly obvious.
My wife thought I had lost my mind as I began pulling items off our shelves and out of the refrigerator, placing them on the counter of our kitchen island. Once I explained what I was doing, she dug right in, helping me lay out a virtual cornucopia of delectables. Even on that random day, there were more goods than we could fit on the countertop.
We primarily selected fresh items produced from the crops that we serviced through our water treatment solutions at Ag Water Chemical. As we placed each item on the counter, it was fun to visualize the bounty. It was even more remarkable to realize that this harvest, much of which had been produced by that liquid gold known as West Coast Water, was now covering our Colorado kitchen counter.
Glancing back outside, watching the rainwater puddle and thinking "Spring showers brings May flowers" I knew that these cloud bursts did so much more. They fill our soil profiles, streams, rivers and reservoirs, even underground aquifers. Since these rains in the West are often few and far between, it reminds us of the significance that sensible water usage has on all of us and how important it is that we continue to spread that message.
Perhaps part of the overall water sustainability solution will be addressed by new technologies, as increased production costs, along with labor and water scarcity, force producers to take a much deeper dive into automation. From automated planting, weeding and spraying options, to cloud-capable flow meters and real-time soil moisture monitors, production becomes more efficient, and data driven.
No longer must we speculate about yield variations across a particular field or farm, as real-time yield monitoring tells us exactly where our best and worst production acres are, so that we can target planting, fertilizer and soil amendment rates based on specific field variables. Some systems can even irrigate with variable rate flow control, a process that will certainly become more common and affordable in time.
So, where do we go from here? We must continue to develop ways to share our important story, giving consumers a deeper understanding of the soil, water and crop production cycles that impact us all. Agricultural entities have got to take a seat at the water policy table or as some have suggested, we will end up on the menu.
Ultimately, the influence that water has on our food security is paramount. It is imperative that we Aggies continue to develop innovative ways to become better at what we do through conservation, innovation and cooperation ... sharing our important story everywhere we go.

title: Wrestlers defeat Yuma; take second place at Garden Co. Invite
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Sedgwick County/Fleming wrestling team delivered a dominant performance on the mat, defeating Yuma in a dual last week with a final score of 48-27. With multiple victories by pin and decision, SCF showcased their strength across various weight classes, securing key wins and extending their momentum throughout the evening. The real highlight of the match came from SCF's wrestlers who...
content:
The Sedgwick County/Fleming wrestling team delivered a dominant performance on the mat, defeating Yuma in a dual last week with a final score of 48-27. With multiple victories by pin and decision, SCF showcased their strength across various weight classes, securing key wins and extending their momentum throughout the evening.
The real highlight of the match came from SCF's wrestlers who dominated with falls. At 132 pounds, Maddox Herskind wasted no time, pinning Thomas Deal in 3:20 to add six points for the team. Austin Knox, competing at 144 pounds, continued the pinning spree, securing a fall in 1:24 over Dallas Brunk.
As the event progressed, Scotty Engle competing at 150 pounds, in addition to a pair of wrestlers competing out of Julesburg, all received forfeits, adding six points each to SCF's total score, pushing their lead to 48-6.
Yuma, while competitive, was unable to match SCF, securing points only through individual victories. At 165 pounds, Daden Beauprez pinned Zach Statz in 54 seconds, and at 175 pounds James Brandner won by pin over Bryden Woodside in 3:08.
The SCF wrestling team secured an impressive 48-27 victory over Yuma, thanks to their powerful performances in multiple weight classes. The team not only dominated in terms of victories but also capitalized on forfeits and pins to maintain control of the dual from start to finish.
This victory adds another win to SCF's growing season and strengthens their position as a formidable team in the region. With multiple wrestlers stepping up in key moments, SCF looks poised for even greater success as the season continues. The SCF wrestling team showed exceptional depth and determination at the Garden County Invitational last weekend, securing an impressive second-place finish overall. Individual results from wrestlers competing out of Fleming and Haxtun are as follows:
Scotty Engle had a strong tournament but came up just short in the 144-pound finals, finishing in second place. He advanced through the bracket with a 33-second pin over Pierce Phelps of Sandhills Valley and a 1:17 fall over James Jeffords of Bridgeport. In the final, Engle faced Kyler Vincent of Gordon-Rushville, who defeated him in a hard-fought 11-7 decision.
Austin Knox had a tough road in the 138-pound bracket but finished strong with a fourth-place finish. He began his tournament with a 27-second pin over Ethan Nadow of Yuma but was pinned in the quarterfinals by Drake Arensdorf of South Platte. Knox battled back with several dominant wins, including a pin and a tech fall, before falling in the third-place match to Arensdorf again, this time by pin in 49 seconds.
Carter Imhof struggled in his matches but had a notable victory in the consolation bracket. After losing by fall in his opening match, Imhof earned a technical fall win over Noah Hiatt of South Loup in 2:17. However, he was defeated in the consolation semifinals by Kyler Mills of Bridgeport, who won by a 13-7 decision.
Bryden Woodside had a difficult tournament at 175 pounds, finishing with a 1-3 record. Woodside's tournament started with a quick pin by David Bryner of Wauneta-Palisade, but he bounced back with a dominant pin over Laramie Duffield of Hyannis. Unfortunately, he was eliminated by Josh Miller of Hemingford in the second consolation round.
Grant Firme wrestled in the 126-pound division and finished with a 2-2 record. Firme started strong with a fall in 1:55 over Micah Woodbeck of Hemingford. However, he was pinned by Tagen Yrkoski of Dundy County Stratton in the quarterfinals. Firme then bounced back to win by fall over his teammate Gabriel Becerra but was ultimately eliminated by David Gaytan of Yuma in the consolation rounds.
Maddox Herskind faced an uphill battle at 132 pounds, finishing with a 2-2 record. He was pinned in his first match by Wyatt Kyle of Overton but bounced back with a major decision win (11-0) over Jaycek Belknap of Bayard. He also advanced by medical forfeit in the consolation rounds before being pinned by Asa Funk of Gordon-Rushville, ending his tournament.
Zach Statz competed in the 165-pound division, finishing with a 1-3 record. Statz began his tournament with a solid 8-5 decision victory over Jared Perkins of Bayard. He faced Daden Beauprez from Yuma in the quarterfinals, where he was pinned in 3:07. In the consolation rounds, Statz bounced back with a pin over Jess Fanning of Dundy County-Stratton in 1:49. Unfortunately, his tournament came to an end in the third consolation round, where he was pinned by Kameran McCrumb of Wauneta-Palisade in 1:41.
Gabriel Becerra had a tough tournament at 126 pounds, but showed determination. He started in the championship bracket where he faced Luke Wetherington from Bayard and was pinned in 2:51. In the consolation round, Becerra bounced back with a win by fall over Logan Dalimata of Bridgeport, securing the victory in 2:20. However, his tournament ended in the next round, where he faced his teammate, Grant Firme. In a tough matchup, Firme pinned Becerra in 3:32, ending his hopes of advancing further.
Despite some tough individual matches and setbacks, the Sedgwick County/Fleming team finished in second place overall at the Garden County Invite. Their second place finish with 163.0 total team points reflects the strength of the team as a whole, with contributions from wrestlers in almost every weight class. The team's strong finish at the Garden County Invitational provides them with a solid foundation heading into the second half of the season. The team will be traveling to Elm Creek, Neb. on Friday, Jan. 17 and then hit the road again on Saturday, Jan. 18 to participate in the Chase County Invite.

title: Merger of two CUs proposed
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Haxtun Community Federal Credit Union Board of Directors recently announced talks of a merger with the Sterling Federal Credit Union. The local board of directors recently released the following…
content:
The Haxtun Community Federal Credit Union Board of Directors recently announced talks of a merger with the Sterling Federal Credit Union. The local board of directors recently released the following statement:
"The Board of Directors for Sterling Federal Credit Union and Haxtun Community Federal Credit Union have entered discussions for a proposed merger of the two credit unions. The Directors of the credit unions deem a merger could be advantageous to the members of both credit unions, thereby providing synergies and products that will benefit both memberships and all the communities they serve."
Haxtun Community Federal Credit Union Chief Executive Officer Kristin Hadeen said a merger would mean added services, additional advanced products and up-to-date solutions for members. A merge adds the possibility of real estate and ag lending as well as for more competitive interest rates.
"Sterling is a larger institution with a small, local feel," said Hadeen. "It's a great rural, community fit."
At this time, the merge is in a discussion phase and Hadeen is working closely with Sterling's CEO Darrin Blankenbeckler. Additional information will be released as it comes.
For more information or questions contact Hadeen at (970) 774-7396.

title: Lady Wildcats go 2-1 over past week
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald

content:
The Fleming Lady Wildcats opened last week's play with a loss to Akron, but followed it up with wins over Peetz and Genoa Hugo.
The contest with Akron ended at 42-33 with junior Brooke Schaefer leading on the scoreboard. She tacked on double digits with 13 points; six of those off three-point shots. Sophomore Hayley Chamberlain also put up double digits with 11 points. She went five for six from the free-throw line.
Freshman Hadley Stull led under the basket with nine rebounds. Junior Ciana Lousberg followed with six. Juniors Siena Donnelson and Ashley Bornhoft pulled down five apiece.
On Friday the team traveled to Peetz where they earned a league victory, 70-22, over the Lady Bulldogs.
The Lady Wildcats gave up just single digits on the scoreboard for three of four of the game's quarters. The Lady Bulldogs' highest scoring quarter came in the third when they added 11.
Schaefer again led her team in scoring with 15 points. She went six for nine attempts from the field including one three-point shot and 100 percent from the charity stripe for two points. Lousberg also hit double digits with 12 points. She also shot 100 percent from the free-throw line.
Sophomore Emma Feather led under the hoop with eight rebounds. She brought down four on offense and four on defense. Chamberlain followed with seven boards. Lousberg, sophomore Hadley Stull and freshman Madi Johnson each tallied six rebounds.
On Tuesday, the team traveled to Genoa Hugo for a makeup contest. Scoring on MaxPreps reported a close game that finished with Fleming on top by two, 49-47. Scores by quarter and individual stats were not reported as of press time.
The Lady Wildcats now sit at 10-2 on the season. They have taken the top spot in the league from the Briggsdale Lady Falcons with a 2-0 record. Briggsdale currently sits at 1-0 in league play.
The Lady Wildcats return to their home court for a three-game stretch this week. Action tips off on Thursday, Jan. 30 at 4 p.m. when the Stratton Eagles come to town. On Saturday, Feb. 1, the Wildcats are set to host Union Colony Prep beginning at 1 p.m. The week wraps up with Merino next Tuesday, Feb. 4 starting at 4 p.m.

title: Lady Bulldog edge out 1-point win on the road in Akron last week
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Thursday night was huge for the Lady Bulldogs as the team pulled out a final second, one-point win over Akron at the home of the Lady Rams. According to girls' basketball rankings from Colorado High School Activities Association posted on Feb. 10, Haxtun sits 20 out of 58 teams in the 2A Classification. The two league teams met for a non-league contest just six games into the season as part...
content:
Thursday night was huge for the Lady Bulldogs as the team pulled out a final second, one-point win over Akron at the home of the Lady Rams. According to girls' basketball rankings from Colorado High School Activities Association posted on Feb. 10, Haxtun sits 20 out of 58 teams in the 2A Classification.
The two league teams met for a non-league contest just six games into the season as part of the annual Holiday Tournament in mid-December. That match up narrowly went to the Rams by an 11-point spread.
This time the Lady Bulldogs came out to show out and kept fans on the edges of their seats. As the clock ticked away, the home team Rams pulled away with a one-point advantage but the Lady Bulldogs weren't done fighting. Stellar rebounding from senior Jayleigh Bullard put her in prime position to put a last second shot back up in the hoop just before the final buzzer to give Haxtun the victory when it counted. The Lady Bulldogs came out on top, 36-35.
"I can honestly say our girls had a lot of grit that night. We had girls diving on the ground for loose balls, we boxed out harder than we have all year and we had a lot of smart passes inside. We were also able to hold their best player to 11 points. That's half of what she had against us at the Holiday tournament," said Alicia Schram, Lady Bulldog Head Basketball Coach.
Seniors Bobbi Starkebaum and Emily Anderson each registered eight points in Akron on Thursday. Seniors Jayleigh Bullard and Kelsie Hadeen each contributed seven points. Freshman Leah Edwards totaled four points and sophomore Emma Lemesany added two.
Edwards led under the basket with eight rebounds. She brought down four on offense and six on defense. Bullard and Starkebaum each pulled down six rebounds, Anderson brought down four and Hadeen and Lemesany both tallied two.
Bullard led in assists with three on Thursday and Anderson grabbed six steals, the team high.
As a team, Haxtun shot 60 percent from the free throw line. Anderson and Lemesany both went 100 percent from the charity stripe. Bullard and Hadeen both shot 50 percent.
The following night, the Lady Bulldogs traveled to Brush to take on the higher classified Brush Beetdiggers. Haxtun was down 21 at half time, but again, the Lady Bulldogs showed some fight, battling throughout the third and bringing the game within five in the fourth. Ultimately Haxtun just ran out of time, falling 56-47.
"I am so proud of the way the girls played this past week. We had an amazing comeback in Brush and the girls just keep gaining. A lot of things are coming together," said Schram.
Bullard and Starkebaum led the Lady Bulldogs on the scoreboard with double-digits. Bullard racked up 16 and right behind was Starkebaum with 13. Edwards registered eight, Anderson added five and Hadeen scored three.
Starkebaum pulled down 13 rebounds, six on offense and seven on defense. Bullard brought down seven, Edwards tallied six and Hadeen and Lilly Lemesany each pulled down five.
Anderson added six assists to her list of stats while also leading in steals with five. Edwards shot 100 percent from the free-throw line, sinking two of two.
This week Haxtun is set to host Idalia on Friday and Caliche on Saturday.
"Idalia is quick and very handsy, so we will be working hard at controlling the ball and limiting the number of turnovers. We have some big-time opportunities coming up in the next couple of weeks. I feel like the girls have gone from the mindset of 'who do we have this week?' to 'who can we go out and challenge this week?' That's been amazing to see as a coach," Schram said. "We've seen a real shift in the mentality of the girls. They no longer look at the schedule and just see opponents. They see challenges and look forward to them."
After this weekend's match ups, one single game remains on the regular season schedule. The Bulldogs host Sedg. Co. on Feb. 21.
"We need to continue to put full games together. Top to bottom. We have a tendency to start off a little slow, so we need to step up the tempo early and put the gas pedal down," said Schram. "The coaching staff can give them all the fuel in the world when we prep for the game, but we can't ignite the fire. The girls have to do that part. We will continue to work hard as a team to accomplish our pre-season goal of making the postseason."

title: Dietary Fiber webinar: the unsung hero of health
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: Did you know most Americans don't eat enough fiber? Fiber plays an essential role in maintaining overall health, yet many fall short of the recommended daily intake. To help address this issue,…
content:
count
Jessica Clifford
Did you know most Americans don't eat enough fiber? Fiber plays an essential role in maintaining overall health, yet many fall short of the recommended daily intake. To help address this issue, Colorado State University's Department of Food Science and Human Nutrition, in partnership with CSU Extension, is hosting the next installment of the Everyday Nutrition for Health Webinar Series: Dietary Fiber: An Unsung Hero of Your Health.
This 30-minute pre-recorded webinar, led by Jessica Clifford, a Registered Dietitian and Extension Nutrition Specialist, will explore the different types of dietary fiber, health benefits and practical strategies to incorporate more fiber-rich foods in your diet.
The webinar will be available via Zoom on Tuesday, Feb. 25 at 12 p.m. While there will not be a live Q and A, participants can submit questions through a post-webinar survey. All submitted questions will be answered in a follow-up email. A recording of the webinar will be available in English and Spanish a couple of weeks after the event.
To guarantee access to the recording and follow-up materials, register at https://col.st/ykiop. Don't miss this opportunity to enhance your nutrition knowledge and discover how dietary fiber can benefit your health.

title: Weeds, wind towers topics of county commissioners' meeting
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: During the Jan. 31 meeting of the Phillips County Board of County Commissioners, local farmer Vern Rafert attended the Public Comment segment of the meeting to express concerns about noxious weeds.…
content:
count
During the Jan. 31 meeting of the Phillips County Board of County Commissioners, local farmer Vern Rafert attended the Public Comment segment of the meeting to express concerns about noxious weeds.
Rafert, who is a member of the County's Weed and Pest Board, identified a few specific locations and types of weeds spreading out of control on both private land and in ditches. He urged that more aggressive spraying be done in areas controlled by the county. He also thinks that some of the Conservation Reserve Program landowners are not doing enough to keep up with curtailing noxious weeds which can result in seeds being carried to adjacent properties.
The board agreed to pass along Rafert's concerns to the County's Weed and Pest manager, Kerri Doleshall.
Wind regulations, moratorium
The Board discussed the fact that an anticipated study in Colorado on wind energy and regulations had not yet begun because a Memorandum of Understanding between involved parties had not yet been signed. Commissioner Garold Roberts reported that he and County Planner Andrew Nygaard met with a representative of National Renewable Solutions on Jan. 30. He indicated that NRS might be submitting an application to permit 20 to 22 pad sites in the western part of the county sometime near the end of 2025.
The Board approved extending the current moratorium on the processing of permits related to the construction of any wind farm system or facility within Phillips County through Sept. 30.
For background, the original moratorium Resolution, 2024-06-18-02, was adopted last June to allow "sufficient time to review, study, hold public hearings and prepare and adopt amendments" if determined to be necessary. The Board wanted to explore ways to prevent the high density of hundreds of towers being established in Phillips County as is currently planned in Sedgwick County. High density was not the intent of the board when finalizing the wind regulations in the new Phillips County Land Use Code that was adopted June 30, 2023. Because more time was still needed when the moratorium was set to expire in September of 2024, the board extended the moratorium through Jan. 31. Because study results are still not available, the board thought it necessary to extend the moratorium again through September.
Public hearing
A public hearing was held to consider the subdivision exemption application from Prenzlow Enterprises Co. LLC to sell 6.36 acres of a 115-acre parcel to Eugene and Carol Kumm. The 6.36 acres are adjacent to the Kumm's property in the SW ¼ of Section 6, Township 6 North, Range 43 West. No comments from the public were offered. The Board approved the application.
Timed appointments
Aaron Sprague, representing the Republican River Water Conservation District, updated the commissioners on the progress made toward compliance with reducing irrigated acreage, funding and the overall status of water in the district. He also informed the board that he would be travelling soon for meetings in Washington D.C. in regard to the federal Farm Bill.
Assessor Doug Kamery and Deputy Assessor Toby Thompson discussed particulars about the Amherst Road and Bridge department property in Amherst, including pinpointing the location of the well. They also indicated options for vacating a strip of land along what would be the west edge of the property if it were to be sold. The map still indicates the strip to be the continuation of Main Street even though the street was never extended that far.
Miscellaneous projects
Roberts reported on the Weldco Farms well monitoring report and his meeting with General Manager Brian England. Nitrate levels still test within the State's acceptable range. The Board will continue to monitor the reports' nitrate levels.
The Holyoke Lions Club has committed $5,000 for a new shelter at the county fairgrounds. The Phillips County Recreation District Board will be approached to see if it would consider additional funding for it.
The Biesemeier gravel pit, located in the southwest region of the county, has about an acre of water in it that must be remediated no later than March 17. Roberts said, "It's not uncommon for the pits to have some standing water in them, but there's a difference between water run-off from rain and groundwater rising from below." In this case groundwater is suspected. The Road and Bridge department will investigate pumping it out and then adding and packing two more feet of material.
Bids have been received for the Pleasant Valley Road and Bridge storage building, well and septic work.
Business decisions
The Board visited with Landfill Manager Bill Andrews by phone to discuss the roll-off truck. It experienced a major problem with the motor and oil line. After considering the pros and cons of repairing the motor versus replacing the truck, Andrews will seek bids for a new motor. Rentals of roll-off dumpsters will not be available until further notice.
The Board switched out Commissioner Tom Timm with Lori Lundgren, Director of Phillips County Human Services, to serve as the proxy on the Colorado Counties, Inc. Health and Human Services Steering Committee during the 2025 session.
The board also:
• Signed a Letter of Support for the NJC Colorado Opportunity Scholarship Initiative;
• Appointed Jean Clayton to complete the unexpired term of Elton Olofson on the Phillips County Recreation District Board; and
• Appointed Alan Nall to complete the unexpired term of Lea White on the Phillips County Economic Development Corporation board of directors.
The commissioners' board meetings are open to the public. The meeting schedule is posted at the Phillips County homepage, https://phillipscounty.colorado.gov/ and on the bulletin board near the west entrance of the courthouse. The schedule can also be requested in the administration office or calling the office at (970) 854-3778.

title: Lady Wildcats defeat Arickaree; move into next round on Friday at 5 p.m.
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Fleming Lady Wildcats have advanced to the final round of the NCL/YWKC Season Finale Tournament set for Friday, Feb. 28. Last week the Lady Wildcats closed regular season play with a loss to the…
content:
(Herald photo by Spring Atchison) count
FLEMING LADY Wildcat Tijana Milojevic brings the ball up court in the final seconds of play against Denver Waldorf.
The Fleming Lady Wildcats have advanced to the final round of the NCL/YWKC Season Finale Tournament set for Friday, Feb. 28. Last week the Lady Wildcats closed regular season play with a loss to the Idalia Lady Wolves and earned a victory over Arickaree in the opening round of tournament action.
On Friday, Feb. 21, the Lady Wildcats traveled to Idalia where they faced off with the top team in 1A's YWKC league. Fleming kept pace to open the contest and trailed by just one point after the first quarter. Idalia out scored Fleming by six in the second to own a seven-point advantage at halftime.
The local ladies were out scored by two in the third quarter which put them down by nine overall. Idalia closed with a 17-point fourth quarter and gave up just 12 to Fleming for the 43-29 victory on their home court.
Tournament play opened on Monday, Feb. 24 for the Lady Wildcats who entered as the top team in the North Central League. They took on YWKC's fourth ranked Arickaree Lady Bison.
Fleming jumped to an early lead putting up 13 in the first quarter while giving up just two points. The Lady Bison closed in on one point of that advantage in the second, out scoring the Lady Wildcats 12-11. Fleming held the upper hand at the half, 24-14.
The Lady Wildcats added 10 points to their advantage in the third, 15-5, putting them out in front 34-19. Arikaree put forth their best effort in the fourth trying for the come back, but fell short after adding 11 points and giving up 10. The final tally read 49-30, Fleming.
Monday's win over the Lady Bison allows Fleming to advance to the next round of tournament play on Friday. In that contest they are set to take on the Hi-Plains Lady Patriots, the number two team out of YWKC. That contest is set for Friday, Feb. 28 at 5 p.m. at Northeastern Junior College in Sterling.

title: McCracken to retire, but remain superintendent
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: School closures, next year's calendar and the superintendent's contract took top priority at the February meeting of the Frenchman Board of Education. The local school board gathered in the Fleming…
content:
count
School closures, next year's calendar and the superintendent's contract took top priority at the February meeting of the Frenchman Board of Education. The local school board gathered in the Fleming School/Community Library for a meeting that lasted just about an hour.
School board members voted to approve the 2025-26 school calendar as well as a superintendent contract through 2027. Those two items were at the top of action items that also consisted of a number of second and final readings of administrative regulations.
Next year's calendar is similar to the current year and includes a two-week break for Christmas and a one-week spring break.
"The high school students will attend school for 150 days and the elementary students will attend for 148 days," Superintendent Steve McCracken said.
In his report earlier in the meeting, McCracken noted that the District's four-day application for the coming year was submitted to the Colorado Department of Education. This application is submitted annually to continue to operate on a four-day school week.
McCracken's Superintendent contract was approved after the calendar. His contract is to run from 2025 through 2027. The Superintendent contract runs from July 1 to June 30.
"I plan to retire in June of this year, however, I will continue to work under the PERA rules and regulations for an employee who is working while retired," McCracken added.
At the start of the February meeting, board members read through correspondence from CDE. The letter was to inform the District that 2023-24 audit and financial data was submitted.
"The School Finance unit commends our District and there are no concerns," said McCracken.
At the start of the meeting, administration gave reports to board members, starting with Principal Kortney Firme. Firme said she is prepping for the upcoming school year in preparing class schedules, paraprofessional assignments and class locations.
McCracken, in his report, noted that the District is currently working on an ineligible policy for online and home school students in order to participate in school activities.
In approving the consent agenda, the Board ratified the decision to cancel school on Jan. 28, 29 and Feb. 11, a two-hour delay on Feb. 12 and remote learning days on Feb. 18 and 19.
"We typically schedule about three and a half snow days in our District calendar," McCracken said. "We have already used those days, so we have our students log in remotely to our system using their school issued Chromebooks and our teachers can instruct students using the Google classroom program or zoom meetings."
To wrap things up, board members approved final readings of five administrative regulations. The first reading of each took place in January.
"The administrative regulations were revised and amended to update then in accordance to what our current practices are," said McCracken.

title: Haxtun Board of Education approves coaches for spring sports
author: The Haxtun-Fleming Herald
description: The Haxtun Board of Education met for a short, monthly February meeting on Wednesday, Feb. 19. Board members met in the School Library to act on a short list of regular business items including hiring…
content:
count
The Haxtun Board of Education met for a short, monthly February meeting on Wednesday, Feb. 19. Board members met in the School Library to act on a short list of regular business items including hiring spring coaches and to approve third and final readings for policies regarding relations with charter schools and federally mandated family and medical leave.
At the start of the meeting last month, board members addressed concerns stemming from the way parents approach and treat athletic coaches. After some discussion, it was noted that in the future Superintendent Aron Jones and the District Athletic Director plan to attend parent meetings to address athletics. Crowd behavior at games was also discussed and is to be examined by administration.
Following the meeting, a letter was sent to all parents of junior high and high school students asking for cooperation in creating a positive and encouraging environment at all sporting events.
In approving the consent agenda, board members approved closure of school on Feb. 18-19 due to cold temperatures and blizzard-like conditions.
Later in action items, the Board approved the following list of coaches for spring sports: high school baseball head coach, Trent Ham; high school baseball assistant coach, Ryan Nolin; high school baseball assistant coach, Rob Martinez; high school track head coach, Jared Anderson; junior high track head coach, Noah Toops; and junior high track assistant coach, Heather Kurtzer.
The Board of Education also approved a final resolution pertaining to armed school personnel, which is currently in the initial stages of implementation at the District and third and final policy readings for the following: Policy LBD Relations with District Charter Schools; Policy LBD-R Relations with District Charter Schools; Policy GBGF Federally-Mandated Family and Medical Leave; and Policy GBGF-R Federally-Mandated Family and Medical Leave.
The RE-2J policy book can be found on the District website at haxtunk12.org under the Board of Education tab.

title: Class of 7 graduates FHS
author: Spring Atchison Office Manager
description: A class of seven students undoubtedly becomes like an extended family. And a class of seven students gets to know one another in a way only a family would. Commencement ceremonies at Fleming High…
content:
FLEMING GRADUATE Will Bornhoft takes time out of Sunday's commencement ceremonies to thank and honor his mother Carla Bornhoft during the parent appreciation portion of the day's events.
A class of seven students undoubtedly becomes like an extended family. And a class of seven students gets to know one another in a way only a family would. Commencement ceremonies at Fleming High School were a true testament to those statements as each speaker at the podium choked back tears during heartfelt farewells to the class of 2024.
Senior Class President David Betley opened the occasion with accolades to the mothers in the audience in observance of Mother's Day before turning the microphone over to Harry Harms for the invocation.
Guidance Counselor Randy Stahley took the podium to announce scholarship and award winners from this year's graduating class. He opened asking the crowd to ponder how the success of a school should be evaluated and offered possible answers that might come to mind. He said in his belief, the success of a school comes down to graduating seniors who are good people and good citizens who are prepared. "I am confident that these young people will go on and be very successful," Stahley said.
One by one, Stahley called each graduate forward, telling of their plans for the future, scholarships and awards received. He noted that collectively, the class has already completed several years at Northeastern Junior College through concurrent enrollment.
The class slideshow was presented followed by the traditional recognition of parents and family.
Principal Kortney Firme introduced this Salutatorian MadiKay Serrato and Valedictorian David Betley.
Both Serrato and Betley spent their time at the microphone speaking of character traits and values of each member of the class.
Serrato opened by telling of her goals. "But how much money I make or how big my house is will not matter to me quite as much as the kind of person I became along the way."
She spoke of the great role models she's had in her life, but added that she didn't realize for the longest time was that she had six great role models seated right behind her. She spoke of confidence, determination, authenticity, hard work, kindness and loyalty shown by her classmates that she will strive to live up to.
(Herald photo by Spring Atchison)
FLEMING HIGH School's 2024 Valedictorian David Betley flashes a smile and gets a fist bump from Marv "Coach" Conyers as he exits the gym following Sunday's commencement ceremony.
Betley opened by saying the perception of Gen Z as lazy and without work ethic has been disproved by his class who has lived through one of the greatest health crisis of this century, competed in athletics at the highest level, taken hundreds of hours of coursework and earned hundreds of thousands of dollars in scholarships.
"These six things I believe define our class, passion, determination, reaching out of our comfort zone, laughing, pushing ourselves to the limit and valuing people," Betley said. "As the valedictorian of the class of 2024, I promise that you guys haven't seen anything yet."
Firme returned to the podium for conferring of diplomas and left the graduates with these words, "As you embark on this next chapter of your lives I urge you to remember the values that have guided this far - your integrity, compassion and perseverance. Hold fast to your dreams and never be afraid to pursue them with all of your heart."
After turning their tassels and tossing their caps, the seven graduates exited the gym to "I Lived" by One Republic.

title: Trooper Tips
author: Patrick Rice Sergeant
description: As we move towards the spring weather, still being hounded with snow … It's that time of year when Coloradoans are reminded that we live in an extraordinary state, with extraordinary weather and the…
content:
April showers brings May snow
Series: Colorado State Patrol | Story 1 Share Tweet 0 Comments May 16, 2024
As we move towards the spring weather, still being hounded with snow … It's that time of year when Coloradoans are reminded that we live in an extraordinary state, with extraordinary weather and the need for proper equipment and precautions never goes away. We all have budgets and wish to be fiscally responsible. I see long lines at the tire shops nearing the end of April and moving into May as people are quick to remove those snow tires and save the tread for next season. While I like this idea and support the decision to use quality tires over multiple snow seasons, let's not be too quick to make that swap. The snow in high elevations continues late into what we consider the springtime and the need for those snow tires is just as crucial for these spring storms as it is on New Year's Eve. I know if you're leaving Denver or Grand Junction and headed to the mountains for the weekend when you get in your car, it will be sunny and 80 outside, but dress appropriately. Be sure your windshield wiper fluid is topped off, and those tires are ready for the conditions you will likely find yourself in as you ascend I-70 to your destination.
The number of cars on the road and the number of troopers clearly don't match. In the middle of the winter, the number of drivers we need to help tends to be lower as people travel prepared. In the spring, not only do we see unprepared vehicles but also drivers and passengers who are not prepared to be stuck. They are not wearing warm clothing and may not have food or drinks in their car. It does not take long to become cold, not just in the sense of comfort but to the point of risking injury and the need for medical attention. You cannot count on your vehicle to keep you warm while you wait for help.
While you didn't plan for it, your windows might be broken out, your engine might be dead, you ran out of gas or your vehicle may be in a perilous location where sitting in it is even more dangerous than getting out. I would implore everyone in Colorado to designate space in their vehicles for a few items to stay year-round. Find a corner of the trunk for a blanket, some food and water and that windshield fluid you never knew you'd miss until it's gone. We are not beyond the dangers of winter driving yet. Think like a Coloradoan and plan ahead.

title: Bamford signs to play softball with NW Kansas Technical College
author: Candie Fix Managing Editor
description: A successful four-year high school softball career has afforded Fallon Bamford the opportunity to compete at the collegiate level next fall. Bamford, recent Haxtun High School graduate, signed a…
content:
(Herald photo by Candie Fix)
FALLON BAMFORD, recent Haxtun High School graduate, signed a letter of intent to play softball next fall. Pictured with her are front row (l-r), Holyoke High School Softball Coach Kendra Schlachter, mom Amy Bamford, Fallon and Haxtun High School Athletic Director Don Myers; back row (l-), brother Jace Bamford and dad Chad Bamford.
A successful four-year high school softball career has afforded Fallon Bamford the opportunity to compete at the collegiate level next fall. Bamford, recent Haxtun High School graduate, signed a letter of intent to join the softball team at Northwest Kansas Technical College in front of family, coaches and supporters two week ago.
Fallon was a part of the Holyoke High School softball team throughout high school, playing outfield for the Lady Dragons. As a senior, she helped lead her team to the 2023 3A State Softball Tournament. The Lady Dragons finished with an overall 12-12 record.
"Fallon's speed and overall athleticism on the field are what instantly caught my eye when recruiting," said Bailey Honne, Head Softball Coach at Northwest Kansas Technical College. "She brings enthusiasm for the sport that our team is going to need next season. As a vocal teammate she will help lead the infield via her communication skills."
In her senior season, Fallon earned a .478 batting average and a .562 on base percentage. She registered 32 hits, 22 runs-batted-in and tallied 29 runs. She also boasts a .950 fielding percentage. Fallon was a captain for the Lady Dragons last season.
Throughout her four years on the field, Fallon registered 52 hits, 41 RBIs and 51 runs with a four-year fielding average of .902. Her high school batting average comes in at .325.
While playing softball at Northwest Kansas Technical College, Fallon plans to study precision ag.
She is the daughter of Chad and Amy Bamford, Haxtun, and the granddaughter of Kent and Naida, Haxtun, Ruby McLamb, Hudson, and Mike Bradley, Haxtun.
"I see Fallon working hard to earn a spot in the middle infield next season for us," Honne said. "Fallon's work ethic, in game knowledge and her enthusiasm will help our program compete at a higher level in our conference next season."

title: Haxtun student wins mural design competition for Rural Action Project
author: From PCED
description: Olivia Stone, a bright and talented student from Haxtun, has achieved a remarkable milestone by winning the mural design competition for the Colorado State University Rural Action Project. Her…
content:
(Courtesy photo)
OLIVIA STONE pictured with her wining design.
Olivia Stone, a bright and talented student from Haxtun, has achieved a remarkable milestone by winning the mural design competition for the Colorado State University Rural Action Project. Her artistic vision and creativity have earned her this prestigious recognition.
The competition, aimed at showcasing the artistic talents within rural communities, saw numerous impressive entries. However, Stone's design stood out for its originality and the vibrant representation of the local culture. The Haxtun Town Council, responsible for selecting the winning design, unanimously chose Olivia's work as the standout submission.
"We were incredibly impressed by the quality and thoughtfulness of Olivia's design," said Mikey Brown, Phillips County Economic Development. "Her artwork truly captures the essence of our community and the spirit of the CSU Rural Action Project."
Olivia's mural will soon be brought to life and displayed prominently on a building in Haxtun, adding a splash of color and a touch of inspiration to the town. The mural is expected to become a local landmark, celebrating the creativity and talent that exists within the community.
The unveiling of the mural will be announced in the coming weeks and residents are encouraged to attend the event to show their support for Olivia and enjoy the new artistic addition to their town.
This achievement not only highlights Stone's artistic abilities but also underscores the importance of encouraging and recognizing young talent in rural areas. The CSU Rural Action Project continues to support such initiatives, fostering a sense of community and pride among residents. title: HPD re-registers offender
author: Candie Fix Managing Editor
description: The Haxtun Police Department re-registered a sex offender living within Haxtun's city limits. Steven Michael Saign lives in the 200 block of North Wallace Avenue. According to the local police…
content:
The Haxtun Police Department re-registered a sex offender living within Haxtun's city limits. Steven Michael Saign lives in the 200 block of North Wallace Avenue.
According to the local police department, Saign is a dual resident, meaning he is registered at two locations; one on North Wallace Avenue and a another on County Road 7 in Phillips County. This is his required quarterly registration.
Saign was convicted of sex assault on a child and sex assault on a child, age 15-18, by someone in a position of trust on Nov. 29, 2012 in El Paso County. As part of his sentencing, he is required to register annually as well as quarterly with law enforcement.

title: Goddard closes HS career with honors
author: Candie Fix Managing Editor
description: Haxtun's Cassidy Goddard received All-Conference honors in her final high school track season. The recent Haxtun High School graduate has committed to the Black Hills State track and field team to…
content:
Share Tweet 0 Comments May 30, 2024
Cassidy Goddard
Haxtun's Cassidy Goddard received All-Conference honors in her final high school track season. The recent Haxtun High School graduate has committed to the Black Hills State track and field team to continue her throwing career at the collegiate level next fall.
Goddard received All-Conference honors with her first place finish in discus at the LPAA-YWKC-NC League Meet in Julesburg on May 4. Goddard took first with a throw of 134 feet, 4.5 inches.
She currently holds the Haxtun High School girls discus record set at 135 feet, four inches. Goddard set that record in Holyoke on May 1.
At the 1A Colorado State Track meet last week, Goddard finished third in discus and fifth in shot put.
Track athletes earn All-Conference designations with a first place finish at their respective league meets.

content: A MEMORIAL DAY ceremony held Monday, May 27 at Haxtun Cemetery, featured local singers Janice Kilpatrick and Alyssa Hahn. The duo performed "America the Beautiful" for those who gathered in honor of military personnel who died while serving. Former State Senator Jerry Sonnenberg served as a guest speaker for the ceremony.
